candidates.name: Chain of Torah Tradition (Mesorah)
candidates.notes: The transmission of Torah from Sinai through generations: Moses to Joshua to elders to prophets to Men of Great Assembly, and onward. A central theme of Avot ch. 1.

candidates.name: Ten Utterances of Creation (Asarah Maamarot)
candidates.notes: The world was created with ten divine utterances; the theological significance of this for reward and punishment (Avot 5:1).

candidates.name: Restrictions on Esoteric Teaching
candidates.notes: Rabbinic restrictions governing who may be taught and how the most esoteric subjects — Maaseh Bereishit, Maaseh Merkavah, and related speculative topics — may be transmitted.

candidates.name: Restriction on Teaching Maaseh Bereishit (Cosmogony)
candidates.notes: The restriction against expounding the account of Creation before two or more individuals; paired with the restriction on Maaseh Merkavah.

candidates.name: Restriction on Teaching Maaseh Merkavah (Divine Chariot)
candidates.notes: The prohibition of teaching the Design of the Divine Chariot even one-on-one, unless the student is wise and understands on his own; source for esoteric teaching restrictions.

candidates.name: Four Forbidden Speculative Topics (Above, Below, Before, After)
candidates.notes: The four matters one should not speculate about: what is above the firmament, what is below the earth, what was before creation, what will be after the world ends.

candidates.name: Prohibition to Use Maaseh Merkavah as Haftarah
candidates.notes: Prohibition to conclude public Torah reading with the section of the Divine Chariot (Ezekiel 1); Rabbi Yehuda permits it.

candidates.name: Heretical Prayer Formulations (Minim in Prayer)
candidates.notes: Prayers that indicate heretical belief — 'may the good bless You,' double 'we give thanks,' extending mercy of shiluach haken to all — are silenced.

candidates.name: Ways of the Amorite (Darkei haEmori)
candidates.notes: Prohibition of superstitious practices associated with gentile customs, such as using a fox's tooth or a crucifixion nail as a remedy.

candidates.name: Folk Remedies and Superstitious Cures
candidates.notes: Items used as folk remedies such as locust eggs, fox teeth, and nails from the crucified — Rabbi Meir permits, Rabbis prohibit as darkei haEmori.

candidates.name: Ma'alim b'Kodesh (Elevating in Matters of Sanctity)
candidates.notes: The principle that one elevates to a higher level in matters of sanctity and does not downgrade; illustrated by the shewbread placed on gold upon removal from the Sanctuary.

candidates.name: Shamir Worm
candidates.notes: The legendary shamir worm used to cut the Temple stones without iron; said to have ceased after the Second Temple's destruction.

candidates.name: Disputes with Minim (Heretics)
candidates.notes: Recorded debates between rabbis and minim (heretics/sectarians) on halakhic and theological matters.

candidates.name: Laws of Bikkurim (First Fruits)
candidates.notes: Detailed halakhic sub-topics within the laws of bikkurim, including eligibility, ceremony, priestly rights, and responsibility

candidates.name: Laws of Challah (Dough Tithe)
candidates.notes: Detailed halakhic sub-topics within the laws of challah, including measures, eligibility, territorial distinctions, and purity

candidates.name: Sdeh Achuzah — Ancestral Field Consecration Laws
candidates.notes: Detailed laws: redemption at 50 shekels per beit kor; counting years to Jubilee; crevices and boulders; who may redeem; one-fifth addition for owner; what happens if not redeemed by Jubilee; Levite cities fields

candidates.name: Batei Arei Chomah — Houses in Walled Cities
candidates.notes: Detailed laws: 12-month redemption window; becomes permanent after one year; Hillel's enactment of chamber for deposit; definition of walled city (from Joshua's era); houses vs. fields within walls; Levite city houses

candidates.name: Redemption of Ancestral Field During Jubilee Period
candidates.notes: Cannot consecrate less than 2 years before Jubilee; cannot redeem less than 1 year after Jubilee; counting months for Temple treasury; what happens if not redeemed; priests entering the field; Rabbi Eliezer's view of abandoned field

candidates.name: Sale of Field with Jubilee Provisions
candidates.notes: Cannot redeem within first two years; blight/shemitah years don't count; resale price calculation; prohibition on selling distant field to redeem nearby; incremental redemption; comparison to Temple treasury redemption

candidates.name: Hillel's Enactment for Walled City House Redemption
candidates.notes: Buyer's concealment to prevent redemption; Hillel's enactment that seller deposits money in court chamber and breaks down the door; procedural reform

candidates.name: Fields That Do Not Return in the Jubilee Year
candidates.notes: Properties that do not revert to original owners in the Jubilee Year: the firstborn's extra inheritance portion, a husband inheriting wife's property, a yavam inheriting his brother's property, and the dispute between Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis regarding gifts

candidates.name: Person Suspected of Sabbatical Year Violations
candidates.notes: Restrictions on purchasing flax and other products from one suspected of Sabbatical Year violations; graduated trust depending on degree of processing

candidates.name: Person Suspected of Terumah Violations
candidates.notes: Restrictions on purchasing food items from one suspected of selling terumah as non-sacred produce; dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon on scope of suspicion

candidates.name: Bikkurim Declaration (Viduy Bikkurim)
candidates.notes: The recitation of Deuteronomy 26:3-10 accompanying the bringing of first fruits; who recites and who does not (convert, guardian, slave, woman, tumtum, androginus)

candidates.name: Eligibility to Bring Bikkurim
candidates.notes: Who brings and recites, who brings but does not recite, and who does not bring at all — including sharecroppers, robbers, converts, women, slaves, guardians

candidates.name: Bikkurim from the Seven Species
candidates.notes: Requirement that bikkurim come specifically from the seven species; restrictions on produce from hills, valleys, or non-choice olives

candidates.name: Bikkurim Pilgrimage Procession
candidates.notes: The festive procession of bringing bikkurim to Jerusalem — the maamad assemblies, the ox with gilded horns, the flute, the greeting by Temple officials

candidates.name: Waving of Bikkurim (Tenufah)
candidates.notes: The ritual waving of the bikkurim basket by the owner and priest together at the Temple

candidates.name: Additions to Bikkurim (Tosfet Bikkurim)
candidates.notes: Laws of produce added to bikkurim baskets beyond the bikkurim themselves, and the ornamentation of bikkurim — their status and rules

candidates.name: Designation of Bikkurim (Hekdesh bikkurim)
candidates.notes: The act of marking first fruits while still attached to the soil; the dispute whether a second designation is required after plucking

candidates.name: Bikkurim as Priestly Property
candidates.notes: Status of bikkurim as priest's property — may be used to purchase slaves, land, or unclean animals; distribution to mishmar

candidates.name: Owner's Responsibility for Bikkurim Until Delivery
candidates.notes: The owner bears financial/halakhic responsibility for bikkurim from designation until arrival at the Temple Mount; replacement obligations if lost, stolen, or became impure

candidates.name: Bikkurim and the Onen
candidates.notes: An onen (mourner before burial) is forbidden from eating bikkurim; dispute of R. Shimon who permits

candidates.name: Biur Bikkurim (Removal of Bikkurim)
candidates.notes: Bikkurim are subject to the law of biur (removal); dispute whether this applies equally or is exempted per R. Shimon

candidates.name: Challah — Dough Tithe (Laws of Hallah)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of the challah obligation: minimum measure (five-fourths of a kav), who is obligated, when the obligation begins (rolling/formation of crust), and how it is separated

candidates.name: Minimum Measure for Challah (Shiur Challah)
candidates.notes: The minimum amount of dough (five-fourths of a kav) that triggers the challah obligation, and the proportion to be separated (1/24 for private bakers, 1/48 for commercial bakers)

candidates.name: Challah Outside the Land of Israel
candidates.notes: Differences in challah law between the Land of Israel, Syria, and lands further outside; three territorial zones with different obligations; two challah portions in Syria

candidates.name: Challah Obligation for Gentile Dough
candidates.notes: Whether dough belonging to or made by a non-Jew is subject to challah; cases of conversion and partnership with a non-Jew

candidates.name: Combining Different Grain Species for Challah
candidates.notes: Rules about which of the five grain species combine with each other to reach the minimum measure for challah; wheat and spelt combine, barley with other species except wheat, etc.

candidates.name: Challah and Ritual Purity
candidates.notes: Separating challah in a state of cleanness vs. uncleanness; proportions for intentionally vs. unintentionally defiled dough; separating from clean dough to exempt unclean dough

candidates.name: Challah and Hekdesh (Dedicated Dough)
candidates.notes: Effect of dedicating dough to the Temple before or after reaching the point of obligation on challah liability; parallel with tithes and produce dedicated before ripening

candidates.name: Dough Mixed with Rice or Non-Grain Ingredients
candidates.notes: Whether dough containing rice or other non-obligated species mixed with grain is subject to challah; depends on whether it has the taste of grain

candidates.name: Commercial Baker's Challah
candidates.notes: Commercial bakers separate a smaller proportion (1/48) than private individuals (1/24); women selling in the market treated like commercial bakers

candidates.name: Challah from Demai Dough
candidates.notes: Separating challah from demai (doubtfully tithed produce); challah for demai can be taken from clean dough for unclean, and even from dough not in close proximity

candidates.name: Three Territories for Challah (Land of Israel, Syria, Abroad)
candidates.notes: Rabban Gamliel's division of three zones — from Israel to Chezib (one challah portion), from Chezib to the river (two portions), and beyond the river (two portions with different rules for priest)

candidates.name: Point at Which Dough Becomes Obligated in Challah
candidates.notes: The rolling/kneading (galgul) for wheat or formation of solid mass for barley as the trigger for the challah obligation; eating before this point vs. liability for death afterwards

candidates.name: Geographic Restrictions on Bikkurim and Priestly Gifts
candidates.hebrew: גבולות ארץ ישראל לבכורים ומתנות כהונה
candidates.notes: Whether bikkurim, firstlings, and other priestly gifts brought from Syria, Babylon, or Alexandria are accepted; the rule that purchasing land in Syria is like purchasing land in the outskirts of Jerusalem

candidates.name: Challah Parallels to Terumah
candidates.notes: Rules shared between challah and terumah: karet for intentional consumption by non-priest, added fifth for inadvertent consumption, nullification in 101 parts, require handwashing and sunset, cannot separate from pure for impure

candidates.name: Israelite Tenant Farmer in Syria
candidates.notes: Dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabban Gamliel whether an Israelite who rents land from a non-Jew in Syria is liable for tithes and shemitah; eventual ruling followed Rabban Gamliel in both

candidates.name: Challah Obligation on Todah Loaves and Nazirite Wafers
candidates.notes: Todah loaves and nazirite wafers made for personal use are exempt from challah; if made for sale they are subject to challah

candidates.name: Laws of Demai — Detailed Framework
candidates.notes: Grouping for detailed laws of demai: exemptions, social categories, produce status, and practical rules

candidates.name: Kilayim in the Vineyard — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Grouping for detailed rules of kilei hakerem: vineyard structure, border spaces, espalier, and bending vines

candidates.name: Types of Kilayim (Mixed Species Categories)
candidates.notes: Grouping for the various categories of kilayim prohibition beyond planting: clothing (shatnez) and animal labor

candidates.name: Reishit HaGez — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: How many sheep trigger obligation; minimum amount of wool to give; distinction from foreleg/jaw/maw gifts; exemption if wool dyed before giving

candidates.name: Demai (Doubtfully Tithed Produce — Laws)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of demai: which produce is subject, exemptions, leniencies, and the full halakhic framework beyond the general entry

candidates.name: Produce Exempt from Demai
candidates.notes: Categories of produce treated leniently or fully exempt from demai laws: unripe figs, jujuba, capers, wild figs, etc.

candidates.name: Ne'eman (Trustworthy Person for Tithes)
candidates.notes: Laws of accepting upon oneself the status of ne'eman — one who is reliable in matters of tithes; obligations this entails

candidates.name: Chaver (Rabbinic Associate — Laws and Obligations)
candidates.notes: Laws of the chaver: one who accepts strict obligations regarding tithes and purity; restrictions on dealings with am haaretz; conditions for membership

candidates.name: Am HaAretz (in Context of Tithes)
candidates.notes: Halakhic status of the am haaretz in matters of tithes: produce bought from him, hosting him, and trusting his declarations

candidates.name: Verbal Tithing Declarations (Designating Tithes by Speech)
candidates.notes: Laws of designating tithes through verbal formulae, including tithing in advance, from a distance, or while in the house of study; complex formulas for combined terumah and tithe designations

candidates.name: Tithing in Advance (Hafrashat Maaser b'Tenai)
candidates.notes: Declaring tithes conditionally before Shabbat or before eating, so that the designation takes effect retroactively; especially in context of demai

candidates.name: Sharecropping and Tithes (Arisut)
candidates.notes: Laws of who is responsible for tithes when a field is rented for a share in the produce (aris); distinctions between Jewish, Gentile, Samaritan, priestly, and Levitical landowners

candidates.name: Samaritans' Produce (Kutim) — Tithes
candidates.notes: Laws regarding produce grown or sold by Samaritans (Kutim) in relation to tithes and demai; their trustworthiness in tithe declarations

candidates.name: Tithing From One Lot for Another
candidates.notes: Rules for when one may separate tithes from one batch of produce for another; distinctions between field owners, wholesalers, and vendors of different batches

candidates.name: Perforated Pot (Atzitz Nakuv) — Agricultural Law
candidates.notes: Status of produce grown in a perforated pot versus unperforated pot in relation to terumah and tithes; perforated pot treated as land

candidates.name: Maaser Ani of Demai (Poor Man's Tithe Designation)
candidates.notes: Whether one must designate (but need not separate) the poor man's tithe from demai produce; dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and the sages

candidates.name: Feeding Demai to the Poor
candidates.notes: Leniency permitting demai produce to be given to the poor, workers, and travelers without first separating all tithes

candidates.name: Produce of Syria — Tithe Status
candidates.notes: Laws of tithing produce sold or grown in Syria; when declarations of tithing or Land of Israel origin are trusted

candidates.name: Dividing Shared Produce Between Chaver and Am HaAretz
candidates.hebrew: חלוקת שותפות בין חבר לעם הארץ
candidates.notes: Rules for how a chaver and am haaretz who are partners or co-heirs may divide produce without the chaver violating tithe laws; what divisions are permitted and which are not

candidates.name: Agent Reliability in Tithe Matters (Shliach b'Maasrot)
candidates.notes: Rules for trusting an agent sent to purchase tithed produce; when agent's report can be relied upon and when not

candidates.name: Innkeeper and Produce Exchange (Suspicion of Switching)
candidates.notes: Suspicion that innkeeper or mother-in-law may exchange produce given to them with untithed produce of their own; resulting tithing obligations on what is returned

candidates.name: Produce Ground by Gentile Miller
candidates.notes: Wheat ground at a Gentile miller's mill acquires demai status; contrasted with Samaritan or am haaretz miller where original status is retained

candidates.name: Minimum Measure of Dough for Challah Obligation
candidates.notes: Dispute between Shammai (one kav), Hillel (two kavs), and the Sages (kav and a half / five quarters) regarding the minimum measure of dough obligated in challah; Eduyot 1:2

candidates.name: Exchanging Second Tithe for Uncoined Metal
candidates.notes: Dispute between Rabbi Dosa and the Sages whether second tithe may be redeemed for uncoined metal (asimon); Eduyot 3:2

candidates.name: Fourth Year Vineyard — Laws of Fifth and Removal
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel whether fourth-year vineyard fruit is subject to the additional fifth (chomesh) and the law of removal (biur); Eduyot 4:5

candidates.name: Large Forgotten Sheaf — Whether Subject to Shikchah
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (a four-kav sheaf that was forgotten is not subject to shikchah) and Beit Hillel (it is subject); Eduyot 4:3-4:4

candidates.name: Declaring Ownerless for the Poor Only
candidates.notes: Dispute whether declaring produce ownerless only for the poor (but not for the rich) counts as valid hefker for peah/shikchah purposes; Beit Shammai permits, Beit Hillel requires hefker for all; Eduyot 4:3

candidates.name: Female Captive and Her Eligibility to Eat Terumah
candidates.notes: Dispute regarding a priest's wife taken captive: whether she may eat terumah upon return; the role of self-testimony and corroborating witnesses; Eduyot 3:6

candidates.name: Prozbul — Hillel's Ordinance
candidates.notes: Hillel's institution of the prozbul document to prevent loan cancellation in the sabbatical year; Gittin 4:3

candidates.name: Wife's Right to Eat Teruma During Get Delivery Process
candidates.hebrew: אשת כהן ואכילת תרומה בעת שליחות גט
candidates.notes: When a priest's wife designates an agent to receive vs. deliver her get, and the effect on her right to eat teruma; Gittin 6:4

candidates.name: Kilayim of Seeds and Plants (Kilei Zeraim)
candidates.notes: Rules against sowing mixed seeds in a field; minimum separations, bed arrangements, and species that do or do not constitute kilayim with one another

candidates.name: Kilayim in a Vineyard — Detailed Rules (Kilei haKerem)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of sowing grain or vegetables near vines: required distances, karahat, mehol, aris, and what causes sanctification/prohibition of seed or vine

candidates.name: Kilayim of Clothing — Shatnez (כלאי בגדים / שעטנז)
candidates.notes: Prohibition of wearing wool and linen mixtures; what constitutes shatnez (spinning, weaving, combing); application to garments, mattresses, shrouds, packsaddles, sellers and tailors

candidates.name: Kilayim of Animals in Work (Kilei Beheimah b'Avodah)
candidates.notes: Prohibition of yoking, plowing, pulling, or leading together two different species of animals; includes liability for driver and passenger

candidates.name: Definition and Structure of a Vineyard (Tzurat haKerem)
candidates.notes: What constitutes a valid halachic vineyard: minimum rows and vines, layout patterns (two-opposite-two with tail), poor vineyard, ruined vineyard

candidates.name: Karahat and Mehol of a Vineyard
candidates.notes: Required minimum dimensions of bare patches (karahat) and border spaces (mehol) in a vineyard to permit sowing; dispute between Bet Shammai and Bet Hillel

candidates.name: Aris (Espalier Vineyard)
candidates.notes: Laws of vines trained along a fence or trellis (aris): required working-space, gaps in an aris, vines suspended over trees, projecting tendrils and blossoms

candidates.name: Bending and Conducting a Vine Underground (Havrakas haGefen)
candidates.notes: Rules for a vine bent into the ground and re-emerging elsewhere; soil cover required, measuring from the second root, combining of bent vines

candidates.name: Detailed Laws of Kilayim
candidates.notes: Grouping for detailed halakhic rules within the kilayim complex beyond the top-level entries

candidates.name: Flowerpot (Atzitz) in Kilayim Context
candidates.notes: Whether a perforated vs. non-perforated flowerpot carried through a vineyard creates kilayim prohibition

candidates.name: Species Classification for Kilayim Purposes
candidates.notes: Determining which plant and animal species are considered the 'same species' or 'different species' for kilayim law; domesticated vs. wild variants; behemah vs. hayyah classification

candidates.name: Sanctification (Prohibition) of Kilayim Produce in Vineyard
candidates.notes: When kilayim of the vineyard takes effect; what causes the seed and vine to become prohibited; forbidden benefit vs. merely forbidden sowing; from which growth stage prohibition begins

candidates.name: Grafting (Harkavah) in Kilayim
candidates.notes: Prohibition of grafting between different species: tree on tree, vegetable on vegetable, tree on vegetable; dispute of Rabbi Judah regarding vegetable on tree

candidates.name: Sowing Multiple Species in Garden Beds (Arugot)
candidates.notes: Rules for sowing up to five or thirteen different species in a small garden bed using borders; required dimensions of furrow and border to separate species

candidates.name: Detailed Laws of Maaser Sheni
candidates.notes: Grouping for the detailed halakhic rules governing second tithe: consumption, redemption, money exchange, permissible uses, impurity, and sanctity

candidates.name: Eating Maaser Sheni in Jerusalem
candidates.notes: Laws governing consumption of maaser sheni specifically in Jerusalem: bringing produce in and taking it out, produce passing through Jerusalem, produce that became impure, eating after Temple destruction

candidates.name: Maaser Sheni that Became Impure
candidates.notes: What happens when maaser sheni or items bought with maaser sheni money become ritually impure: redemption vs. burial, distinctions based on primary vs. secondary impurity, inside vs. outside Jerusalem

candidates.name: Exchange and Currency Laws of Maaser Sheni
candidates.notes: Laws of exchanging maaser sheni money: silver to copper, silver to gold, exchanging in Jerusalem, minimum denominations, changing a sela, debates between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel

candidates.name: Permissible Uses of Maaser Sheni (Food, Drink, Anointing)
candidates.notes: Maaser sheni may be used for eating, drinking, and anointing; prohibition on spicing oil; what may and may not be purchased with maaser sheni money; value improvements and proportional division

candidates.name: Maaser Sheni: Sacred in Value vs. Sacred in Body
candidates.hebrew: קדושת דמים וקדושת הגוף במעשר שני
candidates.notes: Whether the sanctity of maaser sheni is a bodily sanctity or a monetary sanctity, affecting rules of redemption, becoming impure, items bought with maaser sheni money

candidates.name: Transferring Maaser Sheni Status When Produce is Distant
candidates.notes: Procedure for designating and transferring maaser sheni or tithing when one is physically distant from the produce, including the famous case of Rabban Gamliel on the ship; leasing the location to effect the transfer

candidates.name: Second-Tithe Money for Offerings and Libations
candidates.notes: Rules about when second-tithe money may or may not be used to purchase obligatory offerings, voluntary offerings, or libations; libations may never come from second-tithe money

candidates.name: Redemption Procedures for Maaser Sheni
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of redeeming maaser sheni: adding a fifth (chomesh), who may redeem, redemption at lower market price, evaluation by one or three, redemption by owner vs. others, conditional redemption, deceptive redemption techniques

candidates.name: Adding a Fifth When Redeeming Maaser Sheni (Chomesh)
candidates.notes: Obligation to add one-fifth when redeeming one's own maaser sheni; who is obligated; applies to owner and one who received it as a gift; comparison with chomesh for redeeming other sacred items

candidates.name: Rules of Tithe Liability and Exemption
candidates.notes: Grouping for rules determining when and how tithe liability applies: onset of obligation, stages of ripeness, exemptions, and casual eating

candidates.name: Onset of Tithe Obligation (Shiur Malachah / Gmar Melachah)
candidates.notes: Covers when produce becomes obligated in tithes based on completion of agricultural work (threshing floor equivalent) — the specific trigger-point for each type of produce

candidates.name: Casual/Chance Eating Exempt from Tithes (Achilat Arai)
candidates.notes: The principle that eating produce in a casual, incidental manner (not as a formal meal) exempts one from tithing; contrasted with keva eating

candidates.name: Stages of Fruit Ripeness for Tithe Liability
candidates.notes: Specific determinations of when each type of fruit or vegetable reaches the stage at which tithes become obligatory (bichur/peel stage for various species)

candidates.name: Courtyard that Obligates Tithes (Chatzer haMechayevet Maaser)
candidates.notes: Which type of courtyard renders produce brought into it liable for tithes — rules about the nature of the courtyard as a formal domain

candidates.name: Tree Overhanging from One Domain to Another (Tithe Implications)
candidates.hebrew: אילן הנוטה לחצר אחרת לגבי מעשר
candidates.notes: Rules about when fruit from a tree overhanging from garden to courtyard (or from Israel to outside) is liable for tithes, based on root location

candidates.name: Jerusalem Rule: Tithe Determined by Branch Location
candidates.notes: Special rule that for trees overhanging Jerusalem's walls, tithe liability is determined by branch location rather than root location

candidates.name: Species-Specific Tithe Exemptions and Distinctions
candidates.notes: Grouping for rules determining which specific produce, seeds, or species are exempt from or subject to tithes

candidates.name: Exotic or Foreign Produce Exempt from Tithes
candidates.notes: Certain foreign species (e.g., Balbeck garlic, Rikpa onions, Egyptian lentils) exempt from tithes due to their origin

candidates.name: Seeds of Vegetables Not Eaten — Exempt from Tithes
candidates.hebrew: זרעי ירקות שאינם נאכלים פטורים ממעשר
candidates.notes: Seeds of garden vegetables that are inedible are exempt from tithes even if the parent plant was terumah

candidates.name: Tithing Dill and Coriander (Seeds, Plants, and Pods)
candidates.notes: Dispute about whether seeds, plant, and pods of dill and coriander are each separately subject to tithing

candidates.name: Grape-Skin Wine (Yayin Poret / Tirosh miGefanim)
candidates.notes: Rules about tithe obligations for secondary wine made by adding water to grape skins

candidates.name: Ants Carrying Grain Near Completed Pile
candidates.notes: Whether grain dragged by ants from a completed tithe-liable pile overnight is itself liable for tithes

candidates.name: Fourth Year Vineyard Produce (Kerem Revay — Laws)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of kerem revay: redemption procedures, borders of Jerusalem for transport, peret and defective clusters in fourth year, removal, and relation to maaser sheni laws

candidates.name: Biur Maaser Sheni (Removal of Second Tithe)
candidates.notes: The removal of maaser sheni on the eve of Pesach in the fourth and seventh years; timing; cooked dishes; what must be removed vs. what has already been treated as removed

candidates.name: Viduy Maaser (Tithe Confession/Declaration)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of the viduy maaser declaration (Deut. 26:13-15): text, timing (minhah of last festival day), who may recite it (Israelites, mamzerim; not converts or freed slaves per most opinions), disqualifying violations, the blessings invoked

candidates.name: Marking Orlah and Fourth Year Vines
candidates.notes: The practice of marking orlah trees with potter's clay and fourth-year vines with clods of earth and graves with lime; timing of these markings (in the seventh year according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel)

candidates.name: Worker's Right to Eat from Produce (Po'el Ochel)
candidates.notes: The Torah-mandated right of a hired agricultural worker to eat from the produce he harvests and the interaction of that right with tithe obligations

candidates.name: Selling Produce to One Untrusted in Tithes (Am HaAretz)
candidates.notes: Prohibitions on selling untithed produce or byproducts to those suspected of not tithing, and related rules about straw, grape pulp, and olive peat

candidates.name: Tithe Obligations for Produce from Syria
candidates.notes: Special rules governing tithe obligations for produce acquired in Syria, depending on whether the land was purchased

candidates.name: Separating Terumah Before Work is Completed
candidates.notes: Effect on chance-eating exemption when terumah is separated from produce before its agricultural work has been completed

candidates.name: Halakhic Distinction of Walled vs. Unwalled in Various Contexts
candidates.hebrew: הבדל בין מוקף חומה לשאינו מוקף חומה
candidates.notes: The concept of walled cities (from Joshua's time) appears in multiple halakhic contexts: Purim reading, eating consecrated food near Shiloh/Jerusalem, redemption of houses

candidates.name: Waving of Bikkurim
candidates.notes: First fruits require waving but not bringing near, per Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov

candidates.name: Detailed Laws of Orlah
candidates.notes: Grouped parent for detailed orlah sub-topics: tree purpose, replanting, bent shoots, geography, dye/oven, and counting rules

candidates.name: Orlah (Forbidden Fruit of First Three Years — Laws)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of orlah: what trees are subject, counting years, replanting, uprooting, grafting, and geographical differences (Israel, Syria, outside Israel)

candidates.name: Orlah Exemption Based on Purpose of Planting
candidates.notes: A tree planted as a fence or for lumber is exempt from orlah; if planted partly for food and partly for fence, the food-facing part is subject

candidates.name: Replanted Tree and Orlah Counting
candidates.notes: Rules for whether a uprooted and replanted tree restarts the orlah count, depending on whether it could survive on its own root

candidates.name: Bent-Down Shoot (Hiluch) and Orlah
candidates.notes: Laws of a layered/bent-down shoot: whether it takes on the status of its parent tree or is counted anew for orlah

candidates.name: Orlah in Syria and Outside the Land
candidates.notes: Geographical distinctions in orlah law: doubtful orlah is forbidden in Israel, permitted in Syria, and outside Israel one may purchase but not personally gather

candidates.name: Garment Dyed with Orlah — Burning Requirement
candidates.notes: A garment dyed with orlah peels must be burned; if mixed with other garments, Rabbi Meir requires all to be burned while Sages nullify in 201

candidates.name: Oven Heated with Orlah Wood — Bread Baked in It
candidates.notes: Bread baked in an oven heated with orlah shells must be burned; if mixed with other loaves, it is nullified in 201

candidates.name: Nullification of Kilayim of the Vineyard (Bitul)
candidates.notes: Rules for how kilayim of the vineyard become nullified in mixtures, how it combines with orlah, and when it can void terumah

candidates.name: Fourth-Year Vineyard Produce Laws (Kerem Revay/Neta Revay)
candidates.notes: Fourth-year fruit is subject to different rules from orlah: certain items (leaves, sprouts) are permitted in regard to the fourth year though restricted under orlah

candidates.name: Detailed Laws of Agricultural Gifts for the Poor
candidates.notes: Grouped parent for detailed laws of peah, leket, shikchah, olelot, maaser ani, and related topics concerning agricultural gifts to the poor

candidates.name: Peah (Corner of Field — Detailed Laws)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of peah: minimum amount, when and how to leave it, what divides a field for peah purposes, which crops are subject, and distribution to the poor

candidates.name: Leket (Gleanings — Detailed Laws)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of leket: what constitutes a gleaning vs. owner's property, fallen grain from hand/sickle, ant holes, harvesting by night or blind person

candidates.name: Shikchah (Forgotten Sheaf — Detailed Laws)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of shikchah: what qualifies as forgotten, end-of-row rules, sheaves of two seahs, trees (especially olives), standing grain saving sheaves, intentional forgetting

candidates.name: Olelot (Defective Grape Clusters)
candidates.notes: Laws of defective clusters of grapes left for the poor: definition (lacking shoulder and pendant), single grapes, entirely defective vineyard, timing of poor's access

candidates.name: Maaser Ani (Poor Tithe — Detailed Laws)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of poor man's tithe: trustworthiness of am haaretz regarding it, minimum amounts for distribution, sharecropper's rights, who may take it

candidates.name: Divisions of a Field for Agricultural Gifts
candidates.notes: What physical features (streams, roads, paths, fallow land, different species) divide a field requiring separate peah from each section; applies to trees and vines as well

candidates.name: Hefker for the Poor (Declaring Field Ownerless)
candidates.notes: Laws regarding declaring produce ownerless for the poor: debate between Bet Shammai and Bet Hillel on whether hefker for poor alone is valid hefker; effect on tithe obligations

candidates.name: Trustworthiness (Ne'emanut) Regarding Agricultural Gifts to Poor
candidates.notes: Rules on when an am haaretz is trusted to identify produce as leket, shikchah, peah, or poor tithe; distinctions based on processing stage (raw vs. cooked, whole vs. ground)

candidates.name: Fourth Year Vineyard — Peah and Poor Gifts
candidates.notes: Dispute between Bet Shammai and Bet Hillel on whether peret and olelot apply to fourth-year vineyard, and whether all fruit goes to the winepress

candidates.name: Sharecropper's Obligations for Agricultural Gifts
candidates.notes: Laws governing whether a sharecropper (aris) is permitted or forbidden to take leket, shikchah, peah, and maaser ani; depends on terms of sharecropping agreement

candidates.name: Land Requirement for Prozbul
candidates.notes: Rabbi Akiva's view that any size of land is sufficient to write a prozbul; minimum land size debate among Tannaim

candidates.name: Shikchah for Olive Trees
candidates.notes: Special laws of forgotten sheaf applied to olive trees: named trees exempt, trees with two seahs, trees between rows, timing after second rainfall; Rabbi Yose's opinion that no shikchah applies to olive trees

candidates.name: Separating Challah on Yom Tov (Hafrashat Challah b'Yom Tov)
candidates.notes: The problem of separating ritually impure challah on Passover Yom Tov when it cannot be burned yet; dispute between Rabbi Eliezer, Ben Beteira, and Rabbi Yehoshua about the proper procedure

candidates.name: Shofar of Yovel vs. Rosh HaShanah
candidates.hebrew: שופר של יובל ושל ראש השנה
candidates.notes: Comparison between the shofar blown on Yom Kippur of the Jubilee year and that of Rosh HaShanah; debate between R. Yehuda and sages about which horn is used

candidates.name: Diverse Species in a Garden Bed (Arugah)
candidates.notes: The rule permitting five different species in a six-by-six handbreadth garden bed, one in each corner and one in the center, without violating kilayim

candidates.name: Perforated and Unperforated Flowerpots (Atzitz Nakuv)
candidates.notes: The distinction between a perforated flowerpot (treated as connected to the ground) and unperforated pot for purposes of agricultural laws and Shabbat picking prohibition

candidates.name: Detailed Laws of the Sabbatical Year
candidates.notes: Grouped parent for detailed shemitah sub-topics: agricultural labor, sefichin, sanctity of produce, biur, territories, commerce, selling implements, and aiding violators

candidates.name: Plowing Restrictions Before the Sabbatical Year
candidates.notes: Rules governing when plowing of orchards and fields must cease in the sixth year before the sabbatical year begins

candidates.name: Agricultural Labor Permitted/Forbidden in the Sabbatical Year
candidates.notes: Detailed rules about which agricultural acts (manuring, pruning, watering, trimming, etc.) are permitted or forbidden during shemitah

candidates.name: Sefichin (Aftergrowths of the Sabbatical Year)
candidates.notes: Rabbinic prohibition against eating aftergrowths that grew on their own during the sabbatical year; exceptions and categories discussed

candidates.name: Sanctity of Sabbatical Year Produce (Kedushat Shvi'it)
candidates.notes: Laws governing the sacred status of produce grown in the sabbatical year: how it must be eaten, sold, and treated

candidates.name: Biur Shvi'it (Removal of Sabbatical Year Produce)
candidates.notes: Obligation to remove sabbatical produce from one's home when that species is no longer available in the field; three territories for this law; timing based on second rainfall

candidates.name: Three Territories of the Land for Shemitah
candidates.notes: Division of Israel into Judea, Transjordan, and Galilee (each subdivided into three regions) for purposes of biur shvi'it

candidates.name: Money Substitutes for Sabbatical Produce (Peidyon Shvi'it)
candidates.notes: Laws governing money received in exchange for sabbatical year produce, which acquires the sanctity of the produce itself

candidates.name: Prohibition of Commerce with Sabbatical Produce
candidates.notes: Prohibition against engaging in commercial trade using sabbatical year produce; one may only use it for personal consumption

candidates.name: Selling Agricultural Implements in the Sabbatical Year
candidates.notes: Restrictions on selling tools that may be used for forbidden agricultural work during shemitah; distinction between tools for forbidden and permitted use

candidates.name: Aiding Violators of Shemitah (Lifnei Iver in Shemitah Context)
candidates.notes: Rules about lending or selling items to those suspected of violating shemitah; includes cases involving neighbors and women borrowing kitchen items

candidates.name: Agricultural Rules of the Sabbatical Year
candidates.notes: Grouping of rules governing agricultural work, field preparation, and planting during the sabbatical year

candidates.name: Laws of Sabbatical Year Produce
candidates.notes: Grouping of rules governing the classification, use, and treatment of produce that grows during the sabbatical year

candidates.name: Geographic Scope of Shemitah (Outside Israel)
candidates.notes: Grouping of rules concerning application of shemitah laws to lands outside Israel, including Syria and produce export/import

candidates.name: Rules for Giving Terumah (Hafrashat Terumah)
candidates.notes: Grouping of rules governing who may separate terumah, from which produce, in what amounts, and how the designation is made

candidates.name: Terumah Mixtures and Nullification
candidates.notes: Grouping of rules governing terumah that has been mixed with hullin, flavor transfer, pickling, and the conditions for nullification

candidates.name: Eating Terumah and Repayment
candidates.notes: Grouping of rules governing the eating of terumah unlawfully and the obligations of repayment with or without the added fifth

candidates.name: Saplings in the Sabbatical Year (Neti'ot)
candidates.notes: Definition of saplings vs. trees for purposes of shemitah plowing rules; prohibition on planting, sinking shoots, or grafting within 30 days of Rosh Hashanah

candidates.name: Dung Heaps and Manure in Shemitah
candidates.notes: Rules about when and how to pile manure in fields during the sabbatical year without appearance of fertilizing for shemitah

candidates.name: Removing Stones from Fields in Shemitah
candidates.notes: Regulations about removing stones from one's field during the sixth year and sabbatical year to avoid appearance of field improvement

candidates.name: Rosh Hashanah as Shemitah Cutoff Date
candidates.notes: Rosh Hashanah serves as the determining date for whether produce or agricultural work is governed by the sixth or seventh year; rules for produce rooted before vs. after

candidates.name: Hefker of Sabbatical Produce (Ownerlessness)
candidates.notes: Obligation to make sabbatical produce ownerless and accessible to all; rules about gathering and eating ownerless produce from fields

candidates.name: Distribution of Sabbatical Produce at Time of Removal
candidates.notes: Rules about distributing sabbatical produce when biur time arrives; giving three meals to each person; poor vs. rich in post-biur consumption

candidates.name: Categories of Sabbatical Year Produce (Food, Dye, Animal Feed)
candidates.notes: Classification of plants subject to shemitah: human food, animal food, dyeing material; whether biur and money-substitute laws apply to each category

candidates.name: Intended Use Determining Shemitah Status
candidates.notes: How one's intention to use a plant as food, animal fodder, or wood determines which shemitah laws apply to it

candidates.name: Shemitah and Non-Jewish Fields
candidates.notes: Permissibility of renting plowed land from a Gentile in the seventh year and related rulings about working non-Jewish land

candidates.name: Shemitah in Syria
candidates.notes: Special rules for Syria regarding sabbatical year work and produce; permitted detached produce work but not attached; export rules

candidates.name: Export and Import of Sabbatical Produce and Terumah
candidates.notes: Prohibition against exporting sabbatical year produce or terumah from Israel to other countries; special status of Syria

candidates.name: Shemitat Kesafim — Loan Cancellation Details
candidates.notes: Detailed rules of loan cancellation: which debts are cancelled (documented, undocumented, wages, shop debts), and the verbal formula for remission

candidates.name: Prozbul — Details and Formula
candidates.notes: Hillel's enactment allowing debts to be collected after shemitah by transferring them to court; formula, validity rules (pre/post-dated), and land requirement

candidates.name: Bikkurim Declaration (Mikra Bikkurim)
candidates.notes: The specific verbal declaration recited when bringing first fruits to the Temple, required in Hebrew, and its textual content (Deuteronomy 26)

candidates.name: Amount/Measure of Terumah (Shiur Terumah)
candidates.notes: The prescribed proportions for giving terumah: generous (1/30), average (1/50), stingy (1/60), and disputes about minimum and maximum amounts

candidates.name: Who May Give Terumah (Ha-Torem)
candidates.notes: Rules about who is qualified to separate terumah: excludes deaf-mute, imbecile, minor, non-Jew, and others; partial disqualifications for mute, blind, drunk, naked

candidates.name: From Which Produce Terumah May Be Taken
candidates.notes: Rules prohibiting terumah from one species for another, from incomplete-processed produce for completed, from attached for detached, from new for old, from Israel for outside Israel, etc.

candidates.name: Terumah from Kilayim Species (Min b'Mino in Terumah)
candidates.notes: Prohibition against giving terumah from one species for another that is kilayim with it; rules about what counts as the same kind for terumah purposes

candidates.name: Verbal Designation of Terumah (Tenuat Peh)
candidates.notes: Requirements for valid verbal designation of terumah, including that mouth and heart must be in agreement (3:8), and how to designate from within a pile

candidates.name: Terumah Given Through an Agent (Shaliach)
candidates.notes: Rules about appointing a household member, slave, or worker to give terumah on one's behalf, and annulment of such authorization

candidates.name: Giving Terumah from Clean for Unclean Produce
candidates.notes: Rules about separating terumah from pure produce for impure produce and vice versa, disputes between Rabbi Eliezer and sages

candidates.name: Intentional vs. Unintentional Violation in Terumah
candidates.notes: Distinctions between acting intentionally (mezid) versus unintentionally (shogeg) in giving terumah from improper sources, eating terumah, planting on Shabbat, etc.

candidates.name: Eating Terumah Unwittingly (Ochel Terumah b'Shogeg)
candidates.notes: Obligation to repay value plus one-fifth (chomesh) for unintentional eating of terumah; who pays the principal and who pays the fifth

candidates.name: Eating Terumah Intentionally (Ochel Terumah b'Mezid)
candidates.notes: One who eats terumah intentionally repays only the principal value, not the added fifth; the repayment remains hullin and the priest may waive it

candidates.name: Repayment of Eaten Terumah — Same or Different Species
candidates.hebrew: פרעון תרומה שנאכלה מין על מינו
candidates.notes: Dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva whether one repays terumah with the same kind or with any superior kind; repayment becomes terumah in the priest's possession

candidates.name: Medumma (Terumah Mixed with Hullin)
candidates.notes: Produce that has become forbidden through mixture of terumah falling into hullin; rules of nullification in 100 parts, proportional rendering of subsequent mixtures

candidates.name: Nullification of Terumah in 100 Parts (Bitul Terumah)
candidates.notes: The rule that terumah is nullified when mixed with 100 parts hullin; disputes about how to count, cross-type nullification, and deliberate addition of hullin

candidates.name: Flavor/Taste Imparted by Terumah (Noten Taam)
candidates.notes: Rules about terumah ingredients (onions, spices, wine) imparting forbidden flavor to hullin mixtures; application of noten ta'am principle to terumah context

candidates.name: Pickling Hullin Together with Terumah (Kavush b'Terumah)
candidates.notes: Rules about vegetables or olives of hullin pickled together with terumah, whether whole or crushed; prohibited brine resulting from unclean fish

candidates.name: Produce That Grows from Terumah Seeds
candidates.notes: Status of produce growing from terumah seeds: first growth is terumah, second growth is hullin; distinction between seeds that disintegrate and those that do not

candidates.name: Planting Terumah Seeds
candidates.notes: Rules about planting terumah seeds: if unwitting may overturn; if intentional must let remain; distinction based on whether seeds disintegrate in soil

candidates.name: Uncovered Terumah Liquids (Gilui)
candidates.notes: Terumah wine left uncovered must be poured out due to snake-venom concern; also applies to hullin water, wine, and milk left uncovered

candidates.name: Burning Terumah Oil That Must Be Destroyed
candidates.notes: Permissibility of using terumah oil that must be burned for lighting in synagogues, study houses, dark alleys, for the sick, and in celebration vs. mourning houses

candidates.name: Order of Separating Terumah and Tithes
candidates.notes: Bikkurim precedes terumah, terumah precedes maaser rishon, maaser rishon precedes maaser sheni; violation of this order, though a transgression, is post-facto valid

candidates.name: Priest's Daughter Married to Israelite and Terumah
candidates.notes: A daughter of a priest who married an Israelite loses right to eat terumah; if she ate she repays value but not fifth; her adultery penalty differs from ordinary case

candidates.name: Rules of Terumah Separation
candidates.notes: Halakhot governing the act of separating terumah: who may separate, conditions and stipulations, processing stages, and partnership arrangements

candidates.name: Eligibility and Disqualification from Eating Terumah
candidates.notes: Who is permitted or disqualified from eating terumah, including priests with blemishes or disqualifying lineage, and women based on marital status

candidates.name: Stage of Processing Required for Terumah Obligation
candidates.notes: Whether terumah may be taken from olives for oil before pressing or grapes for wine before treading; rules about completed vs. incomplete processing

candidates.name: Partners Separating Terumah
candidates.notes: Rules when two partners separately take terumah from shared produce; dispute about validity of both or only the first; depends on whether they conferred

candidates.name: Conditional Separation of Terumah
candidates.notes: Separating terumah subject to a condition (e.g., 'let this be terumah if it comes up safely' or 'let this be terumah of tithe after nightfall'); whether such conditional designations take effect.

candidates.name: Court Stipulation in Terumah Separation (Tenai Beit Din)
candidates.notes: The court-established stipulation that if terumah separated under a condition (e.g., 'if it comes up safely') breaks before reaching the cistern, it does not retroactively subject the cistern contents to terumah restrictions.

candidates.name: Discovery of Disqualifying Status After Eating Terumah
candidates.hebrew: נודע שהוא בן גרושה כשאכל תרומה
candidates.notes: What happens when a priest discovers mid-eating that he was disqualified (son of divorced woman/halutzah, or has blemish); dispute whether to swallow or spit out

candidates.name: Eligibility to Eat Teruma Based on Marital Status
candidates.notes: When an Israelite woman married to a priest may eat teruma; disqualification through forbidden unions; effects of pregnancy, children, betrothal, and yibbum bond on teruma rights

candidates.name: Disqualification of Kohen's Wife from Teruma by Intercourse
candidates.notes: How forbidden intercourse or betrothal to prohibited men disqualifies a priest's wife from eating teruma; betrothal vs. marriage for this purpose; dispute between Rabbi Elazar/Shimon and the Sages

candidates.name: Doubtful Terumah (Safek Terumah) in Baskets
candidates.notes: Cases of doubt as to which basket contains terumah; the remaining basket treated as terumah for challah purposes; liability when one eats from uncertain basket

candidates.name: Terumah Separated by a Levite from His Tithes
candidates.notes: Rules about a Levite who gave terumah from tithe that had not yet had terumat maaser separated; validity depends on whether done intentionally or inadvertently

candidates.name: Terumah Given by Non-Jew or Samaritan
candidates.notes: Status of terumah, tithes, and dedications given by a non-Jew or Samaritan; dispute about fourth-year vineyard law for non-Jews; whether non-Jewish terumah renders medumma

candidates.name: Feeding Terumah to Animals
candidates.notes: Vetches of terumah may be fed to cattle, wild beasts, and fowl; rules about who may feed terumah to animals based on ownership and hiring arrangements

candidates.name: Stolen Terumah and Its Repayment
candidates.notes: One who steals terumah and eats it must pay double at hullin price plus principal; stealing and not eating requires double payment at terumah price

candidates.name: Changing Terumah Produce from Its Natural State
candidates.notes: Prohibition against changing terumah from its natural state (e.g., dates to honey, grapes to raisins for wine); exceptions only for olives and grapes

candidates.name: Fruit Juice of Terumah as Liquid (Michshirin)
candidates.notes: Dispute whether fruit juices other than wine and olive oil (e.g., date honey, apple wine) are considered liquids for purposes of terumah and susceptibility to impurity

candidates.name: Ammon and Moab in the Seventh Year (Tithes)
candidates.notes: Halakhic debate about which tithe applies to Ammon and Moab in the seventh year (maaser ani vs. maaser sheni); methodology of legal analogy

candidates.name: Samuel the Prophet as Nazirite
candidates.notes: Aggadic discussion on whether Samuel was a nazirite based on the word 'mora' in Hannah's prayer; comparison with Samson.

candidates.name: Ḥoni HaMe'aggel and the Circle (Drawing a Circle for Prayer)
candidates.notes: The narrative of Ḥoni drawing a circle and refusing to move until rain fell; his exchange with Shimon ben Shetach; paradigm of the tzaddik whose prayers are answered

candidates.name: Pit Damage (Bor) — Detailed Rules
candidates.notes: Grouping of detailed rules concerning liability for pit damage, including depth requirements and exemptions for vessels

candidates.name: Fire Damage (Eish) — Detailed Rules
candidates.notes: Grouping of detailed rules concerning liability for fire damage, including spread of fire and hidden items

candidates.name: Condemned Ox (Shor HaNiskal) — Detailed Rules
candidates.notes: Grouping of detailed rules concerning the condemned ox: goring slaves, ransom payments, and exemptions for ownerless/consecrated/gentile oxen

candidates.name: Found Objects with Sacred or Temple-Related Status
candidates.notes: Grouping of rules for found objects whose sacred status must be determined: inscribed money/vessels, money near Temple collection horns, meat in Jerusalem or the Temple courtyard, and animals found near Jerusalem

candidates.name: Forewarned Ox Killing a Canaanite Slave
candidates.notes: Fixed payment of 30 sela regardless of slave's value; contrast with killing a freeman; injury payment based on actual damage

candidates.name: Innocuous Ox (Shor Tam) — Liability from Body of Ox
candidates.notes: The principle that an innocuous ox's owner pays only half-damages exclusively from proceeds of the sale of the belligerent ox, not from other assets

candidates.name: Tooth and Foot Damage (Shen veTefes/Regel)
candidates.notes: Detailed rules for the primary categories of Tooth (eating) and Foot (trampling) damage, including exemption in public domain and payment for benefit derived

candidates.name: Pit Depth Requirement for Liability
candidates.notes: Rule that a pit must be at least ten handbreadths deep to create full liability for death; lesser depth creates liability only for injury

candidates.name: Pit Liability — Exemption for Vessels
candidates.notes: Torah edict exempting the digger of a pit from liability for damage to vessels (as opposed to animals) that fall in

candidates.name: Person Always Forewarned (Adam Muad leOlam)
candidates.notes: The principle that a person is always considered forewarned for damage he causes, whether intentional or unintentional, asleep or awake, requiring full damages

candidates.name: Fire Damage — Liability for Spread of Fire
candidates.notes: Detailed rules on how far fire can spread before owner loses liability, including disputes of Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Akiva, and Rabbi Shimon

candidates.name: Fire Damage — Hidden Items in Stack
candidates.notes: Dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbis whether one who sets fire to a stack is liable for concealed vessels inside it; in a house, all agree he is liable

candidates.name: Robbery with False Oath — Additional Fifth (Chomesh)
candidates.notes: One who robs and takes a false oath must pay principal plus one-fifth additional, and bring a guilt offering; the one-fifth compounds if he takes further false oaths

candidates.name: Robbing a Convert Who Died Without Heirs — Payment to Priests
candidates.notes: One who robs a convert who subsequently dies without heirs must pay the principal plus a fifth to the priests and bring a guilt-offering

candidates.name: Double Payment for Theft (Kefel) — Detailed Rules
candidates.notes: Detailed rules on when kefel applies: admission vs. witness testimony, stolen-then-stolen items, partial sales, invalid slaughter, and interaction with fourfold/fivefold payments

candidates.name: Fourfold and Fivefold Payment (Arba v'Chamisha)
candidates.notes: Fourfold payment for sheep and fivefold for ox when a thief slaughters or sells a stolen animal; detailed rules on when this applies vs. only double payment

candidates.name: Ox Goring a Slave — Thirty Shekel Payment
candidates.notes: Fixed payment of thirty sela when an ox kills a Canaanite slave, regardless of the slave's actual value (whether worth one dinar or one hundred maneh)

candidates.name: Ransom Payment (Kofer) for Forewarned Ox that Kills
candidates.notes: Owner of a forewarned ox that kills a person pays ransom (kofer); owner of innocuous ox is exempt from ransom; both oxen are put to death

candidates.name: Prohibition on Raising Small Animals in Settled Eretz Yisrael
candidates.hebrew: איסור גידול בהמה דקה ביישוב ארץ ישראל
candidates.notes: Rabbinic prohibition on raising small livestock (sheep, goats) in settled areas of Eretz Yisrael due to crop damage; permitted in Syria and wilderness

candidates.name: Ox Forewarned for One Species/Type but Not Another
candidates.notes: An ox may be forewarned regarding one species, size category, or day (e.g., Shabbat) but innocuous for others, with differential liability accordingly

candidates.name: Goring by Ownerless, Consecrated, or Gentile Ox — Exemptions
candidates.hebrew: נגיחת שור הפקר והקדש ושל גוי
candidates.notes: Exemptions from ox-goring liability when the goring or gored ox is consecrated property; and the rule that a gentile's ox that gores a Jew's ox is always liable for full damages

candidates.name: Pigeon Trap Distance Rule
candidates.notes: Prohibition on spreading traps for pigeons within thirty ris of any settled area to prevent catching privately owned birds

candidates.name: Tyrian Maneh (Coinage Standard)
candidates.notes: The Tyrian maneh as the standard for various Torah monetary obligations including the five sela of pidyon haben, thirty shekel for slave killed by ox, fifty shekel for rape/seduction, and one hundred shekel for defamer; Tyrian coinage worth eight times provincial coinage

candidates.name: Stolen Beam Built Into a Palace — Monetary Restitution
candidates.hebrew: קורה גזולה שבנאה בבירה — תשלום דמים
candidates.notes: Testimony that a stolen beam built into a palace may be restored through monetary payment of its value rather than returning the beam itself; Eduyot 7:9 (related to the Talmudic principle of takkanat hashavim)

candidates.name: Found Objects with Markings of Sacred Status
candidates.notes: Laws of found money, vessels, or produce with inscriptions indicating korban, maaser, demai, tevel, or terumah: how to determine their status, presumptions applied, single-letter abbreviations used in times of danger.

candidates.name: Found Money Near Temple Horns
candidates.notes: Rules for determining the status of money found between collection horns or between sacred and non-sacred containers; follows proximity, and in case of equidistance follows the more stringent allocation

candidates.name: Found Meat in Jerusalem or Temple Courtyard
candidates.notes: Rules for determining the status of found meat based on its form (whole limbs vs. small pieces) and location (courtyard, Jerusalem, or outlying areas)

candidates.name: Found Animal Near Jerusalem (Behemah haNimtzet)
candidates.hebrew: בהמה הנמצאת בין ירושלים למגדל עדר
candidates.notes: An animal found straying within a certain distance of Jerusalem is presumed to be designated for an offering; males presumed burnt-offerings, females peace-offerings

candidates.name: Conspiring Witnesses — Detailed Rules (Edim Zomimin)
candidates.notes: Cluster of detailed sub-rules governing the application of edim zomimin: punishment calculation, timing relative to verdict, group testimony invalidation, and organized conspiracy concern

candidates.name: Document Drafting and Formal Requirements
candidates.notes: Cluster of rules governing the formal requirements and drafting of legal documents: tied vs. ordinary documents, contradictory amounts, erased notes, identical names, scribe's rules

candidates.name: Testimony for Permitting a Wife to Remarry (Agunah)
candidates.notes: Cluster of rules governing the special evidentiary standards applied to permit a wife to remarry after her husband's death: single witness, hearsay, women/slaves, bat kol, body identification, water cases

candidates.name: Tied vs. Ordinary Legal Documents (Mekuyyam)
candidates.notes: Distinction between ordinary (pashut) and tied/folded (mekushshar) documents; number of witnesses required for each; placement of signatures (Bava Batra ch. 10)

candidates.name: Erased or Contradictory Amounts in Documents
candidates.hebrew: שטר עם סכומים סותרים או מחוקים
candidates.notes: Rules when a promissory note contains contradictory amounts or erased text; principle of following the lower amount and the bottom entry (Bava Batra 10:2)

candidates.name: Two People with Identical Names in One City
candidates.notes: Problem of two people sharing identical names in the same city for purposes of legal documents; how to distinguish them and what happens to promissory notes when one is paid (Bava Batra 10:7)

candidates.name: Erased Promissory Note — Ratification
candidates.notes: Procedure for ratifying a promissory note that has been erased: producing witnesses who remember its contents and having court issue a new ratification document (Bava Batra 10:6)

candidates.name: Scribe's Rules for Writing Documents
candidates.notes: Rules about when a scribe may write a document for one party without the other being present: get, receipt, promissory note, bill of sale, betrothal documents, sharecropping contracts (Bava Batra ch. 10)

candidates.name: Documents Produced in Gentile Courts
candidates.notes: Validity of documents authenticated by gentile courts for monetary matters, with exception for bills of divorce and manumission; Gittin 1:5

candidates.name: Court Coercion to Bring Voluntary Offering
candidates.notes: Court repossesses property of those obligated in burnt offerings and peace offerings; coercion until person says 'I want to'; parallel to coerced get; distinction from sin and guilt offerings

candidates.name: Prohibition of Wages for Judging or Testifying
candidates.notes: Prohibition against taking wages to serve as judge, witness, or to sprinkle purification waters; rulings of such persons are void; exceptions for compensation for lost work time and transportation

candidates.name: Expert Judge Exempt from Liability for Erroneous Ruling
candidates.notes: An expert judge recognized by the court is exempt from paying compensation for an erroneous ruling, illustrated by the incident of Rabbi Tarfon and the hysterectomized cow; non-experts bear financial responsibility

candidates.name: Recording Minority Opinions in Halakha
candidates.notes: The principle and rationale for recording dissenting individual opinions alongside the majority ruling, so future courts may rely on them; discussed explicitly in Eduyot 1:5-1:6

candidates.name: Court Overruling a Prior Court's Decision
candidates.hebrew: בית דין מבטל דברי בית דין חברו
candidates.notes: The rule that a court may not overturn another court's ruling unless it exceeds the prior court in both wisdom and number; Eduyot 1:5

candidates.name: Akavia ben Mahalalel — Refusal to Retract and Excommunication
candidates.notes: The story of Akavia ben Mahalalel who refused to retract four rulings despite being offered the role of head of court; his excommunication and death while excommunicated; Eduyot 5:6-5:7

candidates.name: Pigeon Racers Disqualified as Witnesses
candidates.notes: Testimony that those who fly racing pigeons are disqualified from giving testimony; Eduyot 2:7

candidates.name: Samaritan Witnesses on Legal Documents
candidates.notes: General invalidity of Samaritan witnesses on documents, with the exception of bills of divorce and manumission; Gittin 1:5

candidates.name: Rulings of Admon (Seven Decrees)
candidates.notes: Seven disputed rulings by the Jerusalem judge Admon, including field ownership after signing as witness, lost path to field, cross-debts

candidates.name: Rulings of Ḥanan ben Avishalom
candidates.notes: Two rulings by Jerusalem judge Ḥanan regarding wife's oath when husband is overseas and reimbursement to one who sustained another's wife

candidates.name: Edim Zomimin — Punishment Calculation
candidates.notes: Specific rules for calculating the punishment of conspiring witnesses, including the division of monetary penalties among witnesses vs. lashes, and the principle that punishment mirrors what they sought to inflict

candidates.name: Edim Zomimin — After Verdict (Not After Execution)
candidates.hebrew: עדים זוממין — לאחר גמר דין ולא לאחר מיתה
candidates.notes: Dispute between Sages and Sadducees: conspiring witnesses are punished after the verdict is finalized but before execution of the condemned, not only after the condemned is killed

candidates.name: Edim Zomimin — Group Testimony Invalidation
candidates.notes: Rules regarding when one disqualified or conspiring witness voids an entire group's testimony; dispute between Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi regarding monetary vs. capital cases

candidates.name: Hazamat Edim (Impeachment of Witnesses)
candidates.notes: The procedural mechanism for rendering witnesses as conspiring (zomemim): witnesses must be impeached personally (alibi-style), not merely contradicted in content

candidates.name: Istatit — Concern of Organized Witness Conspiracy
candidates.notes: Rabbi Yehuda's position that when one set of witnesses renders many successive sets conspiring, this raises concern of organized conspiracy (istatit), and only the first set is executed

candidates.name: Sanhedrin Charutzit — Destructive vs. Virtuous Tribunal
candidates.notes: Dispute regarding a Sanhedrin that executes frequently: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya (once in 70 years = destructive); Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva (would find technical grounds to avoid all executions); Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's response that this increases murderers

candidates.name: Ostracism/Excommunication (Nidui) — Practical Halakhot
candidates.notes: Practical consequences of nidui including prohibition on haircutting and laundering; release from nidui on Chol HaMoed and its effects

candidates.name: Disqualified Witnesses (Gamblers, Usurers, Dove Racers, Shevi'it Merchants, Slaves)
candidates.notes: Categories of people disqualified from giving testimony, as enumerated in Rosh HaShanah: dice players, usurers, pigeon racers, shevi'it merchants, and slaves

candidates.name: Land (Real Property) Not Subject to Oaths or Double Payment
candidates.notes: Land, documents, Canaanite slaves, and consecrated property are exempt from oaths, double payment, and bailees' liability — Shevuot 6:5

candidates.name: Sennacherib's Mixing of the Nations
candidates.notes: The legal principle that Sennacherib's deportations mixed national identities, nullifying national-based prohibitions such as the ban on Ammonites

candidates.name: Testimony of Wife Regarding Husband's Death for Remarriage
candidates.notes: Special rules permitting a woman to testify about her husband's death to allow remarriage; one witness; hearsay; testimony of women, slaves, and gentiles; credibility standards

candidates.name: Testimony on Order of Deaths for Levirate Exemption
candidates.hebrew: עֵדוּת עַל סֵדֶר מִיתוֹת לְעִנְיַן יִבּוּם
candidates.notes: Cases where a woman testifies about whether her husband or child died first; presumptive status and its effect on the credibility of testimony regarding yibbum obligation

candidates.name: Falling into Water — Testimony of Death
candidates.notes: When a man falls into water, rules about testifying to his death; distinction between water with visible end and without visible end; cases from tradition

candidates.name: Identification of the Dead (Partzuf and Simanim)
candidates.notes: Requirement to identify a corpse by the facial features (partzuf); three-day limit; inadequacy of bodily marks or belongings alone for testimony permitting remarriage

candidates.name: Relying on a Disembodied Voice (Bat Kol) for Permitting Remarriage
candidates.notes: Unusual leniency of relying on a disembodied voice as evidence of a husband's death; specific cases cited in the Mishnah

candidates.name: Single Witness Testifying to Husband's Death
candidates.notes: Special rabbinic leniency allowing a woman to remarry based on one witness testifying to her husband's death; tradition from Rabban Gamliel the Elder; inclusion of women, slaves, hearsay

candidates.name: Rival Wife's Testimony — Inadmissibility
candidates.notes: Five categories of women not deemed credible to testify about each other's husbands' deaths due to conflicts of interest: rival wife, mother-in-law, stepdaughter, daughter of mother-in-law, yavam's wife

candidates.name: Laws of Idolatry (Avodah Zarah)
candidates.notes: Comprehensive grouping of practical halakhot related to idol worship, benefit from idols, interaction with gentiles in context of idolatry, and related prohibitions

candidates.name: Cities of Refuge — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Detailed halakhot governing exile, residence in cities of refuge, the role of the High Priest's death, roads, and the blood redeemer

candidates.name: Components of Injury Compensation — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Detailed halakhot governing each of the five components of bodily injury compensation

candidates.name: Execution of a Pregnant Woman
candidates.notes: Court does not wait for pregnant condemned woman to give birth; but if she sat on the birthing chair, execution is delayed; distinction from benefit of her hair after death

candidates.name: Defamer's Fine (Motzi Shem Ra) — 100 Sela
candidates.notes: 100 sela fixed fine regardless of woman's status; compared to rapist/seducer 50 sela; lesson that speech-based sin is graver than action; connection to spies narrative

candidates.name: Avodah Zarah (Idol Worship — General Prohibitions)
candidates.notes: General prohibitions related to idol worship including business dealings, selling items, and benefiting from idols

candidates.name: Commerce Near Gentile Festivals
candidates.hebrew: אסור לשאת ולתת עם הגוים לפני אידיהם
candidates.notes: Prohibition on conducting business with gentiles in the days before their festivals, lest they give thanks to their idols

candidates.name: Selling Items to Gentiles (Issurei Mechirah)
candidates.notes: Prohibitions on selling certain items to gentiles including animals, weapons, and items used for idol worship

candidates.name: Selling Large Animals to Gentiles
candidates.notes: Prohibition against selling large domesticated animals to gentiles lest they cause the Jew's animal to perform labor on Shabbat

candidates.name: Renting Property to Gentiles
candidates.notes: Laws governing renting houses and fields to gentiles in Eretz Yisrael, Syria, and outside Israel, due to concerns about idol worship and land settlement

candidates.name: Nullification of Idols (Bitul Avodah Zarah)
candidates.notes: Laws governing how an idol's forbidden status is revoked, including who can nullify it and what acts constitute nullification

candidates.name: Benefit from Idolatry (Hanaah min Avodah Zarah)
candidates.notes: Prohibition on deriving any benefit from objects of idol worship, their accessories, and items that served idol worship

candidates.name: Ashera (Idolatrous Tree)
candidates.notes: Laws of trees planted or used for idol worship, including their forbidden status, benefit from their shade, and nullification

candidates.name: Markulis (Mercury Idol)
candidates.notes: Laws specific to the Mercury idol worshipped by stone-casting, including which stones near it are forbidden

candidates.name: Statues (Tzlamim) and Idolatrous Images
candidates.notes: Laws regarding statues and images assumed to be idols, what makes them forbidden, and fragments of statues

candidates.name: Leaving Animals with Gentiles
candidates.notes: Prohibition on keeping animals in gentile inns due to suspicion of bestiality

candidates.name: Jewish Midwife Assisting Gentile Birth
candidates.notes: Prohibition on a Jewish woman delivering a gentile child as she would be aiding the birth of an idolater; permitted in the reverse

candidates.name: Nursing by Gentile Woman
candidates.notes: Conditions under which a gentile woman may nurse a Jewish child and restrictions on Jewish woman nursing a gentile child

candidates.name: Haircut from a Gentile
candidates.notes: Prohibition on receiving a haircut from a gentile due to danger, with dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbis regarding public thoroughfare

candidates.name: Building for Idol Worship
candidates.notes: Prohibition on assisting in building structures used for idol worship such as basilicas, tribunals, and stadiums

candidates.name: Accessories of Idol Worship (Mishimshei Avodah Zarah)
candidates.notes: Forbidden status of items used as accessories for idol worship and how nullification of the idol affects its accessories

candidates.name: Idols Abandoned in Peacetime vs. Wartime
candidates.notes: Distinction between idols abandoned voluntarily in peacetime (permitted) vs. in wartime under duress (prohibited)

candidates.name: Gentile's Own Idol — Immediate Prohibition
candidates.hebrew: עבודה זרה של גוי אסורה מיד
candidates.notes: A gentile's idol is forbidden immediately upon its fashioning; a Jew's idol only becomes forbidden upon actual worship

candidates.name: Idolatry Laws Specific to Eretz Yisrael
candidates.notes: Special stringencies in Eretz Yisrael regarding renting to gentiles, land settlement, and avoiding support of idolatry on holy land

candidates.name: Five Payments for Bodily Injury
candidates.notes: The five components of compensation for bodily injury: damage (nezek), pain (tza'ar), medical costs (ripui), loss of livelihood (shevet), and humiliation (boshet)

candidates.name: Pain Compensation (Tza'ar)
candidates.notes: Compensation for pain caused by injury, assessed by how much the victim would accept to undergo such pain; separate from damage to the body's monetary value

candidates.name: Medical Cost Compensation (Ripui)
candidates.notes: Ongoing obligation to pay for the injured party's medical treatment; if wound reopens, liability continues; ends when wound fully heals

candidates.name: Loss of Livelihood Compensation (Shevet)
candidates.notes: Compensation for income lost during convalescence, assessed as wages of a cucumber watchman (not the victim's professional wages, which are subsumed in the damage payment)

candidates.name: Humiliation Assessment (Boshet) — Factors and Method
candidates.notes: Method and factors for assessing humiliation damages, including the dignity of both parties; specific fixed amounts for slap, back-of-hand slap, spitting, uncovering a woman's head

candidates.name: Capital Liability Exempts from Monetary Payment
candidates.notes: One who is liable for capital punishment for an act (e.g., injuring a parent, desecrating Shabbat) is exempt from monetary payments for the same act

candidates.name: Self-Injury: Exempt for Self, Liable for Others
candidates.notes: One who injures himself is exempt from penalties, but others who cause the same injury are liable; analogously, one who damages his own property is exempt but others are liable

candidates.name: Compensation for Miscarriage (Nezek Vlad)
candidates.notes: A person who causes a woman to miscarry must pay compensation for the miscarried offspring to the husband; assessed by value difference of the woman before and after birth, or by value of offspring

candidates.name: Karet (Excision from the World-to-Come)
candidates.notes: The 36 categories of transgression punishable by karet, their enumeration, and the distinction between intentional (karet) and unwitting (sin offering) violation

candidates.name: Galut — Exile for Unintentional Murder
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of who is exiled and who is not: downward vs. upward motion, permission to be in location, optional vs. obligatory activity, blind persons, enemies, and categories of people exempt from exile

candidates.name: Goel HaDam — Blood Redeemer's Powers and Limits
candidates.notes: Specific halakhot of the blood redeemer: within vs. outside the city of refuge boundary, debate whether killing outside boundary is a mitzva, optional, or forbidden

candidates.name: Death of High Priest Releasing Exiled Murderer
candidates.notes: The law that an unintentional murderer returns from exile upon the death of the High Priest; types of High Priests whose death effects this release; mothers providing sustenance so exiles won't pray for the Kohen Gadol's death

candidates.name: Cities of Refuge — Practical Laws of Residence
candidates.notes: Practical rules of residence in the city of refuge: paying rent to Levites, returning to prior office upon release, prohibition on leaving for any purpose including testimony, killing in city requires relocation within city

candidates.name: Roads to Cities of Refuge (Derakhim l'Arei Miklat)
candidates.notes: Obligation to prepare and straighten roads to cities of refuge; court providing two Torah scholars to accompany the fleeing murderer and dissuade the blood redeemer

candidates.name: Malkot — Detailed Laws of Flogging
candidates.notes: Grouping for detailed procedural and legal rules governing the administration of malkot

candidates.name: Malkot — Procedure for Flogging
candidates.notes: Detailed procedure for administering lashes: position of condemned, composition and size of the strap, distribution of lashes (one-third front, two-thirds back), role of court crier reciting verses, assessment of physical capacity

candidates.name: Malkot — Medical Assessment of Capacity (Shuma)
candidates.notes: Requirement to assess beforehand how many lashes the condemned can survive; number must be divisible by three; reassessment after flogging begins; exemption if he cannot receive more

candidates.name: Malkot Atones for Karet
candidates.notes: The principle that one liable to karet who receives lashes is exempted from karet, based on the verse 'your brother shall be debased before your eyes' — he is restored to brotherhood after flogging

candidates.name: Malkot for Multiple Simultaneous Violations
candidates.hebrew: מלקות על עבירות מרובות בבת אחת
candidates.notes: Case of one who performs a single act and violates multiple prohibitions simultaneously, receiving multiple sets of lashes; illustrative case of plowing with multiple concurrent violations

candidates.name: Prohibitions of Body Marking and Grooming
candidates.notes: Grouping for prohibitions enforced via malkot relating to prohibited body marking and grooming practices: tattooing, bald spots in mourning, rounding of head and beard

candidates.name: Prohibition of Tattooing (Ketovet Ka'aka)
candidates.notes: Laws of the prohibition against tattooing: requires both incision in skin and insertion of dye to be liable; debate whether writing God's name is required

candidates.name: Prohibition of Bald Spot in Mourning (Korcha)
candidates.notes: Prohibition against making a bald spot on one's head in mourning; multiple incisions yield multiple sets of lashes

candidates.name: Prohibition of Rounding Head and Beard (Peot)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of the prohibitions against rounding the corners of the head and marring the edges of the beard; number of lashes for each edge; requirement of razor specifically for beard

candidates.name: Shatnez — Lashes for Wearing Mixed Species
candidates.notes: The specific rule that wearing shatnez repeatedly after forewarning incurs separate sets of lashes each time; continuous wearing incurs only one set

candidates.name: War Exemptions (Petur miMilchama)
candidates.notes: Categories of men exempt from military service: new house not dedicated, vineyard not yet used, betrothed not yet married; distinction between obligatory and elective wars
