candidates.name: Obligatory vs. Elective War (Milchemet Mitzvah/Reshut)
candidates.notes: Distinction between obligatory wars (milchemet mitzvah) where no exemptions apply and elective wars (milchemet reshut) where biblical exemptions for new house, vineyard, and betrothal apply

candidates.name: Reward for a Commandment is a Commandment (Mitzvah Goreret Mitzvah)
candidates.notes: One mitzvah leads to another mitzvah, and one transgression leads to another transgression (Avot 4:2).

candidates.name: Shekhinah Among Torah Learners
candidates.notes: Divine presence rests among those studying Torah, whether ten, five, three, two, or even one (Avot 3:2, 3:6).

candidates.name: Serving God Without Expectation of Reward
candidates.hebrew: עבודה שלא על מנת לקבל פרס
candidates.notes: The ideal of serving God like servants who do not expect reward, but purely out of reverence (Avot 1:3).

candidates.name: Divine Foreknowledge and Human Free Will
candidates.notes: The paradox that everything is foreseen yet freedom of choice is granted; world judged by preponderance of deeds (Avot 3:15).

candidates.name: Reward for Abstaining from Desired Transgression
candidates.hebrew: שכר הפורש מן העבירה שנפשו מחמדת
candidates.notes: Principle derived from Rabbi Shimon bar Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi: one who refrains from robbery or forbidden relations, which the soul desires, receives greater reward than one who refrains from blood, which the soul loathes

candidates.name: Measure for Measure (Midah k'Neged Midah)
candidates.notes: Principle that Divine punishment and reward correspond proportionally to a person's actions, illustrated through sota, Samson, Absalom, Miriam, Joseph, Moses

candidates.name: Repentance and Its Role in Atonement
candidates.notes: The graduated system of atonement: repentance for minor sins, Yom Kippur for severe ones, death for gravest; the invalid who says 'I will sin and repent'

candidates.name: This World as Vestibule to the World to Come
candidates.notes: The metaphor of this world as a vestibule (prozdor) preparing for the banquet hall of the World to Come (Avot 4:16).

candidates.name: Catacomb (Kever) Construction Standards
candidates.notes: Detailed laws on dimensions of burial chambers, niches (kukhin), and courtyards when constructing an underground catacomb (Bava Batra 6:8)

candidates.name: Elijah's Role in Restoring Disputed Lineage
candidates.notes: The tradition that Elijah will come to clarify genealogical disputes — removing those wrongly admitted and admitting those wrongly excluded; debate among Rabbi Joshua, Rabbi Judah, Rabbi Shimon, and the Sages; Eduyot 8:7

candidates.name: Nefesh (Grave Monument)
candidates.notes: The monument built on a grave; dispute whether leftover burial funds should be used to build a nefesh on the grave

candidates.name: Footsteps of the Messiah (Ikveta diMeshicha)
candidates.notes: Signs and characteristics of the pre-Messianic era: moral deterioration, disrespect for elders, erosion of faith and family bonds, impudence

candidates.name: Torah Study for Its Own Sake (Torah Lishmah)
candidates.notes: The ideal of studying Torah intrinsically, not for reward or status; contrasted with using Torah as a spade (Avot 4:5, 6:1).

candidates.name: Torah Combined with Worldly Occupation (Torah im Derech Eretz)
candidates.notes: The value and necessity of combining Torah study with a livelihood; discussed in Avot 2:2.

candidates.name: Who is Wise, Mighty, Rich, Honored (Ben Zoma)
candidates.hebrew: איזהו חכם איזהו גיבור איזהו עשיר איזהו מכובד
candidates.notes: Ben Zoma's redefinition of wisdom, strength, wealth, and honor in ethical and spiritual terms (Avot 4:1). Widely quoted throughout Talmudic literature.

candidates.name: Torah Scholars' Wisdom Increasing with Age
candidates.hebrew: תלמידי חכמים כל זמן שמזקינין דעתן מתיישבת עליהן
candidates.notes: The principle that Torah scholars grow wiser with age, contrasted with unlearned people whose intellect diminishes; from the end of tractate Kinnim.

candidates.name: Ribui Mitzvot l'Zakot — Multiplying Commandments to Confer Merit
candidates.notes: Rabbi Chananya ben Akashya's statement that God multiplied Torah and mitzvot to increase merit for the Jewish people, based on Isaiah 42:21.

candidates.name: Pinchas ben Yair's Ladder of Virtues
candidates.hebrew: סולם של רבי פינחס בן יאיר
candidates.notes: The ascending chain of spiritual virtues from Torah study through diligence, cleanliness, purity, piety, humility, fear of sin, holiness, divine spirit, to resurrection.

candidates.name: Teaching Daughters Torah
candidates.notes: Debate between Ben Azzai (obligation to teach daughters Torah) and Rabbi Eliezer (teaching daughters Torah is tiflut/promiscuity).

candidates.name: Persons of Uncertain or Disqualified Lineage
candidates.notes: Group covering shetuki, asufi, gibeonite, and the ten categories of lineage — persons whose lineage is uncertain, disqualified, or restricted for marriage purposes

candidates.name: Order of Precedence Among Persons
candidates.notes: Halakhic hierarchy governing who takes precedence in rescue, redemption, return of lost objects, and clothing — based on lineage, priestly status, and Torah scholarship

candidates.name: Mourning Rites and Observances
candidates.notes: Group covering specific mourning practices: shiva/shloshim periods, keria, seudat havraah, wailing, eulogy rules, and festival interruption of mourning

candidates.name: Mourner's Exemption from Mitzvot
candidates.notes: One whose deceased is before him is exempt from Shema, Amida, and tefillin; pallbearers' exemptions; Rabban Gamliel bathing after his wife's death as one who is delicate

candidates.name: Women and Minors — Obligations in Mitzvot
candidates.notes: Women, slaves, and minors are exempt from Shema and tefillin but obligated in prayer, mezuza, and Grace after Meals; they do not count for zimmun

candidates.name: Convert's Bikkurim and Declaration
candidates.notes: Convert brings bikkurim but cannot recite the declaration ('which the Lord swore to our fathers'); prayer formulations for converts in synagogue vs. private

candidates.name: Androginus (Hermaphrodite) — Detailed Halakhic Status
candidates.notes: Comprehensive treatment of the androginus: ways it is like a man, like a woman, like both, and like neither — covering tumah, inheritance, mitzvot, testimony, yibbum, nazirite vows

candidates.name: Prohibition of Expounding Arayot Before Three
candidates.notes: The prohibition of publicly expounding the laws of forbidden sexual relations before three or more people; classified with other restricted topics of Torah study.

candidates.name: Deaf-Mute Woman's Marriage and Divorce
candidates.notes: Testimony of Rabbi Nehunia ben Gudgada that a deaf-mute woman given in marriage by her father can be divorced with a get; Eduyot 7:9

candidates.name: Proselyte Who Converted on Erev Pesach — May He Bring Korban Pesach
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (may immerse and eat the Passover sacrifice that evening) and Beit Hillel (compared to one separating from a grave, must wait); Eduyot 5:2

candidates.name: Family of Doubtful Lineage (Issa)
candidates.notes: Status of a family of doubtful lineage (issa) and whether widows from such families may marry kohanim; the authority of courts to investigate such lineage; Eduyot 8:3

candidates.name: Deaf-Mute's Legal Transactions (Gestures and Lip Movements)
candidates.notes: Rabbinic enactment validating transactions by a deaf-mute through gestures or lip movements; Gittin 5:7

candidates.name: Limits on Redeeming Captives
candidates.hebrew: פדיון שבויים — אין פודין יתר על דמיהם
candidates.notes: The enactment that captives should not be redeemed for more than their monetary value, and prohibition on aiding their escape; Gittin 4:6

candidates.name: Get Given or Retracted During Temporary Insanity
candidates.notes: Validity of a get or its retraction made during an episode of temporary insanity (kordeyakos); Gittin 7:1

candidates.name: Minor's Purchase in Rabbinic Law (Takkanat Paotot)
candidates.notes: Rabbinic enactment validating commercial transactions of young children (paotot) in movable property for their benefit; Gittin 5:7

candidates.name: Order of Precedence Among Persons (Kohen, Levi, Yisrael, Mamzer, etc.)
candidates.hebrew: סדר הקדימה — כהן לוי ישראל ממזר גר ועבד
candidates.notes: The halakhic hierarchy for rescue, return of lost objects, clothing, and redemption from captivity: priest before Levite, Levite before Israelite, Israelite before mamzer, mamzer before Gibeonite, Gibeonite before convert, convert before freed slave. Torah scholarship overrides lineage.

candidates.name: Priority in Rescue and Redemption — Man vs. Woman
candidates.hebrew: קדימה בהצלה ופדיון — איש לפני אישה
candidates.notes: Woman precedes man for clothing and release from captivity (due to greater humiliation and risk of rape); man precedes woman for rescue from danger and return of lost objects. Special case when both face degradation in captivity.

candidates.name: Torah Scholarship Overrides Lineage in Precedence
candidates.hebrew: תלמיד חכם קודם לכהן גדול עם הארץ
candidates.notes: A mamzer who is a Torah scholar takes precedence over a High Priest who is ignorant. Torah wisdom surpasses all matters of lineage and priestly status in determining priority.

candidates.name: Multiple Liabilities from a Single Act of Intercourse
candidates.notes: Talmudic analysis of how a single act of forbidden intercourse can incur multiple separate sin offering liabilities when the woman stands in multiple prohibited relationship categories to the man simultaneously

candidates.name: Father's Authority Over Daughter (Reshut HaAv)
candidates.notes: Father's legal rights over minor daughter: betrothal proceeds, earnings, found objects, vow nullification, receiving her get

candidates.name: Priest Forbidden to Remarry His Divorcée
candidates.notes: Practical halakhic consequence that a priest is given extra time before being forced to divorce, since he cannot remarry his ex-wife

candidates.name: Shetuki (Child of Unknown Father)
candidates.notes: Person who knows their mother but not their father; their status and marriage restrictions; distinct from foundling (asufi)

candidates.name: Asufi (Foundling)
candidates.notes: Child found in a public place who knows neither parent; their status and marriage restrictions compared to shetuki and mamzer

candidates.name: Gibeonite (Netinei)
candidates.notes: Descendants of the Gibeonites who converted in Joshua's time; their prohibited status with respect to marriage into the congregation (kahal)

candidates.name: Ten Categories of Lineage (Eser Yuchasin)
candidates.notes: The ten categories of those who ascended from Babylonia with Ezra (priests, Levites, Israelites, halalim, converts, freed slaves, mamzerim, Gibeonites, shetukim, asufim) and their permitted intermarriages

candidates.name: Lineage Investigation for Priestly Marriage
candidates.notes: How many generations back a priest must investigate a prospective bride's maternal and paternal lineage; presumptions based on public office or Temple service

candidates.name: Purification of Mamzer Status
candidates.notes: Rabbi Tarfon's view that mamzerim can be 'purified' over generations by marrying a Canaanite maidservant; dispute with Rabbi Eliezer

candidates.name: Bachelor Prohibited from Teaching Children
candidates.notes: Prohibition on an unmarried man serving as a teacher of young children due to concern of improper conduct; parallel prohibition for women teachers

candidates.name: Status of a Foundling (Tinok haNimtzei)
candidates.notes: Rules for determining the religious/national status of an abandoned child found in a city with mixed Jewish/non-Jewish population, following the majority or other criteria (M. Makhshirin 2:7).

candidates.name: Conspiring Witness Testimony to Disqualify a Priest (Chalal)
candidates.notes: Specific case of conspiring witnesses who testified to render a kohen a chalal; punishment is lashes rather than being rendered a chalal themselves

candidates.name: Funeral Eulogy Rows and Comforting Mourners (Shurot Nichum Aveilim)
candidates.notes: Practice of mourners standing and community passing in rows to comfort them; requires a minyan of ten

candidates.name: Festival Interrupting Mourning Period
candidates.notes: Halakhic principle that a pilgrimage festival (Pesach, Shavuot, Sukkot) interrupts and/or cancels the seven-day or thirty-day mourning period; includes rules about how many days before the festival burial must occur

candidates.name: Shiva and Shloshim (Seven and Thirty Days of Mourning)
candidates.notes: The seven-day and thirty-day mourning periods, their requirements and how they interact with Shabbat and Festivals

candidates.name: Seudat Havraah (First Mourner's Meal)
candidates.notes: The meal provided to mourners after burial by neighbors/community; rules about who provides it, what vessels may be used, and whether it applies on Chol HaMoed

candidates.name: Consolation Row (Shurah) and Mourners' Blessing
candidates.notes: Specific practice of consolers standing in a row at the cemetery to console mourners; and the recitation (or non-recitation) of birkat avelim during Chol HaMoed

candidates.name: Wailing and Lamentation (Yelalah and Kinah)
candidates.notes: Distinction between communal wailing (all together) and antiphonal lamentation (one leads, others respond); rules about when each is permitted including on Chol HaMoed, Rosh Chodesh, Chanukah, and Purim

candidates.name: Eulogy on Chol HaMoed and Other Special Days
candidates.notes: Prohibition on eulogies during Chol HaMoed; related rules about not setting down the bier in public; thirty days before Festival restriction

candidates.name: Rending Garments in Mourning (Keria)
candidates.notes: Practice of rending garments as sign of mourning; rules about when it is suspended such as during Chol HaMoed

candidates.name: Festivals Interrupting or Interacting with Mourning
candidates.notes: Group covering how Shabbat, Yom Tov, and the High Holidays interact with the mourning period — whether they interrupt, count toward, or are superseded by the mourning obligations

candidates.name: Stages of Female Development (Ketana, Na'arah, Bogeret)
candidates.notes: Group covering the halakhic stages of female maturation and their legal consequences regarding vows, earnings, marriage, and obligations

candidates.name: Sexually Underdeveloped Persons (Ailonit and Saris)
candidates.notes: Group covering individuals who fail to develop normal sexual characteristics, their determination by age and physical signs, and their halakhic status in marriage and levirate law

candidates.name: Prohibitions on Entering the Congregation (Issur Kahal)
candidates.notes: Group covering the various categories of persons prohibited from marrying into the congregation of Israel, including Ammonites, Moabites, Gibeonites, mamzerim, and men with genital injuries

candidates.name: Laws Specific to the Convert's Legal Situation
candidates.notes: Group covering the unique legal situations that arise from the convert's change of status, including agricultural obligations, inheritance, debts, levirate bonds, and Passover observance

candidates.name: Gathering Bones of the Deceased (Likkut Atzamot)
candidates.notes: Ancient practice of secondary burial — collecting bones from temporary grave for reburial in ancestral tomb; dispute whether permitted on Chol HaMoed due to joy vs. mourning

candidates.name: Shavuot's Status Regarding Mourning
candidates.notes: Dispute whether Shavuot (one-day festival) acts like Shabbat (counts but doesn't interrupt) or like other pilgrimage festivals (interrupts) for purposes of mourning period calculation

candidates.name: Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur's Status Regarding Mourning
candidates.hebrew: ראש השנה ויום כיפור לענין אבלות
candidates.notes: Dispute (Rabban Gamliel vs. Rabbis) whether Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur interrupt the mourning period like pilgrimage festivals or only count like Shabbat

candidates.name: Halakhic Status of the Fetus/Embryo (Ubar)
candidates.notes: Determination of whether a discharged mass is a halakhically significant fetus; formation of the male fetus on the 41st day and female on the 81st day; conditions under which a discharge triggers yoledet impurity obligations

candidates.name: Signs of Halakhic Adulthood (Simanim)
candidates.notes: Two pubic hairs as the primary sign of halakhic adulthood; rules about their minimum length; disputes about the age at which an ailonit or saris is determined (18 or 20 years old)

candidates.name: Grown Woman (Bogeret)
candidates.notes: The third stage of female development (bogeret/grown womanhood) after minor and na'arah; signs indicating its onset (breast development); halakhic consequences including loss of father's authority over her vows and earnings

candidates.name: Sexually Underdeveloped Woman (Ailonit)
candidates.notes: A woman who has not developed signs of puberty by age 18 or 20; her halakhic status as exempt from levirate marriage obligations; distinction from normal women in marriage law

candidates.name: Sexually Underdeveloped Man (Saris)
candidates.notes: A man who has not developed signs of puberty by age 18 or 20; exempt from levirate marriage obligations; determination by age and absence of physical signs

candidates.name: Father's Rights Over Na'arah's Earnings and Finds
candidates.notes: Father's entitlement to found objects, earnings, and power to annul vows of a minor daughter and a na'arah; these rights cease when she becomes a bogeret

candidates.name: Convert's Obligation for Agricultural Gifts
candidates.notes: A non-Jew who converts after harvesting his field is exempt from leket, shikchah, and peah; dispute regarding shikchah since liability arises at binding time

candidates.name: Acute Mourner Eating Sacrificial Food (Avel b'Kodashim)
candidates.notes: The rule that an acute mourner (onen) is prohibited from eating sacrificial food except that he immerses and eats the Paschal lamb on Passover night; distinction from regular mourning rules

candidates.name: Convert Who Converted on Passover Eve
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel regarding whether a convert on Passover eve may immediately eat the Paschal lamb or must wait seven days like one impure from a corpse

candidates.name: Training Minors in Shabbat Observance (Chinuch)
candidates.notes: The obligation of parents to prevent children from desecrating Shabbat even though minors are not obligated, as derived from Mishnah Shabbat chapter 16

candidates.name: Flutes at a Funeral on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Prohibition on a Jew using flutes brought by a gentile on Shabbat for a funeral eulogy unless they were brought from within the techum

candidates.name: Debts Owed to a Convert's Heirs
candidates.notes: When a convert dies leaving sons who converted with him, the legal obligation to repay debts owed to the convert and the moral dimension of voluntary repayment

candidates.name: Children's Obligation in Sukkah
candidates.notes: The rabbinic obligation to train children in the mitzva of sukkah once they no longer need their mother, and the incident of Shammai the Elder roofing for a newborn

candidates.name: Communal Mourning Customs When Fasts Are Unanswered
candidates.notes: When all fasts have been exhausted without rain, the community adopts mourning-like practices: reducing business, building, planting, betrothals, marriages, and greetings

candidates.name: Ammonite and Moabite Converts Entering the Congregation
candidates.notes: The prohibition against Ammonites and Moabites entering the congregation, and the ruling that since Sennacherib mixed the nations this no longer applies

candidates.name: Aylonit (Sexually Underdeveloped Woman)
candidates.notes: A woman incapable of bearing children due to developmental conditions; her effect on marriage, levirate marriage, teruma, and priestly marriage

candidates.name: Petzua Dakka and Kerut Shofkha (Genital Injuries Prohibiting Marriage)
candidates.notes: Men with crushed testicles or severed penis who are prohibited from marrying women born Jewish; their status regarding teruma and marriage

candidates.name: Entering the Congregation (Issur Kahal)
candidates.notes: Prohibition of Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, Edomites, mamzerim, Gibeonites, petzua dakka, and kerut shofkha from marrying into the congregation of Israel

candidates.name: Gibeonites (Netinin)
candidates.notes: Gibeonites who converted in Joshua's time; their prohibition from entering the congregation and marrying Jews of unflawed lineage, eternally

candidates.name: Woman Who Remarried Based on False Testimony
candidates.hebrew: אִשָּׁה שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד שֶׁבַּעְלָהּ מֵת
candidates.notes: Laws governing a woman who remarried based on testimony that her husband died, and her husband later returned; she must leave both husbands, offspring is mamzer, various penalties

candidates.name: Ḥalal and Ḥalala (Disqualified Priestly Lineage)
candidates.notes: Status of children born of forbidden priestly unions; disqualification from priestly privileges and teruma; how a woman becomes a ḥalala through intercourse with a disqualified priest

candidates.name: Mamzer Offspring from Forbidden Relations
candidates.notes: Definition of mamzer: dispute between Rabbi Akiva, Shimon HaTimni, Rabbi Yehoshua — whether it arises from any prohibition, karet-level, or capital-level forbidden relations

candidates.name: Mi'un (Refusal of a Minor Girl to Continue Her Marriage)
candidates.notes: Rabbinic institution allowing a minor girl married by her mother or brothers to refuse her husband; effect on levirate marriage, disqualification from priesthood, repeat refusals; Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel dispute

candidates.name: Mixed Offspring (Offspring of Uncertain Patrilineage)
candidates.notes: Cases where children's lineage is uncertain due to mixing; rules for chalitzah and levirate marriage; status for teruma, Temple service, inheritance, and priestly purity

candidates.name: Converts: No Levirate Bond Between Brothers
candidates.notes: Sons who converted with their mother are not considered brothers for purposes of levirate marriage or chalitzah; conversion is like rebirth

candidates.name: Fulfillment and Details of the Mitzva of Procreation
candidates.notes: Number of children required; Beit Shammai vs. Beit Hillel; ten-year waiting period before divorcing an infertile wife; whether women are obligated

candidates.name: High Priest's Marriage Restrictions
candidates.notes: High Priest may not marry a widow, divorcée, ḥalutza, or grown woman (bogeret); may only marry a virgin; betrothal before appointment; High Priest must perform chalitzah not yibbum

candidates.name: Prohibition of Ammonite and Moabite Converts
candidates.notes: Ammonite and Moabite males are prohibited from marrying into the Jewish people eternally; their females are permitted immediately; distinction from Egyptian and Edomite converts

candidates.name: Presumption Based on Nursing Animal
candidates.notes: The presumption that a nursing animal has previously given birth to the animal it is nursing, used to determine whether an animal purchased from a gentile has firstborn-exempt status

candidates.name: Peh She'asar Hu Peh She'hitir (The Mouth That Forbade Is the Mouth That Permitted)
candidates.notes: Principle that when the same person both creates a prohibition and permits it, we rely on his word; applied in context of seller declaring produce tithed after already stating its origin

candidates.name: The Mouth That Prohibited is the Mouth That Permitted (Peh sheAsar hu Peh sheHitir)
candidates.notes: Credibility principle: one who admits a fact that creates a prohibition is believed when claiming it no longer applies; used extensively in Ketubot

candidates.name: Following the Majority of a City's Population (Rov in Mixed Communities)
candidates.notes: Application of the principle of following the majority in determining status of found objects, abandoned children, bread, meat, and other items in cities with mixed Jewish/non-Jewish populations (M. Makhshirin 2:5-2:10).

candidates.name: Doubtful Status in Chadash, Orlah, and Kilayim — Geographical Distinctions
candidates.hebrew: סָפֵק עָרְלָה, כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, חָדָשׁ — בְּמָקוֹמוֹת שׁוֹנִים
candidates.notes: The last mishnah in Orlah distinguishes the rabbinic vs. Torah status and handling of doubtful orlah, kilayim, and chadash in Israel, Syria, and abroad

candidates.name: Prohibition Cannot Take Effect Where One Already Exists — Oaths
candidates.notes: Applied to oaths: repeated oaths on same act generate only one liability; also applied to oath over already-prohibited foods — Shevuot 3:4, 3:7

candidates.name: Tzedakah Administration and Distribution
candidates.notes: Practical rules governing the collection, distribution, eligibility, and administration of charitable funds and agricultural gifts for the poor

candidates.name: Dispute for the Sake of Heaven (Machloket leShem Shamayim)
candidates.notes: Distinction between disputes conducted for the sake of heaven (Hillel and Shammai) vs. those not (Korach); Avot 5:17.

candidates.name: Causing the Multitudes to Sin or to be Righteous
candidates.hebrew: מחטיא את הרבים / מזכה את הרבים
candidates.notes: One who causes the public to sin cannot repent; one who causes the public to be righteous is credited with their righteousness (Avot 5:18).

candidates.name: Do Not Separate from the Community
candidates.notes: The principle that one should not separate oneself from the communal life (Avot 2:4).

candidates.name: Quoting a Teaching in the Name of Its Author
candidates.notes: The obligation to cite one's source when transmitting a teaching; doing so brings redemption to the world (Avot 6:6).

candidates.name: Honest Measuring and Weighing Practices
candidates.notes: Practical obligations of sellers: cleaning measuring vessels, dripping three extra drops, tilting scales for buyer, following regional customs for heaping or leveling (Bava Batra ch. 5)

candidates.name: Requesting Forgiveness After Paying Damages
candidates.notes: Even after paying all monetary compensation, an assailant must request forgiveness from the victim; without forgiveness the transgression is not fully atoned

candidates.name: Enactments for Ways of Peace (Darkhei Shalom)
candidates.notes: Specific rabbinic enactments enacted to preserve peace — Torah reading order, irrigation precedence, lost items of incompetents, poor gentiles and pe'ah; Gittin 5:8-9

candidates.name: Equality of Father and Mother in Honor Obligation
candidates.notes: Rabbi Shimon's exposition that Torah alternates order of father/mother and mother/father to show equality, yet concludes the father's honor takes precedence because both son and mother are obligated to honor the father; teacher's honor vis-à-vis father

candidates.name: Choice of Vocation and Trade
candidates.notes: Rabbinic guidance on which trades to teach one's son; preference for Torah study over worldly vocation; ethical evaluation of various professions

candidates.name: Minimum Amounts of Charity Distribution
candidates.notes: Minimum quantities to be given to the poor from the threshing floor: wheat, barley, spelt, dried figs, wine, oil; minimum for wandering poor (loaf, overnight needs, Shabbat meals)

candidates.name: Tamchui and Kuppah (Charity Dish and Communal Fund)
candidates.notes: Distinction between the tamchui (charity plate for daily food) and kuppah (weekly communal fund); eligibility thresholds (two meals vs. fourteen meals vs. 200 zuz); collection by two, distribution by three

candidates.name: Eligibility for Charity and Agricultural Gifts
candidates.notes: Thresholds for eligibility to take leket/shikchah/peah/maaser ani vs. communal charity; 200 zuz threshold, assets mortgaged to creditor or ketubah, exempt from selling house or tools

candidates.name: Leftover Charity and Redemption Funds
candidates.notes: Rules governing surplus funds collected for charity, captive redemption, burial of the dead, and specific individuals — how excess is allocated

candidates.name: Appearance Above Suspicion in Temple Service
candidates.hebrew: יציאת ידי שמים ויציאת ידי הבריות
candidates.notes: The requirement that Temple officials appear innocent before both God and man; the rules against wearing cuffed garments, sandals, etc. when collecting from the treasury chamber

candidates.name: Hidden/Sequestered Ark
candidates.notes: The tradition that the Ark was hidden under the wood depository in the Temple; the incident of the priest who discovered a different flagstone and died

candidates.name: Pharisee-Sadducee Halakhic Disputes
candidates.notes: Debates between Pharisees and Sadducees on specific halakhic matters: purity of liquids, liability for slaves' damages, defilement of holy scriptures

candidates.name: Foods and Produce from Gentiles
candidates.notes: Grouping for detailed laws of various foods produced or handled by gentiles, beyond wine

candidates.name: Detailed Laws of Shechitah
candidates.notes: Grouping for detailed halakhic aspects of ritual slaughter: validity, simanim, defects, and special cases

candidates.name: Detailed Laws of Yayin Nesech and Stam Yeinam
candidates.hebrew: פרטי דיני יין נסך וסתם יינם
candidates.notes: Grouping for detailed halakhot governing forbidden gentile wine in its various forms

candidates.name: Wine Used for Libation — Detailed Laws (Yayin Nesech)
candidates.notes: Detailed halakhot of wine used for idolatrous libations: touch by gentile, mixture, safeguarding, supervision, and nullification in mixture

candidates.name: Gentile Wine — Detailed Laws (Stam Yeinam)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of ordinary gentile wine: supervision, temporary absence, placement in public domain, and wage from wine work

candidates.name: Winepress Owned or Used by Gentile
candidates.notes: Laws of purchasing or using a winepress in which a gentile has trodden, including when the juice acquires the status of forbidden wine

candidates.name: Wine Left Unattended with Gentile
candidates.notes: Rules for how long a Jew may be absent from wine in the presence of a gentile before it becomes forbidden as wine used for libation

candidates.name: Wages from Work Involving Idolatrous Wine or Items
candidates.notes: Whether wages earned by a Jew for transporting or handling wine used for libation are forbidden

candidates.name: Wine Cistern Contaminated by Libation Wine
candidates.notes: Wine used for libation that fell into a cistern renders all wine forbidden; dispute about selling the whole and deducting the value of the forbidden portion

candidates.name: Bishul Akum — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Boiled and pickled vegetables prepared by gentiles and their prohibited status

candidates.name: Reason for Prohibition of Gentile Cheese
candidates.notes: Talmudic discussion of the reasons behind the prohibition of gentile cheese, including curdling with carcass stomach or stomach of calf used for idol worship

candidates.name: Milk Milked by Gentile — Supervision Requirement
candidates.notes: Requirement for Jewish supervision when a gentile milks an animal, and status of milk without such supervision

candidates.name: Fish Brine and Certain Foods from Gentiles
candidates.notes: Laws of specific foods from gentiles such as fish brine, cheese of Beit Unyaki, and their level of prohibition

candidates.name: Mixtures Involving Wine Used for Libation
candidates.notes: Rules for how wine used for libation renders mixtures forbidden — same species forbidden with any amount; different species only if flavor is imparted

candidates.name: Mixtures Involving Idolatrous Items
candidates.notes: List of forbidden items that in any amount render their mixture forbidden, including idols, condemned ox, broken-necked heifer, and others

candidates.name: Items That Cannot Be Nullified (Lo Batel)
candidates.notes: Specific list of items such as idols, yayin nesech, and others that render any mixture forbidden regardless of proportion

candidates.name: Kashering Utensils Purchased from Gentiles
candidates.notes: Process of immersion, purging with boiling water, or heating until white-hot for utensils purchased from gentiles, based on how they were used

candidates.name: Covering the Blood on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: The halakhot of covering blood of slaughtered animals on Yom Tov; dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel about whether earth must be pre-prepared

candidates.name: Koy (Animal of Uncertain Classification)
candidates.notes: The koy is an animal of uncertain status — neither clearly domesticated (behemah) nor wild (hayyah); its laws regarding blood covering, chelev, firstborn, kilayim, and shechitah

candidates.name: Validity of Slaughter (Shechitat Chulin)
candidates.notes: Who may slaughter, conditions under which slaughter is valid, including slaughter by deaf-mutes, minors, blind persons, on Shabbat, at night, etc.

candidates.name: Simanim (Organs Cut in Slaughter)
candidates.notes: The windpipe and gullet as the required organs to be cut in valid slaughter; rules about majority of each siman

candidates.name: Shehiyah, Derash, Chalada, Hagramah, Ikkur (Five Defects of Slaughter)
candidates.notes: The five defects that invalidate slaughter: pausing, pressing, burrowing under tissue, slanting, tearing

candidates.name: Slaughter with Idolatrous Intent
candidates.notes: Slaughter performed for the sake of idols, mountains, seas, etc. renders the animal forbidden; rules about joint slaughter with one person having forbidden intent

candidates.name: Slaughter Performed by a Gentile
candidates.notes: Gentile slaughter renders animal a neveilah; concern about idolatrous intent even when Jew intended non-sacred use

candidates.name: Tereifot — Specific Conditions (Animal)
candidates.notes: Enumerated list of eighteen (or more) specific conditions making an animal a tereifa, including perforated organs, broken bones, clawing by predator, etc.

candidates.name: Tereifot — Specific Conditions (Bird)
candidates.notes: Enumerated list of conditions making a bird a tereifa, including weasel strike on head, perforated gizzard, trampling, etc.

candidates.name: Signs of Kosher Birds
candidates.notes: Rabbinic-enumerated signs for identifying kosher birds: extra digit, crop, peelable gizzard membrane; predatory behavior as disqualifier

candidates.name: Signs of Kosher Fish (Fins and Scales)
candidates.notes: Fin and scale requirements for kosher fish; debate about minimum number of scales

candidates.name: Signs of Kosher Grasshoppers
candidates.notes: Four legs, four wings, two jumping legs, wings covering majority of body; species name requirement

candidates.name: Oto v'et B'no — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Detailed application of prohibition against slaughtering mother and offspring same day: combinations of sacred/non-sacred, inside/outside Temple; obligation to inform buyer; four critical days of year

candidates.name: Kisuy HaDam — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of covering blood: which animals require it, valid and invalid covering materials, blood mixtures, the koy, who is obligated

candidates.name: Gid HaNasheh — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Scope of prohibition (right/left thigh, fetus, non-kosher animals per R. Yehuda), how to remove it, minimum measure for lashes, cooking with meat

candidates.name: Shiluach HaKen — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Detailed rules: which birds, domesticated vs. wild, hovering vs. resting, unfertilized eggs, fledglings able to fly, repeated return of mother, taking mother instead of sending

candidates.name: Koy (Animal of Uncertain Status)
candidates.notes: The koy is an animal of uncertain classification (domesticated or undomesticated); affects laws of kisuy hadam, firstborn, fat prohibition, and other halakhot

candidates.name: Eiver Min HaChai from a Fetus
candidates.notes: Whether a limb severed from a fetus in the womb has the status of eiver min hachai; relationship to slaughter of mother animal

candidates.name: Comparative Stringencies of Chelev and Blood Prohibitions
candidates.hebrew: חומרות חלב ודם זה לעומת זה
candidates.notes: Mishnah 8:6 lists unique stringencies: chelev of offerings is subject to meilah, piggul, notar, tumah rules; blood prohibition applies to non-kosher animals and birds

candidates.name: Basar b'Chalav — Detailed Laws (Cooking, Eating, Benefit)
candidates.notes: Whether bird meat may be cooked or placed on table with cheese; udder, heart; which meats are subject to the Torah prohibition vs. rabbinic; milk of non-kosher animal; taste imparted by drop of milk

candidates.name: Darchei HaEmori (Forbidden Superstitious Practices)
candidates.notes: Prohibition against imitating Amorite superstitious practices, such as burying placenta at crossroads or hanging it on a tree to prevent miscarriage

candidates.name: Detailed Laws of Mixtures (Taaruvot)
candidates.notes: Subcategories of mixture laws including nullification ratios, flavor imparting, fermentation, seasoning, and items sold by count

candidates.name: Slaughter of an Animal in Mortal Danger
candidates.notes: Signs required to validate slaughter of a dying animal (convulsion of limbs, blood spurting); disputes among Tannaim

candidates.name: Nefesh HaYafah (Hardy Soul) — Concept in Kashrut
candidates.notes: Concept that items technically permitted but repulsive to most people may be eaten only by one with a hardy, undiscerning soul; applied to placenta

candidates.name: Day Follows Night in Oto v'et B'no
candidates.notes: The 'one day' of the prohibition follows the night; one may slaughter by day and the offspring at night but not slaughter at night and offspring next day; derived via gezerah shavah with Creation

candidates.name: Temed (Beverage from Grape Residue) — Halakhic Status
candidates.notes: Temed before fermentation is not wine and cannot be purchased with maaser sheni money; after fermentation it is wine; effect on mikvah validity

candidates.name: Mixtures Involving Tevel
candidates.notes: Rules for tevel mixed with common produce, tithed produce, or first tithe; calculations for how much must be separated to correct the mixture

candidates.name: Purity of the Ayal Locust
candidates.notes: Testimony of Rabbi Yose ben Yoezer (Yose the Permitter) that the ayal locust is pure/permitted; Eduyot 8:4

candidates.name: Placing Fowl on a Table with Cheese
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (fowl may be placed on the same table as cheese but not eaten together) and Beit Hillel (may neither be placed nor eaten together); Eduyot 5:2

candidates.name: Measure and Time for Forbidden Eating (Shiur Achilah)
candidates.notes: The time span within which consumption of an olive-bulk creates liability; dispute between Rabbi Meir (time to eat toasted grain) and Rabbis (time to eat a half-loaf); also the quarter-log of wine for a priest entering the Temple

candidates.name: Blood Prohibition — Detailed Categories
candidates.notes: Detailed enumeration of which blood is forbidden (slaughter blood, blood of stabbing, blood that departs with the soul) vs. which is permitted (spleen, heart, eggs, grasshoppers, tamtzit exudate blood); dispute of Rabbi Yehuda on exudate blood

candidates.name: Chadash — Prohibition and Permitting by the Omer
candidates.hebrew: איסור חדש והיתרו על ידי העומר
candidates.notes: The omer permits the new grain crop; timing of permission for those near vs. far from Jerusalem; Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai's post-Temple enactment; five grain species and their joining.

candidates.name: Five Grain Species (Chamesh Minei Dagan)
candidates.notes: Wheat, barley, spelt, oats, and rye — the five species obligated in challah, subject to chadash prohibition, and joining together for the measure.

candidates.name: Bitul b'Matayim (Nullification in Two Hundred and One)
candidates.notes: Orlah and kilayim of the vineyard are nullified in a mixture of 201 parts, unlike terumah which is 101; detailed rules for this ratio

candidates.name: Flavor Imparted by Forbidden Substance (Noten Ta'am)
candidates.notes: When a forbidden substance imparts flavor to a mixture it prohibits the whole; distinction between same-species (follows flavor imparting) and different species (follows nullification ratio)

candidates.name: Leaven That Causes Fermentation in Mixtures
candidates.notes: Rules for when orlah or kilayim leaven ferments dough: prohibition depends on whether there is sufficient leaven to ferment; cases where hullin and terumah leaven combine

candidates.name: Seasoning That Flavors a Dish (Me'abeid/Metzamtzem)
candidates.notes: When forbidden seasonings (orlah, terumah, kilayim) season a dish, the dish may be prohibited; rules differ by species type and by whether there is sufficient amount to season

candidates.name: Items Sold by Count That Cannot Be Nullified
candidates.notes: Certain items sold individually (e.g., soft-shelled nuts, pomegranates, loaves) are not nullified even in 201; Rabbi Meir vs. Sages dispute; list of six (or seven) such items

candidates.name: Asherah Tree — Prohibition of Use
candidates.notes: Leaves, sprouts, and sap from an Asherah (idolatrous tree) are forbidden for benefit; contrasted with orlah in what they prohibit

candidates.name: New Grain Prohibition Throughout Day of Omer (Zecher laMikdash)
candidates.hebrew: איסור חדש כל יום הנף זכר למקדש
candidates.notes: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai's institution extending the prohibition on new grain throughout the entire sixteenth of Nisan as a remembrance of the Temple

candidates.name: Offspring of a Tereifa Animal and Altar Eligibility
candidates.notes: Dispute whether offspring of a tereifa may be sacrificed on the altar (R. Eliezer prohibits, Rabbis permit). Also R. Chanina: animal that suckled from a tereifa is disqualified.

candidates.name: Laws of Get Writing (Details)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws governing the physical writing of a get, valid materials, who may write, signatures, dating, and form

candidates.name: Laws of Get Delivery and Transfer
candidates.notes: Laws governing the delivery of a get to the wife, including agent declarations, overseas gets, and transfer of possession

candidates.name: Ketubah Stipulations and Collection
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of court-mandated and voluntary ketubah stipulations, and procedures for collection by widow or divorcée

candidates.name: Widow's Rights from Estate
candidates.notes: A widow's rights to sustenance, residence, and other benefits from her late husband's estate

candidates.name: Seclusion with Gentiles (Yichud im Nochri)
candidates.notes: Prohibition on a Jewish woman secluding herself with gentile men due to fear of sexual assault, and any person with gentiles due to fear of bloodshed

candidates.name: Pre-Wedding Gifts (Sivlonot)
candidates.notes: Gifts sent by groom to bride's father's house after betrothal and their recoverability if the marriage is not completed; depends on whether groom ate a groom's feast (Bava Batra 9:5)

candidates.name: Minimum Value for Valid Kiddushin (Perutah vs. Denar)
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (a denar or its value) and Beit Hillel (a perutah or its value) as the minimum for valid betrothal; Eduyot 4:7

candidates.name: Old Get (Get Yashan) — Seclusion After Writing
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel regarding whether a get written before the husband secluded himself with his wife again is still valid; Eduyot 4:7

candidates.name: Rival Wives (Tzarot) and Yibbum Eligibility
candidates.notes: Major dispute between Beit Shammai (permits rival wives to the surviving brothers for yibbum) and Beit Hillel (forbids); consequences for priestly fitness after chalitzah or yibbum; Eduyot 4:8

candidates.name: Validity of Get/Document — Depends on Signatories
candidates.hebrew: גט שכתבה היא ושובר שכתבו הוא — כשר
candidates.notes: Testimony that a document's legal validity depends only on its signatories, not on who physically wrote it; a wife may write her own get and a husband may write his own receipt; Eduyot 2:3

candidates.name: Get Lishmah (Bill of Divorce Written for Specific Woman)
candidates.notes: Requirement that a get be written specifically for the woman being divorced; core topic of tractate Gittin chapters 2-3

candidates.name: Agent's Declaration for Get (Written and Signed in My Presence)
candidates.hebrew: הבאת גט ממדינת הים — בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם
candidates.notes: Requirement that an agent bringing a get from overseas declare it was written and signed in his presence; major topic of Gittin chapter 1

candidates.name: Get from Overseas to Eretz Yisrael
candidates.notes: Special laws governing a get brought from outside Eretz Yisrael, including agent declaration requirements and borders of Eretz Yisrael for this purpose

candidates.name: Valid Materials for Writing a Get
candidates.notes: What substances and surfaces are valid for writing a get, including ink types, unusual surfaces like olive leaves or animal horns; Gittin chapter 2

candidates.name: Improperly Dated Get
candidates.notes: Laws concerning a get with an incorrect or anachronistic date (e.g., dated by an illegitimate kingdom, or written by day and signed at night)

candidates.name: Cancellation/Revocation of a Get (Bitul Get)
candidates.notes: Laws governing a husband's ability to cancel or revoke a get before it reaches his wife; Rabban Gamliel's ordinance against secret revocation; Gittin chapters 4 and 1

candidates.name: Conditional Get (Get al Tenai — detailed laws)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of conditional divorce — conditions related to return from travel, service, nursing, 'from today if I die'; Gittin chapters 6-8

candidates.name: Coerced Get — Validity and Limits
candidates.notes: When a get given under compulsion is valid vs. invalid; difference between Jewish court compulsion and gentile compulsion; Gittin 9:8

candidates.name: Transfer of Get to Wife's Possession
candidates.notes: Laws of when a get enters the wife's legal possession — throwing, airspace, courtyard, basket, being asleep; Gittin chapter 8

candidates.name: Folded Get (Get Mekushar) and Bare Get (Get Pashut/Kal)
candidates.notes: Laws of the folded-tied get vs. plain get, and the 'bare' get with insufficient witnesses on its folds; Gittin 8:10

candidates.name: Partial Divorce (Get with Exceptions)
candidates.notes: Laws of a get given with conditions excluding certain men; whether such a get is valid; Gittin chapter 9

candidates.name: Prohibition on Remarrying Divorced Wife
candidates.notes: Laws prohibiting a man from remarrying his divorced wife in certain circumstances — after she remarried, or when he divorced her due to bad reputation or specific vows; Gittin 4:7

candidates.name: Rumor of Betrothal or Divorce (Kol)
candidates.notes: When a circulating rumor of betrothal or divorce is sufficient to establish legal status, and what constitutes a valid explanation negating the rumor; Gittin 9:9

candidates.name: Grounds for Divorce (Devar Ervah vs. Any Reason)
candidates.hebrew: טעמי הגירושין — ערות דבר לעומת כל דבר
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (adultery only), Beit Hillel (any grounds), and Rabbi Akiva (found a prettier woman) as to grounds required for valid divorce; Gittin 9:10

candidates.name: Witness Qualifications for Get
candidates.notes: Who may sign as a witness on a get, including women who are enemies, Samaritans, gentile court documents, Hebrew vs. Greek signatures; Gittin 1:5, 2:5, 9:6-8

candidates.name: Who May Write a Get
candidates.notes: Anyone may write a get — deaf-mute, minor, woman, even the husband or wife themselves; what matters is the signatures of witnesses; Gittin 2:5

candidates.name: Husband's Verbal Instruction to Write and Give Get
candidates.notes: Requirements that the husband personally instruct the scribe and witnesses; cases of ambiguous instruction, deathbed instruction, and instruction through a third party; Gittin 6:5-7, 7:2

candidates.name: Get from a Mute Husband
candidates.notes: Procedure for examining a mute husband to determine valid consent for giving a get via nod of head; Gittin 7:1

candidates.name: Divorce of an Ailonit (Sexually Underdeveloped Woman)
candidates.notes: Whether a husband who divorced his wife claiming she is an ailonit may remarry her; and implications for the validity of the marriage; Gittin 4:8, 8:6-7

candidates.name: Divorced Wife Who Spent Night at Inn with Ex-Husband
candidates.notes: Beit Shammai vs. Beit Hillel dispute about whether seclusion at an inn after divorce requires a new get; Gittin 8:9

candidates.name: Virginity Claim (Taanat Betulim)
candidates.notes: Husband's claim that bride was not a virgin; procedures, burden of proof, credibility of parties

candidates.name: Hinnuma (Bridal Veil/Wedding Customs as Evidence)
candidates.notes: Use of bridal veil and uncovered hair as evidence of virgin status at time of marriage

candidates.name: Ketubah Stipulations (Tena'ei Ketubah)
candidates.notes: Court-mandated and voluntary stipulations included in or implied by the ketubah, including redemption from captivity, medical care, daughters' sustenance, widow's residence

candidates.name: Widow's Sustenance from Estate (Mezonot Almanah)
candidates.notes: A widow's right to be sustained from her late husband's estate until she remarries or collects her ketubah

candidates.name: Widow's Right of Residence (Dirat Almanah)
candidates.notes: A widow's right to continue residing in her late husband's house; differences between Jerusalem, Galilee, and Judea customs

candidates.name: Daughters' Sustenance Stipulation (Mezonot Banot)
candidates.notes: Court stipulation that daughters are sustained from the father's estate after his death until married

candidates.name: Sons Inheriting Mother's Ketubah (Ketubot Benin Dichrin)
candidates.notes: Stipulation that male children of a wife inherit her ketubah amount in addition to their share with other brothers

candidates.name: Oath Required for Ketubah Collection (Shevu'at Ketubah)
candidates.notes: Circumstances requiring a woman to take an oath before collecting her ketubah, including partial admission, single witness, collection from orphans or liened property

candidates.name: Widow's Collection of Ketubah (Gviyat Ketubah)
candidates.notes: Procedures and time limits for a widow or divorcée to collect her ketubah, including selling husband's property outside court

candidates.name: Detailed Modes of Betrothal
candidates.notes: Detailed rules for each of the three modes of betrothal and their edge cases

candidates.name: Validity and Defects of Betrothal
candidates.notes: Cases where betrothal may be invalid due to conditions, misrepresentation, forbidden items, or unusual circumstances

candidates.name: Ketubah Precedence Among Multiple Wives
candidates.notes: Order of collection when a man had multiple wives with competing ketubah claims against the estate

candidates.name: Ailonit (Sexually Underdeveloped Woman)
candidates.notes: Halakhic status and marriage rights of an ailonit; whether she is entitled to a ketubah

candidates.name: Husband Who Rebels Against Wife (Mored)
candidates.notes: Incremental increase in ketubah obligation when husband withholds conjugal rights or refuses to support wife

candidates.name: Husband's Vow Restricting Wife
candidates.notes: Cases where husband vows to restrict wife from food, adornment, visiting family, or attending social gatherings, requiring divorce with ketubah payment

candidates.name: Blemishes Discovered After Marriage (Mumim b'Nisuin)
candidates.notes: Physical defects discovered after betrothal or marriage; who bears burden of proof and grounds for divorce without ketubah payment

candidates.name: Wife's Property Rights During Marriage (Nichsei Melog and Tzon Barzel)
candidates.notes: Distinctions between usufruct property (melog) and guaranteed-value property (tzon barzel); husband's rights to produce vs. wife's principal

candidates.name: Wife's Work Obligations to Husband
candidates.notes: Fixed list of household tasks a wife must perform; how the number of maidservants she brings reduces her obligations

candidates.name: Conjugal Frequency Obligation (Onah)
candidates.notes: Detailed schedule of conjugal obligations according to husband's occupation (men of leisure, laborers, donkey drivers, camel drivers, sailors)

candidates.name: Dowry Assessment and Valuation
candidates.notes: Rules for how goods and money of a dowry are assessed in the ketubah; the one-fifth inflation of goods valuation

candidates.name: Obligation to Sustain Stepdaughter
candidates.notes: A husband who stipulates to sustain his wife's daughter from a prior relationship; obligations persist after divorce

candidates.name: Captive Woman's Purity (Ishto Shevuyah)
candidates.notes: Presumption of violation for women captured by enemy forces; husband obligated to redeem wife; priest's wife who was captured

candidates.name: Kohen's Daughter Ketubah (Four Hundred Zuz)
candidates.notes: Custom of priestly courts to grant four hundred dinars ketubah for a virgin daughter of a priest

candidates.name: Relocating a Wife (Havasat Ishah)
candidates.notes: Limits on husband's right to compel wife to move between towns or lands; three geographic regions of Israel

candidates.name: Compelling Aliyah to Eretz Yisrael in Marriage
candidates.notes: Either spouse may compel the other to immigrate to Eretz Yisrael or move to Jerusalem; refusal as grounds for divorce

candidates.name: Rape Fine (Kenas Oness)
candidates.notes: Fine paid to father of raped young woman; who qualifies, who is exempt; distinction from seduction; rapist must marry victim

candidates.name: Seduction Fine (Kenas Mefateh)
candidates.notes: Fine paid to father for seduction of a young woman; three vs. four payments compared to rape; seducer may release the woman

candidates.name: False Defamation Fine (Motzi Shem Ra — Ketubah Context)
candidates.notes: Husband falsely claims wife was not a virgin; 100 sela fine and prohibition from divorcing her; does not apply to converts

candidates.name: Husband Administering Oath to Wife
candidates.notes: Husband's right to administer oaths regarding wife's management of household property; ability to waive this right in ketubah

candidates.name: Husband Who Went Overseas (Ba'al sheHalakh leMedinah haYam)
candidates.notes: Wife's entitlement to sustenance when husband is overseas; oath requirements upon his return; third party who sustained the wife

candidates.name: Ketubah Currency and Geographic Variation
candidates.notes: Which currency standard applies when husband and wife married and divorced in different countries or regions

candidates.name: Mi'un (Refusal by Minor Girl)
candidates.notes: Minor orphan girl's right to refuse marriage arranged by mother or brothers upon reaching majority; no ketubah entitlement upon refusal

candidates.name: Evidence of Virginity at Wedding (Edut al Betulah)
candidates.notes: Forms of testimony and evidence establishing that a woman was married as a virgin, including witnesses to hinnuma and distribution of roasted grain

candidates.name: Dowry for Orphan Girl from Charity
candidates.notes: Charity administrators' obligation to provide at least fifty dinars dowry for an orphan girl they marry off

candidates.name: Widow's Sale of Estate Property for Sustenance
candidates.notes: Rules governing a widow's right to sell her late husband's property to fund her sustenance; whether in court or outside court; limits on overselling

candidates.name: Yevama's Property Rights Pending Levirate Marriage
candidates.notes: Rights of a widow waiting for her yavam regarding property she inherits; how her usufruct property is treated before and after yibbum

candidates.name: Modes of Betrothal (Kinyanei Kiddushin)
candidates.notes: Specific discussion of the three modes of betrothal: money (kesef), document (shtar), and intercourse (biah), including minimum values and conditions

candidates.name: Betrothal by Money (Kiddushei Kesef)
candidates.notes: Betrothal effected through giving money or money's worth; dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel regarding minimum value (dinar vs. peruta)

candidates.name: Betrothal by Document (Kiddushei Shtar)
candidates.notes: Betrothal effected through a written document given to the woman

candidates.name: Betrothal by Intercourse (Kiddushei Biah)
candidates.notes: Betrothal effected through sexual intercourse; also the sole mode of levirate acquisition by the yavam

candidates.name: Conditional Betrothal (Kiddushin al Tenai)
candidates.notes: Betrothal made subject to fulfillment of a condition; rules on what constitutes a valid condition, including the requirement of doubled condition (tenai kaful)

candidates.name: Betrothal under Mistaken Assumption
candidates.notes: Betrothal where one party misrepresented their status or the item used; cases where betrothal is void due to material misrepresentation

candidates.name: Sivlonot (Pre-Marital Gifts)
candidates.notes: Gifts sent by a groom to a bride after betrothal; whether sivlonot sent after an invalid betrothal constitute a new act of betrothal

candidates.name: Betrothal through an Agent (Shaliach l'Kiddushin)
candidates.notes: Rules for appointing an agent to betroth on one's behalf; when agent exceeds instructions; competition between principal and agent betrothal

candidates.name: Betrothal with Forbidden Items
candidates.notes: Whether betrothal is effected using items from which benefit is prohibited (orlah, kilei hakerem, condemned ox, etc.) or items with special sanctity (terumah, maaser sheni, hekdesh)

candidates.name: Betrothal of Two Women Simultaneously
candidates.notes: Case where a man attempts to betroth two women simultaneously with one item worth a peruta, or betroths a woman and her daughter/sister together

candidates.name: Sota Ritual — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Grouping for detailed procedural and substantive laws of the sota ritual, including the scroll, bitter waters, merit, and nullification

candidates.name: Levirate Marriage — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Grouping for detailed laws of yibbum: forbidden relatives, rival wives, levirate bond, ma'amar, sequence of acts, and disputes between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel

candidates.name: Father's Authority to Betroth His Minor Daughter
candidates.hebrew: רשות האב לקדש את בתו הקטנה
candidates.notes: The father's legal right to betroth his minor or young-adult daughter; limits of this authority and when it expires

candidates.name: Credibility of Claims Regarding Betrothal
candidates.notes: Who is believed regarding claims of betrothal, its conditions, or the identity of the betrothed; disputed claims between parties and their legal effect on relatives

candidates.name: Betrothal with Priestly Portions
candidates.notes: Whether a priest who betroths a woman with his share of sacrificial offerings effects valid betrothal; distinction between most-holy and lesser-holy offerings

candidates.name: Prohibited Seclusion — Specific Cases (Yichud)
candidates.notes: Specific rules: man may not be secluded with two women; woman may be with two men; exception when wife is present; seclusion with mother or daughter

candidates.name: Bridegroom's Blessing Requires Ten (Birchat Chatanim)
candidates.notes: The seven wedding blessings (sheva brachot) require a quorum of ten men

candidates.name: Refusal (Mi'un)
candidates.notes: A minor girl's right to refuse a marriage contracted by her mother or brothers after her father's death; this right ceases when she develops pubic hair

candidates.name: Intercourse with Minor Girl (Three Years and One Day)
candidates.hebrew: ביאת קטנה בת שלש שנים ויום אחד
candidates.notes: Halakhic intercourse with a girl aged three years and one day — acquisition through yibbum, liability for adultery, niddah impurity transmission; below that age the hymen regenerates and intercourse has no legal effect

candidates.name: Levirate Intercourse by Boy of Nine Years and One Day
candidates.hebrew: ביאת יבם בן תשע שנים ויום אחד
candidates.notes: A boy of nine years and one day who performs levirate intercourse acquires the yevama; cannot give a get until majority; transmits impurity through niddah intercourse; halakhic consequences regarding teruma and bestiality

candidates.name: Sota Ritual (Bitter Waters)
candidates.notes: Detailed procedure of the sota rite: warning, seclusion, scroll writing, erasing in water, drinking the bitter waters, and its effects

candidates.name: Warning (Kinui) for Sota
candidates.notes: Specific rules for issuing a valid warning (kinui) to one's wife prohibiting seclusion with a named man, number of witnesses required, and its effects

candidates.name: Seclusion (Stiha/Hastarah) in Sota
candidates.notes: Rules regarding the prohibited seclusion that triggers the sota process: duration, witnesses required, and what constitutes sufficient seclusion

candidates.name: Erasing the Scroll (Mechikat HaMegillah)
candidates.notes: Laws of writing and erasing the sota scroll into the bitter waters: materials permitted, passages written, and conditions that invalidate the scroll

candidates.name: Merit Delaying Sota Punishment
candidates.notes: Debate whether personal merit can delay or prevent the sotah water's effects, and implications for teaching daughters Torah

candidates.name: Nullification of Sota Waters (Bitul Mei Sotah)
candidates.notes: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai's nullification of the sota bitter water ritual when adultery proliferated among men, based on Hosea 4:14

candidates.name: Sota Forbidden to Paramour
candidates.notes: The prohibition on the sota woman marrying her paramour after divorce, derived from the double expression of defilement in Numbers 5

candidates.name: Get Written for One Departing on Dangerous Journey
candidates.hebrew: גט לאדם היוצא בשיירה או בספינה
candidates.notes: The rabbinic enactment allowing a get to be written for a man being led to execution or departing on a dangerous sea voyage or caravan journey, even before separation occurs; later extended to the dangerously ill.

candidates.name: Writing Ruler's Name with Divine Name in a Get
candidates.hebrew: שיתוף שם שלטון עם שם שמים בגט
candidates.notes: Complaint about writing the ruler's name alongside Moses's name in a get document; Galilean heretic's objection and Pharisaic response

candidates.name: Yibbum (Levirate Marriage)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of levirate marriage: who is obligated, how it is performed, acquisition of the yevama, and cases where it is inapplicable

candidates.name: Tzarat Ervah (Rival Wife of Forbidden Relative)
candidates.notes: Exemption of rival wife from levirate marriage when the other wife is a forbidden relative of the yavam; chain of rival wives of rival wives

candidates.name: Ḥalitza — Procedural Details
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of ḥalitza: the shoe, the court of three, the text recited, spitting, validity of ḥalitza under various conditions, night, left foot, missing limbs

candidates.name: Ma'amar (Levirate Betrothal)
candidates.notes: Rabbinic act of betrothal by a yavam to a yevama; effect on requiring a get in addition to chalitzah; distinction from full levirate marriage

candidates.name: Fifteen Forbidden Relatives Exempt from Yibbum
candidates.notes: The fifteen categories of women who are forbidden to the yavam as close relatives and are therefore exempt from both yibbum and chalitzah

candidates.name: Sequence of Ma'amar, Get, and Ḥalitza in Levirate Situations
candidates.notes: What actions are effective or ineffective after prior acts by the yavam: get after get, ma'amar after ma'amar, intercourse, ḥalitza; the debate between Rabban Gamliel and the Rabbis

candidates.name: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel Dispute on Rival Wives
candidates.hebrew: מַחְלֹקֶת בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל בְּצָרוֹת
candidates.notes: The fundamental dispute between Beit Shammai (permitting rival wives for levirate marriage) and Beit Hillel (forbidding them); practical consequences; their practice of intermarriage despite the dispute

candidates.name: Three-Month Waiting Period Before Remarriage
candidates.notes: Requirement for widows and divorcées to wait three months before remarrying in order to establish paternity; who is included; exceptions; dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei

candidates.name: Wife of a Brother With Whom He Did Not Coexist
candidates.notes: A brother born after the first brother's death has no levirate bond with the first brother's widow; the exemption of the wife of a brother who predeceased the yavam's birth

candidates.name: Zikah (Levirate Bond)
candidates.notes: The halakhic bond between a widow and her surviving brother-in-law (yavam) prior to yibbum or chalitzah; its effects on remarriage, teruma, and rival wives

candidates.name: Ketubah of a Yevama
candidates.notes: The yevama's marriage contract rights: payable from first husband's estate; property rights during the waiting period; Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel dispute on inheritance if she dies

candidates.name: Jointly Owned Property — Division and Partition
candidates.notes: Laws governing partition, division, and minimum size requirements for jointly owned property such as courtyards, fields, and gardens

candidates.name: Presumptive Ownership of Land (Chazakah)
candidates.notes: Specific rules for establishing presumptive ownership of land, fields, and houses through possession, including the three-year rule and required claims

candidates.name: Neighbor Damage and Distancing Requirements
candidates.notes: Laws governing minimum distances to prevent damage to neighbors and rights/restrictions between neighbors regarding disturbances, windows, odors, and projections

candidates.name: What is Included in a Sale
candidates.notes: Rules determining which components and fixtures are included by default when selling a house, field, ship, or other property

candidates.name: Detailed Inheritance Laws
candidates.notes: Specific rules of inheritance including order of succession, sons vs. daughters, firstborn's double portion, simultaneous death, and bequeathing contrary to Torah order

candidates.name: Deathbed Gifts — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Detailed rules governing deathbed gifts including act of acquisition required, wills and testaments, giving away all one's property, and recovery from illness

candidates.name: Detailed Laws of Robbery
candidates.notes: Specific laws of robbery including valuation at time of theft, acquisition through transformation, returning robbery, and purchasing from suspected thieves

candidates.name: Partition of Jointly Owned Property (Meḥitza)
candidates.notes: Laws governing construction of partitions in jointly owned courtyards, including materials, thickness, cost-sharing, and ownership of fallen walls (Bava Batra ch. 1)

candidates.name: Minimum Size for Division of Property
candidates.notes: Minimum sizes required before court will divide jointly owned property: four by four cubits for courtyard, nine kav for field, half-kav for garden, etc. (Bava Batra 1:6)

candidates.name: Residency Requirements for City Membership
candidates.notes: Laws determining when a resident becomes obligated in communal expenses such as walls and gates; twelve-month rule vs. purchasing a home (Bava Batra 1:5)

candidates.name: Presumptive Ownership After Three Years (Chazkat Shalosh Shanim)
candidates.notes: The specific rule that three years of working and profiting from land establishes presumptive ownership; different rules for irrigated vs. non-irrigated fields (Bava Batra ch. 3)

candidates.name: Claim Required to Validate Possession (Taanah)
candidates.notes: Requirement that possessor of land must provide a valid claim explaining how he became owner for the chazakah to be effective (Bava Batra 3:3)

candidates.name: Presumptive Ownership of Houses and Fields
candidates.notes: Specific application of chazakah to different types of property including houses, pits, cisterns, bathhouses, slaves, irrigated and non-irrigated fields (Bava Batra ch. 3)

candidates.name: Distancing Requirements to Prevent Damage (Harchakat Nezikin)
candidates.notes: Specific minimum distances required between various objects/activities and a neighbor's property to prevent damage: pits, trees, threshing floors, tanneries, dovecotes, etc. (Bava Batra ch. 2)

candidates.name: Neighbor Damage Rights (Hizkei Shechenim)
candidates.notes: Rights and restrictions between neighbors regarding windows, openings, noise, smoke, odors, and other disturbances in shared courtyards and adjacent properties (Bava Batra ch. 2-3)

candidates.name: Right of Way and Access (Zechut Derekh)
candidates.notes: Laws of access paths, public thoroughfares, private paths, and right of way including seller's right to access retained property through buyer's land (Bava Batra 4:2, 6:6-7)

candidates.name: What is Included in Sale of a House
candidates.notes: Detailed rules about which components are included in the sale of a house, courtyard, field, ship, or city when sold without specification vs. with 'all that is in it' (Bava Batra ch. 4)

candidates.name: What is Included in Sale of a Field
candidates.notes: Rules about what is included when selling a field: stones, reeds, attached produce, watch stations, carob trees, cisterns, etc. (Bava Batra ch. 4)

candidates.name: Field Measurements and Discrepancies in Sales (Beit Kor)
candidates.notes: Rules governing land sales where the area is specified by measure; what happens when the actual area differs from stated area, including the quarter-kav per se'a tolerance (Bava Batra ch. 7)

candidates.name: Order of Inheritance and Firstborn's Double Portion
candidates.notes: Detailed order of precedence in inheritance including son before daughter, descendants, brothers, and the firstborn's double portion; daughters' maintenance from the estate (Bava Batra ch. 8)

candidates.name: Sons vs. Daughters in Inheritance
candidates.notes: Distinction between sons who inherit and daughters who receive maintenance (mezonot) from estate; daughters inherit only when there are no sons; daughters' maintenance vs. sons' inheritance (Bava Batra ch. 8-9)

candidates.name: Bequeathing Contrary to Torah Order of Inheritance
candidates.notes: Ability to transfer property contrary to Torah inheritance order through gifts rather than inheritance declarations; deathbed gifts vs. inheritance orders (Bava Batra 8:5)

candidates.name: Inheritance When Both Die Simultaneously (Beit Collapsed)
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel when house collapses on father and son or husband and wife and order of death is unknown; rules for dividing disputed inheritance (Bava Batra ch. 9)

candidates.name: Guarantor After Loan (Arev she'Achar Matan Maaseh)
candidates.notes: Distinction between a guarantor who committed before the loan was made vs. after; Ben Nannas's ruling that post-loan guarantors have no obligation since the lender did not rely on them (Bava Batra 10:8)

candidates.name: Loan by Promissory Note vs. Oral Loan — Lien on Sold Property
candidates.hebrew: מלוה בשטר ומלוה על פה וגביית משועבדים
candidates.notes: Distinction between promissory note loan (can collect from sold/liened property) vs. oral loan or handwritten note without witnesses (can collect only from unsold property) (Bava Batra 10:8)

candidates.name: Act of Acquisition for Deathbed Gift
candidates.notes: Whether a deathbed gift requires a formal act of acquisition or whether verbal instruction suffices; dispute between Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yehoshua/Eliezer (Bava Batra 9:7)

candidates.name: Will / Testament (Dayetikei)
candidates.notes: Laws of a written will or testament, its validity, requirements for delivery, and distinction between a will found on the deceased vs. one properly transferred (Bava Batra 8:6, 9:6)

candidates.name: Giving Away All One's Property
candidates.notes: Rules for a person on his deathbed who writes away all his property; whether gift stands if he recovers; requirement to reserve some land; healthy person giving away all property (Bava Batra 9:6)

candidates.name: Acquired Privilege for Communal Easements (Chazkat Mavoi)
candidates.notes: Rules about when one acquires a prescriptive easement for use of another's property including spouts, gutters, windows, ladders, projections — fixed vs. movable structures (Bava Batra 3:6)

candidates.name: Trees Sold for Felling — What Seller Retains
candidates.notes: When buying trees in another's field — two trees vs. three trees and whether land is acquired; rights to new growth from trunk vs. roots; what happens if trees die (Bava Batra 5:4)

candidates.name: Acquisition of Produce by Pulling (Meshichah)
candidates.notes: Specific rules about when pulling vs. measuring effects acquisition of produce; when renting a place effects acquisition; different rules for flax (Bava Batra 5:7)

candidates.name: Standard Building Dimensions
candidates.notes: Standard dimensions for various building types: small house, large house, banquet hall, bridal home, cowshed, and their heights proportional to length and width (Bava Batra 6:4)

candidates.name: Projections into Public Domain
candidates.notes: Prohibition on extending balconies and projections into public domain; acquired privilege of existing projections; digging underneath public domain (Bava Batra 3:8)

candidates.name: Receipt for Partial Debt Payment
candidates.notes: Dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei about whether to exchange note for smaller one or issue a receipt for partial payment; danger of receipt being destroyed by mice (Bava Batra 10:6)

candidates.name: Robbery with Change (Shinui) — Acquisition by Transformation
candidates.notes: A robber who transforms stolen property (e.g., wood into vessels, wool into garments) acquires it via the change, and pays value at time of robbery rather than returning the item

candidates.name: Robbery Valuation at Time of Theft
candidates.notes: Principle that robbers pay according to the value of the stolen item at the time of the robbery, even if it subsequently appreciated or depreciated

candidates.name: Owner's Despair of Recovery (Yiush)
candidates.notes: When an owner despairs of recovering stolen or lost property, another person may acquire the item; relevant to salvage from river, troop, bandits, and swarms

candidates.name: Returning Robbery in Settled vs. Unsettled Area
candidates.notes: One who robbed in a settled area may not return the item in an unsettled area where it is of no benefit to the owner

candidates.name: Liability for Objects Left in Public Domain
candidates.notes: Rules on liability for damage caused by objects left or spilled in public domain, including thorns, water, straw, hay, and poured liquids

candidates.name: Damage Between Two People Walking in Public Domain
candidates.notes: Rules for when two people or carriers collide in public domain — including barrel vs. cross beam, walking vs. running — determining liability based on direction and stopping

candidates.name: Prohibition on Purchasing from Suspected Thieves
candidates.notes: Prohibition on purchasing wool, milk, kids, wood, or produce from shepherds and watchmen who tend others' property, due to presumption of theft

candidates.name: Craftsman's Payment — Enhancement vs. Expenses
candidates.notes: When a craftsman performs work improperly or damages, the owner pays only the lesser of enhancement or expenses; dispute regarding dyer who dyed wrong color

candidates.name: Craftsmen and Bailees — Liability and Rights
candidates.notes: Group covering rules specific to craftsmen who receive items to work on, including damage liability, remnants, and transfer of bailee responsibility

candidates.name: Craftsman Who Damages the Work
candidates.notes: Craftsmen (carpenter, builder, dyer) who damage items entrusted to them are liable to pay for the damage caused

candidates.name: Craftsman's Claim to Remnants and Threads
candidates.notes: Rules on which scraps, threads, and shavings belong to the craftsman (launderer, carder, tailor, carpenter) vs. the customer, based on whether the customer values them

candidates.name: Transfer of Ox to Bailee — Shifting Responsibility
candidates.notes: When an owner conveys a dangerous ox to a bailee (unpaid, borrower, paid, renter), the bailee assumes the owner's liability for damage caused by the ox

candidates.name: Rabbinic Enactments for Social Order (Takkanot — Gittin)
candidates.notes: Group of rabbinic ordinances enacted for the public good or to encourage repentance, including sikarikon, stolen beam, minor's transactions, and apotropus rules

candidates.name: Sikarikon (Law of Extorted Land)
candidates.notes: Laws governing purchase of land from a Sicarius (violent extorter) — order of acquisition from Sicarius vs. original owner; Gittin 5:6

candidates.name: Stolen Beam Built into a Building (Ordinance for the Penitent)
candidates.hebrew: גזל קורה ובנאה בבירה — תקנת השבים
candidates.notes: Ordinance allowing a robber who built a stolen beam into a building to pay its value rather than destroy the building; encourages repentance; Gittin 5:5

candidates.name: Minor's Transactions in Movable Property
candidates.notes: Rabbinic enactment validating purchases and sales by young children (paotot) for movable property; Gittin 5:7

candidates.name: Steward (Apotropus) for Orphans — Appointment and Accountability
candidates.notes: Laws of a court-appointed vs. father-appointed steward for orphans, including obligation to tithe and take oaths; Gittin 5:4

candidates.name: Debt Collection — Creditors, Orphans, and Liened Property
candidates.notes: Group covering rules about collecting debts from orphans' estates, from liened property sold to third parties, and quality of land collected

candidates.name: Debt Collection from Orphans' Inherited Property
candidates.notes: Rule that a creditor collecting from orphans' inherited property collects only from inferior-quality land; Gittin 5:1-2

candidates.name: Collection from Liened Property Sold to Third Parties (Bnei Chorin vs. Meshubad)
candidates.notes: Rules about when creditors, injured parties, and women collecting ketubah may seize liened property sold to others; Gittin 5:1-3

candidates.name: Distribution of Estate Among Orphans
candidates.notes: Rules for distributing estate when there are multiple creditors, widows, and heirs including the 'weakest one' dispute between R. Tarfon and R. Akiva

candidates.name: Modes of Acquisition — Animals, Slaves, and Barter
candidates.notes: Group covering specific modes of acquisition for animals, Canaanite slaves, and exchange/barter not covered under existing kinyan entries

candidates.name: Acquisition of Animals (Kinyan Behemah)
candidates.notes: Large animals acquired by passing reins/bit; small animals acquired by lifting or pulling; dispute between Rabbi Meir/Eliezer and Rabbis regarding pulling

candidates.name: Acquisition of Slaves (Kinyan Avadim)
candidates.notes: Modes of acquiring a Canaanite slave: money, document, or chazakah; how a slave acquires his own freedom; comparison with acquisition of land and movables

candidates.name: Barter Acquisition (Kinyan Chalifin/Chalipin)
candidates.notes: Acquisition through exchange of one item for another; once a party acquires what he receives, the risk for the item he gives transfers to the other party

candidates.name: Bailee Oaths — Claims, Changes, and Collateral
