candidates.notes: Group covering detailed rules of bailee oaths from tractate Shevuot, including changing claims and disputes over collateral

candidates.name: Oaths of the Four Bailees (Shevuot Arba Shomrim)
candidates.notes: Detailed rules of what oath each of the four bailees takes and when; principle that oath stringent on defendant is exempt, lenient is liable — Shevuot ch. 8

candidates.name: Changing One's Claim (Shinui be'Tevi'ah) — Bailee Oaths
candidates.notes: Principle: bailee who changes from one claim of liability to another, or from exemption to liability, affects guilt-offering liability — Shevuot 8:2-8:6

candidates.name: Dispute Over Value of Lost Collateral (Mashkon)
candidates.notes: Special rules when creditor and debtor dispute the value of collateral that was lost; who takes the oath — Shevuot 6:7

candidates.name: Regional Disaster Exemption for Robber (Massikin)
candidates.notes: If thugs seize a robbed field as part of a regional seizure, the robber is exempt (the field would have been taken anyway); if they came specifically due to the robber, he must compensate

candidates.name: Salvage and Compensation — Rescuing Another's Property
candidates.notes: One who salvages another's property (honey, donkey) without agreement is entitled only to wage compensation; prior agreement obligates owner to pay the full value of what the rescuer sacrificed

candidates.name: Firstborn's Double Inheritance Portion
candidates.notes: Details of the firstborn's double portion: applies to father's property but not mother's; does not include property due but not yet possessed; does not apply to appreciation after death; compared to wife's ketubah and daughters' maintenance rights

candidates.name: Sons vs. Daughters in Small Estate
candidates.notes: Dispute between Admon and Rabbis: when estate is insufficient for both sons' inheritance and daughters' sustenance, daughters take precedence

candidates.name: Movable Property Acquired Together with Land (Agav Karka)
candidates.notes: Movable property can be transferred simultaneously with land through the act of acquisition performed on the land; also binds land to oath obligations of movables

candidates.name: Prozbul
candidates.notes: Document authorizing court to collect loans despite shemitat kesafim; listed among documents that may be written on Chol HaMoed

candidates.name: Deathbed Gift — Retention of Land
candidates.notes: Laws of deathbed gifts: validity requires retention of any land; if no land retained, gift is invalid; assigning land to wife causes loss of ketubah

candidates.name: Yavam's Inheritance of Deceased Brother's Estate
candidates.notes: Whether a yavam who consummates levirate marriage acquires his brother's estate solely, or shares equally with other brothers; dispute including Rabbi Yehuda's view about the father's priority

candidates.name: Laws of Naziriteship (Nezirut)
candidates.notes: Comprehensive grouping of nazirite vow laws from tractate Nazir and related sources: vow formulations, prohibitions, duration, shaving, offerings, and special cases.

candidates.name: Laws of Arachim (Valuations)
candidates.notes: Comprehensive grouping of valuation laws from tractate Arakhin: fixed Torah valuations, assessment distinctions, affordability provisions, and valuation of limbs.

candidates.name: Arachim (Torah Valuations)
candidates.notes: Fixed Torah valuations by age and sex (Lev. 27:3-7); who can vow/be valuated; tumtum, androginus, minor, deaf-mute in context of valuations; age categories (1 month-5, 5-20, 20-60, 60+)

candidates.name: Arachim vs. Erech — Valuation vs. Assessment Distinction
candidates.notes: Distinction between fixed Torah valuation (erech) and market-value assessment (damim); cases where one is stricter/more lenient than the other

candidates.name: Affordability in Valuations (Yashot haYad)
candidates.notes: The priest's ability to reduce valuation payment for destitute person; minimum of one sela; maximum of fifty sela; whose means determine the amount

candidates.name: Valuation of Limbs
candidates.notes: Whether one can vow the valuation of a limb; items upon which the soul depends trigger full valuation; vow of one's weight

candidates.name: Status of Condemned Person in Valuations and Vows
candidates.notes: Whether a moribund person or one sentenced to death can be subject to vows of assessment or valuation; dispute between Rabbi Chanina ben Akavya and Rabbi Yosi

candidates.name: Cherem (Dedication to Priests or Temple)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of cherem: dedicating property, animals, or persons; whether cherem goes to priests or Temple treasury; limits on what may be dedicated; priests and Levites and cherem

candidates.name: Vow of One's Weight (Mishkal)
candidates.notes: Vowing to donate one's weight in silver or gold; incident of Yirmatya's mother; how to measure weight of a limb; dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosi on displacement method

candidates.name: Konam Vow Affecting Inheritance
candidates.notes: If a father vowed that his son may not benefit from his property, the son may inherit after father's death (no longer the father's property), unless the vow explicitly covered life and death

candidates.name: Dissolution of Vows — Lack of Biblical Basis
candidates.notes: The mishna's statement that the halakhot of dissolving vows 'fly in the air' with no scriptural support; categorization of Torah topics by the strength of their biblical basis.

candidates.name: Nazirite Who Made Vow Outside the Land and Came to Israel
candidates.hebrew: נזיר שגלח בחוץ לארץ ובא לארץ
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel about how long such a nazir must observe naziriteship upon arriving in the Land of Israel; Eduyot 4:11

candidates.name: Nazirite — Two Witness Groups Testifying Different Numbers of Neziruyot
candidates.hebrew: נזיר שיש לו שתי כתות עדים
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (testimony divided, no naziriteship) and Beit Hillel (two are included within five, must be nazirite twice) when witnesses disagree on the number of neziruyot vowed; Eduyot 4:11

candidates.name: Nazirite's Offering for Impurity (Korban Nazir Tamei)
candidates.notes: The nazirite who became ritually impure brings an offering for intentional impurity the same as for unwitting impurity; the nazirite's mechusar kapparah status until offerings are sacrificed

candidates.name: Conditional Vow Contingent on Birth
candidates.notes: A vow made contingent on giving birth, e.g., 'I vow a pair of birds if I give birth to a male child,' and the halakhic obligations that result

candidates.name: Nazirite Violations and Lashes
candidates.notes: Rules for when a nazirite receives multiple sets of lashes: continuous violation vs. repeated violations after forewarning for wine drinking, corpse impurity, and shaving

candidates.name: Disposition of Nazirite Funds Upon Death
candidates.notes: What happens to funds set aside for a nazirite's three offerings when the nazirite dies, including disposition of designated sin offering money, burnt offering money, and peace offering money

candidates.name: Vows to Bring Specific Meal Offerings
candidates.notes: Rules when one vows a specific type of meal offering (pan vs. deep pan, loaves vs. wafers, specific measures); bringing wrong type; what happens when the specification was vague.

candidates.name: Vows to Bring Specific Animal Offerings
candidates.notes: Rules for vague vows to bring burnt offerings or peace offerings; what animals must be brought when the animal type is unspecified; obligations of value vs. type.

candidates.name: Nazirite Vow (Nezirut)
candidates.notes: The laws of naziriteship: vow formulations, duration, prohibitions, and conclusion. Core topic of tractate Nazir.

candidates.name: Nazirite Prohibitions (Issurei Nazir)
candidates.notes: Three categories: wine and grape products, shaving, corpse impurity.

candidates.name: Nazirite Prohibition on Grape Products
candidates.notes: Prohibition on wine, grapes, chartzanim and zaggim (skins and seeds); combining quantities; olive-bulk threshold.

candidates.name: Nazirite Prohibition on Shaving (Taar HaNazir)
candidates.notes: Prohibition on cutting hair during naziriteship; what actions constitute a violation; shampooing vs. combing.

candidates.name: Nazirite Prohibition on Corpse Impurity
candidates.notes: Prohibition on contracting corpse impurity; which sources of impurity obligate shaving; met mitzvah exception.

candidates.name: Duration of Nazirite Term
candidates.notes: Default thirty-day term; extended terms; vow formulations affecting duration; multiple consecutive naziriteships.

candidates.name: Nazirite Like Samson (Nezirut Shimshon)
candidates.notes: Permanent naziriteship modeled after Samson; cannot lighten hair; no offering for impurity; distinction from ordinary permanent nazirite.

candidates.name: Permanent Nazirite (Nazir Olam)
candidates.notes: One who vows naziriteship forever; may lighten hair when it grows heavy; brings offerings like completing a term.

candidates.name: Nazirite Shaving of Purity (Giluach Taharah)
candidates.notes: Shaving and offerings at completion of pure nazirite term; procedure, order of offerings, throwing hair under the pot.

candidates.name: Nazirite Shaving of Impurity (Giluach Tumah)
candidates.notes: Shaving and offerings when nazirite becomes impure mid-term; sprinkling on third and seventh days; negating the tally.

candidates.name: Nazirite Offerings (Korbanot Nazir)
candidates.notes: Three offerings at end of naziriteship (sin, burnt, peace offering); bird offerings for impurity; wave offering of cooked foreleg.

candidates.name: Husband's Nullification of Wife's Naziriteship
candidates.hebrew: הפרת נזירות האשה על ידי הבעל
candidates.notes: When and how a husband can nullify his wife's nazirite vow; effect on separated offerings; limits of nullification after offerings begun.

candidates.name: Father's Naziriteship for Minor Son
candidates.notes: A father may impose naziriteship on his minor son; son may reject it; disposition of already-separated offerings.

candidates.name: Naziriteship Observed Outside Eretz Yisrael
candidates.notes: Dispute of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel whether one must repeat naziriteship upon arriving in Eretz Yisrael; case of Queen Helene.

candidates.name: Impurity Negating the Nazirite Tally
candidates.notes: Rules for when corpse impurity negates all or part of the days counted; disputes between Sages.

candidates.name: Conditional Nazirite Vow
candidates.notes: Vow contingent on birth of son, outcome of battle, etc.; what happens if condition is met mid-term.

candidates.name: Language and Substitutes for Nazirite Vow
candidates.notes: Valid substitute terms (nazik, nazi'ach, pazi'ach); intimations of nazirite vows; partial statements binding as naziriteship.

candidates.name: Uncertain Impurity of Nazirite (Safek Tumah shel Nazir)
candidates.notes: Two nazirites where one may have become impure; procedures for offerings under uncertainty; case of the unknown impurity.

candidates.name: Specific Laws of Naziriteship
candidates.notes: Cluster of specific halakhic topics within naziriteship: who can take the vow, chain vows, cemetery vows, funding others' offerings, and dissolution effects

candidates.name: Naziriteship of Women, Slaves, and Gentiles
candidates.notes: Gentiles excluded from naziriteship; women and Canaanite slaves included; relative stringencies between women and slaves.

candidates.name: Taking Nazirite Vow While in a Cemetery
candidates.notes: Days spent in a cemetery at start of naziriteship do not count toward term; re-entry triggers impurity obligation.

candidates.name: Effect of Dissolving a Nazirite Vow
candidates.notes: What happens to separated offerings when a nazirite vow is dissolved by a halakhic authority; retroactive effect.

candidates.name: Chain of Nazirite Vows (And I — Va'Ani)
candidates.notes: When multiple persons vow naziriteship by saying 'and I' sequentially; dissolving one affects the others; interdependence of vows.

candidates.name: Vow to Fund Another Nazirite's Offerings
candidates.notes: One who accepts obligation to pay for another nazirite's shaving offerings; half vs. full obligation; mutual shaving arrangement.

candidates.name: Types of Vows (Neder Categories)
candidates.notes: The Mishnaic classification of vow categories: exhortation, exaggeration, unintentional, and circumstantially impeded vows — each treated leniently by the Sages

candidates.name: Vows of Exhortation (Nidrei Zeiruzin)
candidates.notes: Vows used to encourage or pressure another in bargaining or social interaction, which the Sages dissolved without requiring a halakhic authority

candidates.name: Vows of Exaggeration (Nidrei Guzma)
candidates.notes: Hyperbolic vow expressions not intended literally, dissolved by the Sages without requiring a request to a halakhic authority

candidates.name: Unintentional Vows (Nidrei Shegagot)
candidates.notes: Vows taken under mistaken assumptions or forgotten circumstances, which the Sages dissolved without a formal request to a halakhic authority

candidates.name: Vows Impeded by Circumstances Beyond One's Control (Nidrei Ones)
candidates.notes: Vows that could not be fulfilled due to unforeseen circumstances (illness, flood, etc.) which are not binding

candidates.name: Prohibition of Benefit by Vow (Hadarah — Muddar Hana'ah)
candidates.notes: Group covering the category of vows prohibiting benefit from another person, including scope, shared property, and use of gifts to circumvent such vows

candidates.name: Prohibition of Benefit by Vow (Hadarah/Muddar Hana'ah)
candidates.notes: The specific category of vow prohibiting one person from deriving benefit from another, covering what transactions, entry, lending, and assistance are included or excluded

candidates.name: Shared Property and Vows of Benefit
candidates.notes: How vows of benefit prohibition operate when partners share a courtyard or other property; whether each can enter their own portion; forced sale of portion to avoid causing transgression

candidates.name: Validity of Gift as Means of Circumventing a Vow
candidates.notes: The rule that a gift given solely to circumvent a vow must be a genuine gift capable of being consecrated; the Beit Horon incident; transferring property to a third party to feed someone bound by a vow

candidates.name: Detailed Laws of Vow Annulment by Husband/Father (Hafarah)
candidates.notes: Cluster covering the detailed rules of hafarah: which vows a husband or father may annul, the yavam's authority, preemptive annulment, and edge cases

candidates.name: Husband's Nullification of Wife's Vows
candidates.hebrew: הפרת נדרי האשה על ידי הבעל
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of when and how a husband can nullify his wife's vows, including timing (same day), which vows qualify (affliction, affecting relations), betrothed vs. married, and joint nullification by father and husband

candidates.name: Father's Authority over Betrothed Daughter's Vows
candidates.notes: The joint authority of father and betrothed husband over the vows of a betrothed young woman, including what happens when one of them dies, and the limits of each one's authority

candidates.name: Yavam's Authority over Yevama's Vows
candidates.notes: Dispute among Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yehoshua, and Rabbi Akiva whether a yavam can nullify the vows of his yevama while she awaits levirate marriage

candidates.name: Pre-emptive Nullification of Future Vows
candidates.notes: The question of whether a husband can preemptively nullify all future vows his wife will take; debate between Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis; includes the practice of Torah scholars before marriage

candidates.name: Vows of Affliction (Inui Nefesh)
candidates.notes: The category of vows a husband can nullify because they cause affliction to the wife — definition and scope of what constitutes inui nefesh vs. what does not

candidates.name: Vows Affecting Relations Between Husband and Wife
candidates.notes: The category of vows a husband can nullify because they affect their marital relationship — including vows about work obligations, sexual prohibition, and similar matters

candidates.name: Vow of Woman Removing Herself from All Jews
candidates.notes: The case of a woman who vows to be removed from all Jews sexually; the husband nullifies his portion and she remains forbidden to all others; the evolution of this halakha to prevent women from exploiting vows

candidates.name: Categories and Types of Oaths (Shevuot)
candidates.notes: The Mishnaic classification of oath categories: the four oaths framework, oath in vain, and oath on an utterance

candidates.name: Four Categories of Oaths (Arba Shevuot)
candidates.notes: The Mishnaic framework of four oath types: future positive, future negative, past positive, past negative — foundational structure of tractate Shevuot

candidates.name: Oath Taken in Vain (Shevuat Shav)
candidates.notes: Oath about something impossible or obviously false, or oath to violate a commandment; distinct from shevuat sheker (false oath) — treated in Shevuot ch. 3

candidates.name: Oath on an Utterance (Shevuat Bitui)
candidates.notes: Oath to do or refrain from doing something in the future, or affirming/denying something about the past; primary category in Shevuot ch. 3

candidates.name: Substitute Terms for Vows (Yad and Kinuyim)
candidates.notes: Covers the substitute and analogous terms (konam, konaḥ, konas, etc.) that function as valid vow formulations, and intimations of vows (yad l'nedarim)

candidates.name: Dissolution of Vows by Halakhic Authority (Hatarat Nedarim — Process)
candidates.notes: The procedural mechanism by which a sage dissolves a vow, including the 'opening' (petach) — finding an extenuating circumstance — and regret (charatah); covers what types of openings are valid

candidates.name: Interpretation of Unspecified Vows (Stam Nedarim)
candidates.notes: Rules for determining the scope of vows when the vow term is unspecified — whether it follows common usage, regional custom, or the speaker's intent; includes lenient treatment of specified intent

candidates.name: Scope of Food Vows (What Foods are Included)
candidates.notes: Detailed rules for which foods and derivatives are included when one vows against a food type (wine includes/excludes vinegar, olive includes/excludes oil, etc.)

candidates.name: Partially Dissolved Vow is Entirely Dissolved
candidates.notes: The principle, attributed to Rabbi Akiva, that if part of a vow is dissolved it is entirely dissolved; covers interconnected vs. separate vow formulations

candidates.name: Time Limits in Vows
candidates.notes: Rules governing vows with specified time limits — 'today,' 'this week,' 'this month,' 'until Passover,' 'until the rains' — including whether 'until' means before or at the end of the event

candidates.name: False Vows to Protect Life or Property from Murderers and Robbers
candidates.notes: The permission to make false vow-like declarations to protect oneself or one's property from robbers and tax collectors; dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel on scope

candidates.name: Interpretation of Vow Language According to Common Usage
candidates.notes: The principle that vow language is interpreted according to the common usage of the speaker and their locale — covering terms like 'seafarers,' 'those with dark heads,' 'those who rest on Shabbat,' etc.

candidates.name: Vow by Association with Forbidden or Sacred Object
candidates.hebrew: נדר הבא מכוח קדשים או איסורים
candidates.notes: The rule that a vow takes effect only when the object of association is itself forbidden by vow (e.g., korban), not by Torah law (e.g., pig, neveilah); includes the hierarchy of valid vow associations

candidates.name: Vow Within a Vow (Neder b'Neder)
candidates.notes: The rule that an additional vow can stack onto an existing vow prohibition, unlike oaths which cannot stack (ein shevuah chal al shevuah)

candidates.name: Differences Between Vows and Oaths (Nedarim vs. Shevuot)
candidates.hebrew: חומרי נדרים על שבועות וחומרי שבועות על נדרים
candidates.notes: The comparative stringencies and leniencies of vows vs. oaths — vows apply to objects (devar sheyesh bo mamash) but not actions; oaths apply to actions but cannot override mitzvot; vow within vow vs. no oath within oath

candidates.name: Examination of Minors' Vows
candidates.notes: Rules about validity of vows made by girls (age 11-12) and boys (age 12-13) — their vows require examination of understanding; once they develop pubic hair, vows are valid without examination

candidates.name: Annulling Vows on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Permission to nullify or dissolve vows on Shabbat when the vow affects Shabbat observance or oneg Shabbat

candidates.name: Details of the Oath of Testimony (Shevuat Edut)
candidates.notes: Sub-rules governing the oath of testimony: where it is administered, what claims it applies to, etc.

candidates.name: Rabbinic Oath Enactments (Takkanot Shevuah)
candidates.notes: Rabbinic enactments shifting or extending oath obligations beyond biblical law, including plaintiff oaths, partner oaths, and storekeeper oaths — Shevuot ch. 7

candidates.name: Oath of Testimony (Shevuat Edut)
candidates.notes: Oath taken by witnesses falsely denying knowledge of testimony; special rules re: who can administer it, liability, and sliding-scale offering — Shevuot ch. 4

candidates.name: Oath of Testimony — Court vs. Outside Court
candidates.hebrew: שבועת עדות בבית דין ושלא בבית דין
candidates.notes: Dispute whether witnesses become liable only when denying testimony in court or also outside court — Shevuot 4:1, 4:3

candidates.name: Oath of Testimony Limited to Monetary Claims
candidates.notes: Oath of testimony applies only where testimony would generate monetary liability; exempt for capital cases, fines, status claims — Shevuot 4:6–4:7

candidates.name: Oath on a Deposit (Shevuat Pikadon)
candidates.notes: Oath falsely denying possession of another's deposit, loan, pledge, or stolen/lost item; requires guilt-offering and repayment with fifth — Shevuot ch. 5

candidates.name: Oath of Testimony Not Applicable to Fines (Kenas)
candidates.notes: One who denies a fine (double payment, four/five-fold, rape fine) is exempt from false oath offering since fines are not paid on self-admission — Shevuot 5:5

candidates.name: Partial Admission Oath (Modeh beMiktzat — Shevuot)
candidates.notes: Detailed rules of partial admission oath: minimum claim amount (two ma'ah), minimum admission (one peruta), same-type requirement — Shevuot ch. 6

candidates.name: Rabbinically Imposed Oath — Claimant Takes Oath and Collects (Shevuat HeSset/Takkanat Chachamim)
candidates.notes: Rabbinic enactment where plaintiff (not defendant) takes oath and collects: hired worker, robbery victim, injured party, opponent of oath-suspect — Shevuot ch. 7

candidates.name: Person Suspected of Taking False Oaths (Chashud al HaShevuah)
candidates.notes: When one litigant is disqualified from taking an oath due to prior false oaths, the opposing party takes the oath and collects — Shevuot 7:4

candidates.name: Storekeeper's Ledger Oath (Shevuat Chanvani al Pinkaso)
candidates.notes: Rabbinic enactment allowing storekeeper to take oath and collect when employer sent workers to receive goods — Shevuot 7:5–7:6

candidates.name: Oath of Partners and Managers (Shevuat Shutafin)
candidates.notes: Partners, sharecroppers, stewards, and household managers can be required to take oaths even without specific claims — Shevuot 7:8

candidates.name: Oath Administered Using Divine Names and Appellations
candidates.notes: Dispute between R. Meir and Rabbis whether oaths and curses using divine appellations (not Tetragrammaton) generate liability — Shevuot 4:13

candidates.name: Oath to Perform or Refrain from a Mitzvah — Exempt
candidates.notes: One who swears to perform or not perform a mitzvah is exempt from sliding-scale offering for violation; dispute with R. Yehuda ben Beteira — Shevuot 3:6

candidates.name: Laws of Shema
candidates.notes: Detailed laws governing the recitation of Shema, including times, posture, intention, interruptions, and order of paragraphs

candidates.name: Laws of Tefillah
candidates.notes: Detailed laws governing the recitation of the Amida and general prayer practice, including times, direction, preparation, and special circumstances

candidates.name: Laws of Birkat HaMazon
candidates.notes: Detailed laws governing Grace after Meals, including zimmun, place of recitation, and special foods

candidates.name: Laws of Food Blessings
candidates.notes: Laws governing blessings over various categories of food, priority among foods, and the principle of primary and secondary foods

candidates.name: Times for Recitation of Shema
candidates.notes: Laws governing the earliest and latest times for reciting Shema in the morning and evening

candidates.name: Blessings Accompanying Shema
candidates.notes: The blessings recited before and after Shema in both morning and evening: Yotzer Or, Ahavah Rabbah, Emet veYatziv, Emet veEmunah, Hashkivenu

candidates.name: Intention in Shema (Kavvanah)
candidates.notes: The requirement to have intent while reciting Shema, and whether reading Torah that happened to be Shema fulfills the obligation

candidates.name: Interruptions During Shema
candidates.notes: Laws concerning permissible and impermissible interruptions between paragraphs of Shema and within each paragraph, including greeting others

candidates.name: Posture for Reciting Shema
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel whether one must recline at night and stand in the morning, or may recite in any position

candidates.name: Order of Shema Paragraphs
candidates.notes: The rationale for ordering the three paragraphs of Shema as they are, including acceptance of yoke of Heaven before yoke of mitzvot

candidates.name: Groom's Exemption from Shema
candidates.notes: A groom is exempt from reciting Shema on his wedding night due to preoccupation; Rabban Gamliel's practice of reciting it anyway

candidates.name: Mentioning Exodus at Night
candidates.notes: Obligation to mention the Exodus from Egypt at night as part of Shema; derived by Ben Zoma from 'all the days of your life'; dispute with Rabbis about inclusion of messianic era

candidates.name: Times for Prayer (Amida)
candidates.notes: The latest permissible times for Shacharit, Mincha, Maariv, and Musaf prayers

candidates.name: Facing Jerusalem During Prayer
candidates.notes: Requirement to face toward the Temple/Holy of Holies when praying; adjustments for those traveling by donkey, ship, etc.

candidates.name: Preparation for Prayer (Kavanah and Stillness)
candidates.notes: The early pious would wait one hour before praying to achieve proper gravity and submission; not interrupting prayer even for a king or snake

candidates.name: Fixed Prayer vs. Supplication
candidates.notes: Rabbi Eliezer's ruling that one whose prayer is fixed (mechanical) has not properly supplicated; the ideal of kavvanah in prayer

candidates.name: Prayer in Dangerous Situations
candidates.notes: Abbreviated prayer for one walking in a dangerous place; Rabbi Yehoshua's formula of short prayer

candidates.name: Prayer Leader (Shaliach Tzibbur)
candidates.notes: Laws of the communal prayer leader, including replacement when he errs, what constitutes heretical additions to prayer, and birchat kohanim in this context

candidates.name: Musaf Prayer
candidates.notes: Additional prayer corresponding to the Musaf offering; times and quorum requirements for Musaf

candidates.name: Distancing from Filth for Prayer
candidates.notes: Requirement to distance at least four cubits from urine and feces before reciting Shema or praying

candidates.name: Traveler's Prayer (Tefillat HaDerech)
candidates.notes: Prayer upon entering and exiting a city; Ben Azzai's view of four prayers — two upon entrance and two upon exit

candidates.name: Vain Prayer (Tefillat Shav)
candidates.notes: Prohibition against praying for something that has already occurred or cannot be changed, e.g., praying the sex of an already-conceived child

candidates.name: Prayer upon Entering/Exiting Study Hall
candidates.notes: Rabbi Nechunia ben HaKana's practice of reciting a brief prayer upon entering and exiting the beit midrash for protection from mishaps and gratitude

candidates.name: Fluency of Prayer as Omen of Acceptance
candidates.notes: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa's practice of knowing whether his prayer for the sick was accepted based on whether it was fluent in his mouth; erring in prayer as bad omen

candidates.name: Mention of Rain in Amida (Geshem/Tal)
candidates.notes: Recitation of 'mashiv haruach' in the second blessing and the request for rain in the ninth blessing of the Amida

candidates.name: Abbreviated Amida (Tefillah Ketzarah)
candidates.notes: Dispute among Rabban Gamliel, Rabbi Yehoshua, and Rabbi Akiva about whether the full eighteen blessings or an abbreviated form is required

candidates.name: Zimmun (Invitation for Grace After Meals)
candidates.notes: Laws of the zimmun — the formal invitation to recite Grace after Meals jointly; who counts toward the quorum, formula for different group sizes, division of groups

candidates.name: Place of Recitation for Grace After Meals
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel whether one who forgot to recite Grace after Meals must return to the place where he ate

candidates.name: Grace After Meals for Special Foods
candidates.hebrew: ברכת המזון על פירות שבעת המינים
candidates.notes: Dispute whether full three-blessing Grace after Meals or abbreviated single blessing is required after eating fruit of the seven species

candidates.name: Blessings over Categories of Food
candidates.notes: Specific blessings for tree fruits (borei pri haetz), ground produce (borei pri haadama), bread (hamotzi), wine (borei pri hagafen), vegetables, and the catch-all shehakol

candidates.name: Priority of Seven Species in Blessings
candidates.notes: Which food to bless first when multiple foods are present; dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbis regarding priority of seven species

candidates.name: One Blessing Exempting Another
candidates.notes: When a blessing over a primary food exempts a secondary food from its own blessing; the principle of ikar and tafel

candidates.name: Primary and Secondary Food (Ikar veTafel)
candidates.notes: The principle that a blessing over the primary food exempts the secondary food accompanying it from a separate blessing

candidates.name: Blessing over Diluted vs. Undiluted Wine
candidates.hebrew: ברכה על יין מזוג ושאינו מזוג
candidates.notes: Dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbis whether a blessing may be recited over undiluted wine or only after water is added

candidates.name: Blessings on Natural Phenomena
candidates.notes: Blessings over lightning, thunder, storms, mountains, seas, rivers, deserts, the great sea, and shooting stars

candidates.name: Blessing on Places of Miracles
candidates.notes: Blessing recited upon seeing a place where miracles were performed for Israel; blessing upon seeing where idolatry was eradicated

candidates.name: Blessing on Good and Bad Tidings
candidates.notes: Reciting 'hatov vehameitiv' for good tidings and 'dayyan ha'emet' for bad tidings; obligation to bless for bad just as for good

candidates.name: Prayer for the Welfare of the Government
candidates.notes: The obligation to pray for governmental stability, since without it people would devour one another (Avot 3:2).

candidates.name: Mentioning God's Name in Greetings
candidates.notes: Rabbinic institution to greet others using God's name, as Boaz did; derived from biblical precedent to prevent neglect of this custom

candidates.name: Arba Parshiyot (Four Special Torah Portions)
candidates.notes: The four special Torah portions read on Shabbatot surrounding Adar: Shekalim, Zachor, Parah, HaChodesh

candidates.name: Musaf Blessings of Rosh HaShanah (Malkhuyot, Zikhronot, Shofarot)
candidates.notes: The three special blessings of the Rosh HaShanah Musaf Amidah and their associated laws

candidates.name: Languages Required for Prayer and Recitation
candidates.notes: Mishnaic category distinguishing recitations valid in any language from those requiring Hebrew (Lashon HaKodesh)

candidates.name: Sanctity and Laws of the Synagogue
candidates.notes: Halakhic sanctity of synagogues, their sale, permitted uses, and hierarchy of sacred objects

candidates.name: Blessing over Incense at a Meal
candidates.notes: One who blesses over wine at the end of a meal also recites the blessing over the incense (mugmar) brought after the meal

candidates.name: Responding Amen to Another's Blessing
candidates.notes: One answers amen after a Jew even if he did not hear the full blessing; but one does not answer amen after a Samaritan unless he heard the full blessing

candidates.name: Four Special Torah Portions (Arba Parshiyot)
candidates.notes: The four special Torah portions read on Shabbatot surrounding Adar: Shekalim, Zachor, Parah, HaChodesh

candidates.name: Parshat Shekalim
candidates.notes: Special Torah portion read on Shabbat of or before Rosh Chodesh Adar, relating to the half-shekel Temple tax

candidates.name: Parshat Zachor
candidates.notes: Special Torah portion read on the Shabbat before Purim; mitzva to remember/eradicate Amalek

candidates.name: Parshat Parah
candidates.notes: Special Torah portion about the Red Heifer read on the third special Shabbat, to prepare for Passover purity

candidates.name: Parshat HaChodesh
candidates.notes: Special Torah portion about the first month (Exodus 12) read on the fourth special Shabbat before Passover

candidates.name: Number of Torah Readers (Aliyot) by Day
candidates.notes: Rules governing the number of people called up to read Torah: 3 on Monday/Thursday/Shabbat Mincha, 4 on Rosh Chodesh/Chol HaMoed, 5 on Yom Tov, 6 on Yom Kippur, 7 on Shabbat

candidates.name: Laws of Haftarah Reading
candidates.notes: When haftarah is read, who reads it, skipping within Prophets, the person who reads haftarah also leads other parts of service

candidates.name: Blessings Before and After Torah Reading
candidates.notes: Who recites blessings before and after the Torah reading — first and last reader bless; middle readers do not

candidates.name: Minimum Verses in Torah Reading
candidates.notes: Each Torah reader must read a minimum of three verses; rules about reading to a translator one verse at a time

candidates.name: Aramaic Translation (Targum) During Torah Reading
candidates.notes: Rules about translating Torah and Prophets into Aramaic during public reading — one verse at a time for Torah, three for Prophets

candidates.name: Requirements of Ten for Sacred Matters (Davar shebKedushah)
candidates.notes: List of sacred activities requiring a minyan of ten: Shema blessings, prayer repetition, Priestly Blessing, Torah reading, haftarah, funeral rites, bridegroom's blessing, zimmun with God's name

candidates.name: Sanctity of Synagogue (Kedushat Beit Knesset)
candidates.notes: Halakhic sanctity of synagogues and their sale; restrictions on uses even in ruin; hierarchy of sacred objects

candidates.name: Sale of a Synagogue (Mechirat Beit Knesset)
candidates.notes: Rules governing the sale of a synagogue — conditions, permitted uses after sale, downgrading of sanctity prohibition

candidates.name: Prohibited Sections in Public Torah Reading and Translation
candidates.hebrew: סדרי קריאה — נקרא ולא מתורגם, לא נקרא ולא מתורגם
candidates.notes: Certain Torah passages (Reuben/Bilhah, second Golden Calf narrative, Priestly Benediction, David/Amnon) are read but not translated or neither read nor translated in public

candidates.name: Qualifications of Prayer Leader (Shaliach Tzibbur)
candidates.notes: Who may lead public prayer — restrictions on those with exposed limbs, the blind (dispute), heretics; also covers Priestly Blessing eligibility

candidates.name: Eligibility for Priestly Blessing (Birchat Kohanim — Who May Duchen)
candidates.notes: Priests with blemished or discolored hands, those who attract undue attention, may not duchen; rules about who performs the blessing in connection with Torah reading service

candidates.name: Passing Before the Ark (Maavar Lifnei HaTevah)
candidates.notes: Rules about who leads the repeated Amida prayer — connection to haftarah reader, restrictions on those in colored/no-sandal garments

candidates.name: Special Torah Portions for Holidays and Occasions
candidates.notes: The specific Torah portions assigned for each holiday: Passover, Shavuot, Rosh HaShanah, Yom Kippur, Sukkot, Hanukkah, Purim, Rosh Chodesh, fast days

candidates.name: Zimmun with God's Name (Zimmun beShem with Ten)
candidates.notes: The elevated form of zimmun using God's name requires ten adult men present

candidates.name: Directing One's Heart to Heaven in Offerings
candidates.notes: Final mishna principle: one who brings a large offering and one who brings a meager offering have equal merit if they direct their heart to Heaven.

candidates.name: Hallel at the Seder
candidates.notes: The recitation of hallel at the Passover seder split between before and after the meal, dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel about where the first portion ends, and the concluding blessing (Geulah)

candidates.name: Musaf Blessings of Rosh HaShanah (Malkhuyot, Zikhronot, Shofarot)
candidates.notes: The three special blessings of the Rosh HaShanah Musaf Amidah: Malkhuyot (Kingship), Zikhronot (Remembrances), Shofarot (Shofar verses); minimum ten verses each; order of shofar blowing relative to each blessing

candidates.name: Zikhronot (Remembrances Blessing)
candidates.notes: The Rosh HaShanah Musaf blessing containing verses about God's remembrance of creation, covenant, and deeds

candidates.name: Malkhuyot (Kingship Blessing)
candidates.notes: The Rosh HaShanah Musaf blessing proclaiming God's kingship with ten biblical verses; debate between R. Akiva and R. Yochanan ben Nuri about its placement

candidates.name: Shofarot (Shofar Verses Blessing)
candidates.notes: The Rosh HaShanah Musaf blessing containing ten verses mentioning the shofar, from Torah, Writings, and Prophets

candidates.name: Prayer Leader Fulfilling Obligation for Congregation
candidates.notes: Debate between Rabban Gamliel and sages whether the shaliach tzibbur's prayer fulfills the obligation for individuals who do not know how to pray; context of Rosh HaShanah Musaf

candidates.name: Recitations Valid in Any Language
candidates.notes: Category of Torah recitations and declarations (e.g., Shema, Amidah, Birkat Hamazon, vow oaths) that may be said in any language, not only Hebrew

candidates.name: Recitations Required in Hebrew (Lashon haKodesh)
candidates.notes: Category of Torah recitations that must specifically be said in Hebrew: bikkurim declaration, chalitza, blessings and curses at Gerizim/Ebal, priestly blessing, High Priest's Yom Kippur reading, Hakhel, eglah arufah, war priest's address

candidates.name: Blessings and Curses at Gerizim and Ebal
candidates.notes: The ceremony of blessings and curses pronounced on Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal: who stood where, procedure of Levites turning and reciting, the people's Amen responses

candidates.name: Manner of Singing the Song at the Sea
candidates.notes: Debate whether Israel sang the Song of the Sea responsively after Moses (like Hallel) or in unison together with Moses (like Shema)

candidates.name: Hallel on Sukkot
candidates.notes: Recitation of the full Hallel throughout the eight days of Sukkot and Shemini Atzeret, including waving the lulav during Hallel

candidates.name: Prayer for Rain (Geshem / Tefillat Geshem)
candidates.notes: The insertion of rain-related phrases in the Amida (mashiv haruach, veten tal umatar) and the timing of when one begins and ends requesting rain

candidates.name: Anenu and Special Fast Day Prayers
candidates.notes: The twenty-four blessing prayer recited on fast days, including the six additional blessings with special conclusions invoking historical episodes of divine response

candidates.name: Ne'ila Prayer (Closing Prayer)
candidates.notes: The closing prayer recited on communal fast days and Yom Kippur, representing a fourth Amida in a single day alongside shacharit, musaf, and mincha

candidates.name: Recitation of Ten Commandments in the Temple
candidates.notes: The daily practice of the priestly watch in the Chamber of Hewn Stone to recite the Ten Commandments along with the Shema and its blessings

candidates.name: Differences in Priestly Blessing in the Temple
candidates.notes: Distinctions between the Priestly Benediction as performed in the Temple vs. outside: recited as one blessing, use of the divine name as written, hands raised above the head, and the response formula

candidates.name: Levels of Purity and Social Classes (Am HaAretz, Haver, Perushim)
candidates.notes: The graduated system of purity levels and the social classes associated with them: am haaretz, perushim, haverim, and their interactions regarding trustworthiness and transmission of impurity

candidates.name: Purity Practices at Meals (Handwashing)
candidates.notes: Rabbinic purity practices associated with meals: handwashing before eating and after eating (mayim acharonim)

candidates.name: Vessel Impurity by Material Type
candidates.notes: Laws of vessel susceptibility to impurity organized by material: earthenware, wood, metal, etc., each with distinct rules

candidates.name: Immersion of Vessels Purchased from Gentiles
candidates.notes: Requirement to immerse vessels purchased from gentiles in a mikvah before use

candidates.name: Impurity Transmitted by Idolatrous Objects Through Carrying
candidates.notes: Dispute whether objects of idol worship transmit impurity like a creeping animal (by touch) or like a menstruating woman (by carrying)

candidates.name: Immersion on Yom Tov and Shabbat
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel regarding immersion of vessels and persons before Yom Tov or on Yom Tov/Shabbat itself

candidates.name: Handwashing at a Meal (Netilat Yadayim)
candidates.notes: Laws of handwashing before and after a meal, including the dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel about the order of washing and mixing wine

candidates.name: Final Waters (Mayim Acharonim)
candidates.notes: Washing hands after a meal before Grace after Meals; dispute about whether to sweep the house first or wash first

candidates.name: Immersion for Baal Keri (Ezra's Decree)
candidates.notes: Ezra's decree requiring immersion before Torah study and prayer for one who experienced a seminal emission; what Torah activities are permitted beforehand

candidates.name: Tumah Status of Human Blood
candidates.notes: Human blood compared to animal blood (renders seeds susceptible to tumah) and to sheretz blood (not liable for eating) — its dual halakhic nature

candidates.name: Am HaAretz and Ritual Purity
candidates.notes: The status of an am haaretz with respect to ritual purity; their garments as sources of impurity for those more scrupulous; trusted periods (winepress season, pilgrimage festival).

candidates.name: Perushim (Those Scrupulous in Purity)
candidates.notes: The class of people who are meticulously careful in ritual purity; their garments are considered impure with the treading of a zav for priests eating teruma.

candidates.name: Tumat Midras (Impurity by Treading/Pressure)
candidates.notes: Impurity conveyed when a zav or niddah treads on or sits/lies upon an object; the garments of an am haaretz are considered midras for perushim, and so on up the levels of purity.

candidates.name: Levels of Purity (Non-Sacred, Tithes, Teruma, Kodesh, Mei Chatat)
candidates.hebrew: מדרגות הטהרה: חולין, מעשר, תרומה, קודש, חטאת
candidates.notes: The graduated system of purity levels: one who immersed for non-sacred food may not eat tithes; for tithes may not eat teruma; for teruma may not eat sacrificial food; for sacrificial food may not touch purification waters. Each level has stricter requirements.

candidates.name: Stringencies of Kodesh over Terumah (Greater Strictness for Sacrificial Food)
candidates.notes: Detailed halakhic differences requiring greater purity for sacrificial foods than for teruma: immersing vessels inside other vessels, carrying trodden objects, hands, fourth-degree impurity, etc.

candidates.name: Tevul Yom and Purity Levels
candidates.notes: The distinction in purity requirements for a tevul yom (one who immersed that day) regarding teruma vs. kodesh; immersion without intent to achieve purity status is ineffective.

candidates.name: Trustworthiness of Amei HaAretz in Purity (Ne'emanut)
candidates.notes: Periods and circumstances under which amei haaretz are deemed trustworthy regarding ritual purity: during winepress season, during pilgrimage festivals, within Modi'im boundaries, etc.

candidates.name: Fourth-Degree Impurity (Revi'i l'Tumah)
candidates.notes: The concept that sacrificial food can be rendered impure to a fourth degree (disqualified but not transmitting impurity further), while teruma is only susceptible to third-degree impurity; a unique stringency for kodesh.

candidates.name: Haver vs. Am HaAretz Distinction
candidates.notes: The social/religious distinction between a haver (one meticulous in purity and tithes) and an am haaretz; practical halakhic consequences for accepting food and vessels from an am haaretz.

candidates.name: Modi'im Boundary for Purity Trustworthiness
candidates.notes: Potters within the boundary of Modi'im (15 mil from Jerusalem) are trusted regarding purity of earthenware vessels; those outside are not; geographic demarcation for purity trustworthiness.

candidates.name: Ritual Impurity of Animal Hide
candidates.notes: When animal hide retains halakhic status of flesh for impurity purposes; threshold of flaying for hide to separate from flesh status; different rules for carpet vs. jug preparation

candidates.name: Skin of Eight Creeping Animals (Sheratzim)
candidates.notes: Whether skins of the eight sheratzim impart impurity like their flesh; dispute between R. Yochanan ben Nuri and Sages; specific animals listed

candidates.name: Placenta and Edibility According to Personal Disposition
candidates.notes: Placenta found in slaughtered animal: permitted for one with hardy soul; intent to eat raises it to status of food for impurity purposes but not carcass impurity

candidates.name: Partially Severed Limb or Flesh Hanging from Animal
candidates.notes: Halakhic status of a limb or flesh that is partially severed and still attached to a living animal or person; impurity status and effect of slaughter on them

candidates.name: Joining of Attached Parts to Complete Egg-Bulk for Food Impurity
candidates.hebrew: צירוף עור ועצמות לביצה לטומאת אוכלין
candidates.notes: Hide, congealed gravy, spices, bones, sinews, hooves join with meat to form egg-bulk for food impurity but not for carcass impurity (olive-bulk)

candidates.name: Bones of Living Animals and Impurity
candidates.notes: Thigh bones of carcasses and creeping animals: sealed vs. perforated bones and their different impurity status for contact and carrying

candidates.name: Impurity of a Limb Severed from a Living Person
candidates.notes: Dispute among Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Joshua, and Rabbi Nehunia regarding the impurity status of flesh and bone severed from a living person (as opposed to a corpse); Eduyot 6:2-6:3

candidates.name: Drawn Water Invalidating a Mikveh (Mayim She'uvim)
candidates.notes: The quantity of drawn water that invalidates a mikveh; dispute between Shammai (nine kavs), Hillel (a hin), and the testimony of weavers in the name of Shemaiah and Avtalion (three logs); Eduyot 1:3

candidates.name: Oven Cut Into Rings (Tannur) — Susceptibility to Impurity
candidates.notes: Testimony that an oven cut into rings with sand between them is susceptible to impurity; Rabbi Eliezer disagrees; Eduyot 7:7 (related to the famous Tannur shel Akhnai context)

candidates.name: Retroactive Reckoning of Niddah Impurity
candidates.notes: Dispute between Shammai, Hillel, and the Sages about how far back a woman's niddah impurity applies retroactively upon discovery; the 24-hour rule vs. the examination-to-examination rule; Eduyot 1:1

candidates.name: Purity of Liquids in the Temple Slaughterhouse
candidates.notes: Testimony of Rabbi Yose ben Yoezer that liquids in the Temple slaughterhouse are pure (not subject to impurity); Eduyot 8:4

candidates.name: Impurity from Touching a Corpse (Testimony of Yose ben Yoezer)
candidates.hebrew: טומאת מגע במת — עדות יוסי בן יועזר
candidates.notes: Yose ben Yoezer's testimony that one who touches a corpse becomes impure (he declared this as a leniency relative to the prior practice); Eduyot 8:4

candidates.name: Doubtful Tumah in Public vs. Private Domain
candidates.hebrew: ספק טומאה ברשות הרבים ורשות היחיד
candidates.notes: Cases of doubtful impurity debated between Rabbi Joshua (impure) and the Sages (pure) involving impure person passing pure person, and impurity in public vs. private domains; Eduyot 3:7

candidates.name: Ashes of Red Heifer Defiled by Touching Part of Them
candidates.notes: Testimony of Rabbi Shimon ben Bathyra that if a defiled person touched part of the ashes of purification, the whole batch is defiled; Eduyot 8:1

candidates.name: Vessel Impurity — General Laws (Keilim)
candidates.notes: Comprehensive laws of vessel susceptibility to impurity: what makes a vessel susceptible, minimum sizes, when vessels become pure upon breakage, and the distinction between flat and receptacle vessels across all materials

candidates.name: Hierarchy of Impurity Grades (Hishtalshelut haTumot)
candidates.notes: The graduated levels of impurity transmission — rishon, sheni, shlishi, revi'i — and which sources are av hatumah vs. derivative, as discussed extensively in Keilim ch. 1

candidates.name: Earthenware Vessels (Kelei Cheres)
candidates.notes: Specific laws unique to earthenware vessels: impurity only through airspace, not through back/outside, completion of manufacture in the kiln, minimum sizes for broken fragments

candidates.name: Wooden Vessels (Kelei Etz)
candidates.notes: Laws of wooden vessel susceptibility to impurity: flat wooden objects are pure, receptacles are susceptible; minimum sizes; when manufacture is complete; large vessels holding 40 se'ah are pure

candidates.name: Vessel Impurity by Material Type
candidates.notes: Grouping of laws specific to each vessel material — metal, leather, glass, earthenware/ovens, and cloth — and their distinct rules of susceptibility

candidates.name: General Principles of Vessel Impurity
candidates.notes: Cross-material principles governing vessel impurity: completion of manufacture, intention, connected parts, inner/outer sides, remnants, minimum sizes, and hierarchy of susceptibility

candidates.name: Liquids and Their Role in Conferring Susceptibility (Hechsher Mashkim)
candidates.notes: Laws governing which liquids render produce susceptible to impurity, including the seven primary liquids, their derivatives, flows between vessels, and bodily fluids

candidates.name: Laws of Mikveh Waters and Measures
candidates.notes: Specific mikveh laws: minimum measure of forty seah, invalidity through drawn water, categories/degrees of water sources, and living waters

candidates.name: Metal Vessels (Kelei Matachot)
candidates.notes: Laws of metal vessel impurity: susceptibility whether flat or receptacle, reversion to impurity if reforged, vessels attached to the ground are pure, named vessels vs. unnamed, specific rules for swords, needles, keys, wagons

candidates.name: Leather Vessels (Kelei Or)
candidates.notes: Laws of leather vessels susceptibility to impurity including minimum sizes, when manufacture is complete, susceptibility of hides by intention, midras impurity of various leather goods

candidates.name: Glass Vessels (Kelei Zechuchit)
candidates.notes: Unique rabbinic extension of impurity laws to glass vessels: flat glass is pure, receptacles are susceptible; breakage purifies; remanufacturing restores susceptibility; tractate Keilim ends with glass vessels

candidates.name: Impurity of Ovens and Stoves (Tum'at Tanur veKirayim)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of impurity of ovens, double stoves, and single stoves: when manufacture is complete, minimum sizes, how breakage purifies, the oven of Akhnai, protection of objects inside from impurity transmission

candidates.name: Impurity of Cloth and Garments (Tum'at Begadim)
candidates.notes: Laws specific to cloth susceptibility to impurity: minimum size of 3x3 fingerbreadths for corpse impurity, 3x3 handbreadths for midras, how remnants are treated, patches and their connection, poor men's patchwork garments (chapters 27-29)

candidates.name: Midras Impurity (Tum'at Midras)
candidates.notes: Impurity contracted by objects used for lying/sitting/riding by a zav or zavah — its distinct rules from corpse impurity, which vessels are susceptible, minimum sizes for beds and seats

candidates.name: Remnants of Broken Vessels (Gistera / Shiyarei Kelim)
candidates.notes: Laws concerning fragments of broken vessels — minimum sizes for continued susceptibility, the principle that remnants do not have remnants, when a repaired vessel reverts to its original status

candidates.name: Connected Parts of Vessels (Chibbur Kelim)
candidates.notes: When parts of a vessel are considered connected for purposes of impurity transmission — handles, plugs, coverings, ropes, staffs, plumb-lines, and other attachments; measured lengths for various implements (chapters 13, 29)

candidates.name: Inner and Outer Sides of Vessels (Penei uGevei Kelim)
candidates.notes: Distinction between inner side (susceptible by airspace) and outer side (susceptible only by contact) of vessels; when inner impurity spreads to outer and vice versa; the 'holding place' of vessels (chapter 25)

candidates.name: Completion of Manufacture of Vessels (Gemar Melacha)
candidates.notes: The principle that vessels only become susceptible to impurity upon completion of their manufacture — what constitutes completion for different vessel types (ovens, beds, baskets, leather goods, cloth)

candidates.name: Intention to Make Vessel Susceptible (Kavvanah l'Hachshir Kelim)
candidates.notes: The role of intention (as opposed to act) in rendering a vessel susceptible to impurity, and the converse — when intention can render a vessel insusceptible. Vessels become susceptible by intention but cannot be rendered insusceptible except by a change-effecting act (chapter 25-26)

candidates.name: Minimum Sizes in Laws of Vessels (Shiurei Kelim)
candidates.notes: The extensive system of minimum measurements governing vessel impurity — hole sizes that purify, minimum capacities for susceptibility, standard measures used (olive, fig, pomegranate, egg, log, se'ah), as systematized in chapter 17

candidates.name: Five Grades of Vessel Susceptibility by Material
candidates.notes: The hierarchy of vessel materials and their susceptibility: cloth (5 types), sackcloth (4), leather (3), wood (2), earthenware (1) — as enumerated in Keilim 27:1

candidates.name: Tightly Fitting Cover Protection (Tzamid Patil)
candidates.notes: Details of what materials constitute a valid tightly fitting cover, which vessel materials can protect their contents in a tent of a corpse, and minimum hole sizes that invalidate the cover — Keilim chapters 9-10

candidates.name: Riding-Upon vs. Sitting-Upon Impurity (Merkav vs. Moshav)
candidates.notes: Distinction between objects used for riding (merkav) and objects used for sitting (moshav) — practical halakhic differences in how impurity is transmitted by contact versus carrying (chapter 23)

candidates.name: Offering of a Woman after Childbirth (Korban Yoledet)
candidates.notes: Detailed rules of which types of miscarriage or birth obligate a sin offering, including sandal fetus, placenta, amniotic sac, caesarean birth; cases of uncertainty; aggregation of multiple births into one offering

candidates.name: Ki Yutan — Susceptibility to Impurity through Liquid Contact
candidates.notes: The law that produce becomes susceptible to impurity only after contact with one of seven liquids with the owner's desire/approval (Ki Yutan, Lev. 11:38). Central topic of Makhshirin covering when intent/desire renders liquid contact effective.

candidates.name: Owner's Desire/Intent as Condition for Hechsher
candidates.notes: The requirement that liquid contact renders produce susceptible to impurity only if the owner desired or approved of the wetting, whether initially or retroactively (beshaat nefila or lvasofa). The complex rules of initial vs. final desire.

candidates.name: Seven Liquids (Shiva Mashkim)
candidates.notes: The seven liquids that can render produce susceptible to impurity: dew, water, wine, oil, blood, milk, and bees' honey (M. Makhshirin 6:4). Includes distinctions between different types and their derivative status.

candidates.name: Derivatives of the Seven Liquids (Toladot Mashkim)
candidates.notes: Liquids that are derivatives of the seven primary liquids (e.g., eye discharge as derivative of water, whey as derivative of milk, olive sap as derivative of oil) and their status regarding susceptibility-conferring and impurity.

candidates.name: Human Perspiration and Its Status
candidates.notes: Rules regarding human perspiration — whether it causes susceptibility to impurity or not, and under what circumstances (e.g., perspiration after entering drawn water vs. after drying off).

candidates.name: Sweat/Condensation of Structures
candidates.notes: The condensation/sweat of houses, cisterns, ditches, and caverns and whether it causes susceptibility to impurity. Distinct from human perspiration.

candidates.name: Liquid Flow Between Vessels (Nisoach/Tziruf)
candidates.notes: Rules about whether a stream/flow of liquid connecting two vessels constitutes a connection for impurity purposes. M. Makhshirin 5:9-10 discusses flows from vessel to vessel and their clean/unclean status.

candidates.name: Legal Incapacity: Acts Without Halakhic Intent (Cheresh, Shoteh, Katan in Tumah)
candidates.hebrew: חרש שוטה וקטן — מעשיהם בלא כוונה בדיני הכשר
candidates.notes: The rule that a deaf-mute, imbecile, or minor cannot confer susceptibility to impurity through their actions because their intent/desire has no halakhic standing — 'their act counts but not their intent' (M. Makhshirin 3:8, 6:1).

candidates.name: Am HaAretz Trustworthiness in Matters of Purity
candidates.notes: Rules about when an am haaretz (common person not careful about purity laws) may be trusted to declare produce or liquids clean (M. Makhshirin 6:3).

candidates.name: Kilon (Pump-Beam) and Duration of Susceptibility
candidates.notes: Rules regarding water drawn through a kilon (pump-beam or shaduf), how long it continues to confer susceptibility to impurity (M. Makhshirin 4:9).

candidates.name: Bodily Fluids of Zav/Zavah/Niddah as Active Liquids
candidates.hebrew: משקי הזב והנידה לעניין הכשר וטומאה
candidates.notes: Specific status of the bodily fluids of a zav (flow, spittle, semen, urine) and menstrual blood: they both convey impurity and render produce susceptible to impurity regardless of desire (M. Makhshirin 6:6).

candidates.name: Blood of Slaughter as Hechsher Liquid
candidates.notes: Whether blood from slaughter of clean animals renders produce susceptible to impurity and under what conditions, including blood of clean vs. unclean animals (M. Makhshirin 6:5, 6:7).

candidates.name: Human Milk vs. Animal Milk in Purity Law
candidates.notes: The debate about whether human milk causes susceptibility regardless of desire while animal milk requires desire, with Rabbi Akiva's kal vachomer argument and the sages' responses (M. Makhshirin 6:8). A standalone halakhic discussion.

candidates.name: Nitzok (Uninterrupted Liquid Flow as Connection)
candidates.notes: Whether a continuous stream of liquid connecting a clean and unclean vessel creates a connection (Nitzok) that conveys impurity or susceptibility. M. Makhshirin 5:9 addresses the flow/stream being clean.

candidates.name: Joining of Impure Foods and Impurities to Constitute Requisite Measures
candidates.notes: Rules for combining different impure foods or items of different impurity levels to constitute requisite measures for various halakhic consequences; principle attributed to Rabbi Yehoshua

candidates.name: Shiur of Forty Seah (Mikveh Minimum Measure)
candidates.notes: The requirement that a mikveh contain at least forty seahs of valid water; debates about what happens when a mikveh is found to be lacking

candidates.name: Drawn Water Invalidating a Mikveh (Mayim She'uvim)
candidates.notes: The rule that three logs of drawn water (mayim she'uvim) invalidate a mikveh; details of when and how this applies, including cases of doubt

candidates.name: Six Degrees/Categories of Mikveh Water
candidates.notes: The hierarchy of water sources for immersion: pools, cisterns, rain flows, springs, living waters, etc., each with different purifying capacities

candidates.name: Living Waters (Mayim Chayyim)
candidates.notes: Flowing spring water (mayim chayyim) required for purification of zavim, metzoraim, and preparation of mei chatat; distinguished from mikveh water

candidates.name: Mikveh Water Composition and Validity
candidates.notes: Rules governing what types of water and liquids may constitute or supplement a mikveh, and what invalidates it

candidates.name: Signs of Tzaraat Uncleanness
candidates.notes: The specific physical signs that render a person or nega unclean: colors, white hair, quick flesh, spreading

candidates.name: Types of Bodily Tzaraat
candidates.notes: The distinct categories of tzaraat appearing on different parts or conditions of the body: skin-of-flesh, boil, burn, scall, baldness

candidates.name: Tzaraat Inspection and Isolation Procedure
candidates.notes: Procedural laws of tzaraat: how and when the priest inspects, isolation periods, and outcomes of inspection

candidates.name: Hashakah (Connecting Two Mikvaot)
candidates.notes: The halakhic mechanism of connecting two bodies of water so that valid mikveh water renders drawn water valid; minimum hole size required (tube of a water-skin)

candidates.name: Color Change Invalidating a Mikveh
candidates.notes: Whether wine, olive sap, or dye that changes the color of mikveh water invalidates it; distinction between color change and actual mixing of liquids

candidates.name: Chatzitzah on Vessels (Interposition Blocking Immersion of Utensils)
candidates.notes: Materials (pitch, myrrh, clay, etc.) that block valid immersion of vessels; distinction based on whether the owner minds the substance being there

candidates.name: Chatzitzah on Persons (Interposition Blocking Immersion of People)
candidates.notes: Materials (threads, matted hair, pus, excrement, dough, clay) that block valid immersion of persons; rule that hidden or wrinkled parts do not require water penetration

candidates.name: Requirements for Valid Immersion of Vessels
candidates.notes: Specific requirements for vessels to be validly immersed: orientation in water, handles, knots, sealed containers, water entering inside; practical rules for tefillin, sandals, water-skins

candidates.name: The Sea as Equivalent to a Mikveh
candidates.notes: Dispute whether all seas are valid as a mikveh or only the Great Sea; whether flowing seawater is valid for zavim and metzoraim

candidates.name: Retroactive Unfitness of Mikveh (Lemafrea)
candidates.notes: When a mikveh is measured and found to lack forty seahs, all prior immersions are retroactively invalid; distinction between major and minor impurity

candidates.name: Snow, Hail, and Ice in a Mikveh
candidates.notes: Whether snow, hail, frozen dew, ice, salt, and thin mud can complete the forty-seah requirement of a mikveh; they supplement but do not invalidate

candidates.name: Other Liquids in a Mikveh (Juice, Wine, Brine)
candidates.notes: Status of grape juice, wine, brine, fish brine, and grape-skin wine that fell into a mikveh; whether they can supplement the forty seahs or invalidate

candidates.name: Spring Water (Ma'ayan) — Laws and Status
candidates.notes: Spring water purifies in any quantity when flowing; distinctions between a spring and a mikveh; what happens when a spring is channeled through vessels or troughs

candidates.name: Details of Seminal Emission Impurity (Keri)
candidates.notes: Details of what constitutes keri impurity: murky urine, white viscous fluid, heated flesh after a dream, drops from the member; timing of woman's discharge after intercourse

candidates.name: Purity Status of Mikvaot in the Land of Israel vs. Diaspora
candidates.hebrew: מקוואות ארץ ישראל לעומת חוץ לארץ
candidates.notes: Land of Israel declared clean; mikvaot of gentiles outside Israel valid for keri; within Israel, location relative to city entrance affects validity for different levels of impurity

candidates.name: Adjacent Mikvaot — Pooling Together (Hibur Mikvaot)
candidates.notes: Rules for when two adjacent mikvaot are considered joined (e.g., crack in wall, hole size); how water from one renders the other valid

candidates.name: Doubtful Immersion (Safek Tevilah)
candidates.notes: Status of person when there is doubt whether they immersed, or whether the mikveh had the required measure; distinction between doubt in public vs. private domain

candidates.name: Swallowed Objects and Immersion
candidates.notes: Status of a ring or other object swallowed by a person who then immerses or enters a tent of a corpse; whether the object is purified or remains impure after being vomited up

candidates.name: Effect of Immersion on Impurity Caused by Eating Unclean Foods
candidates.notes: Foods and liquids that cause bodily unfitness requiring immersion; the combining of all liquids for the quarter-log measure; whether immersion after eating unclean food removes the impurity of the food itself

candidates.name: Orientation of Vessels During Immersion
candidates.notes: A vessel immersed with its mouth downward is not validly immersed; vessels narrow at both ends or with inward-turned mouths require special handling

candidates.name: Bathhouse Pools and Mikveh Validity
candidates.notes: Rules regarding bath basins, their outlets, and the 'purifier' pipe in a bathhouse; when drawn water in the lower pipe invalidates the valid water above

candidates.name: Tzaraat Examination on Chol HaMoed
candidates.notes: Dispute about whether a priest may examine tzaraat symptoms during Chol HaMoed; Rabbi Meir permits lenient examination but not stringent; Rabbis prohibit both

candidates.name: Marking Graves on Chol HaMoed
candidates.notes: Requirement to mark graves for public impurity awareness; inspectors going out to uproot kilayim; public welfare activities permitted on Chol HaMoed

candidates.name: Impurity of the Depths (Tumat HaTehom)
candidates.notes: Unknown impurity from a corpse buried in the depths; does not negate a nazirite's tally; distinction from known impurity.

candidates.name: High Priest and Nazirite vs. Met Mitzvah
candidates.hebrew: כהן גדול ונזיר לעומת מת מצווה
candidates.notes: Dispute whether High Priest or nazirite must tend to met mitzvah when both are present; relative sanctity and offering obligations.

candidates.name: Nazirite Who Is Also a Leper
candidates.notes: Complex interaction when nazirite also has leprosy; shaving obligations of each conflict; procedure over 120-day period.

candidates.name: Tzaraat of the Skin (Negaim — Detailed Laws)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of tzaraat on human skin: signs of uncleanness (white hair, quick flesh, spreading), inspection procedure, isolation and certification, minimum sizes, color variations, and the four principal shades of negaim

candidates.name: Signs of Tzaraat — Baheret and Se'et
candidates.notes: The four principal colors of negaim: baheret (bright white like snow), second shade of baheret (lime of Temple), se'et (egg membrane white), second shade of se'et (wool white); and their legal interactions

candidates.name: Spreading of a Nega (Pisyon)
candidates.notes: Laws governing the spreading of a tzaraat nega as a sign of uncleanness: minimum size of effective spreading, spreading to and from different types of negaim, spreading outside original sign

candidates.name: White Hair in a Nega (Se'ar Lavan)
candidates.notes: Laws of white hair as a sign of tzaraat uncleanness: minimum required, whether it causes uncleanness at the beginning or only after the nega, color requirements, length, interaction with boils and burns

candidates.name: Quick Flesh in a Nega (Michyah)
candidates.notes: Laws of quick flesh (michyah) as a sign of tzaraat: its function as a sign of uncleanness, its role in scalp and forehead baldness negaim, inability to cause uncleanness in boil/burn, its prevention of all-white cleanness

candidates.name: Inspection of Negaim by the Priest
candidates.notes: Laws governing the inspection of tzaraat: timing of inspection (days of week, hours of day), lighting conditions, bodily posture of examinee, qualifications of inspecting priest (sight), role of priest in declaring clean or unclean, inability to inspect one's own negaim

candidates.name: Isolation Periods in Tzaraat (Hesger)
candidates.notes: The one-week and two-week isolation periods for different types of negaim; rules about re-inspection, bridegroom's grace period, festival grace period, and counting the days of isolation

candidates.name: Tzaraat Spreading Over Entire Body (Hefsach)
candidates.hebrew: פרח בכולו — טהרת המצורע שפרח בו הנגע
candidates.notes: When tzaraat spreads over the entire body the person becomes clean; rules about reappearance of natural skin (ends of limbs), whether it originated in clean or unclean status, interaction with quick flesh and white hair

candidates.name: Scall Tzaraat of Head and Beard (Neteck)
candidates.notes: Specific laws of tzaraat of the head and beard (neteck/scall): signs of uncleanness are thin yellow hair and spreading (not quick flesh or white hair), protective role of black hair, shaving for inspection, two scalls side by side

candidates.name: Tzaraat of Scalp and Forehead Baldness (Karahat/Gabahat)
candidates.notes: Laws of tzaraat on scalp baldness (karahat) and forehead baldness (gabahat): definition of each area, signs of uncleanness (quick flesh and spreading), they do not combine with each other

candidates.name: Tzaraat of Boil and Burn (Shechin and Michvah)
candidates.notes: Laws of tzaraat that appears on a boil or burn: only one week isolation, only two signs (white hair and spreading), definition of boil vs. burn, scar formation, they do not combine with skin-of-flesh negaim

candidates.name: Minimum Size of a Nega (Gris — Split Bean)
candidates.notes: The minimum size required for a skin tzaraat nega to be susceptible to uncleanness: a Cilician split bean squared (36 hairs); minimum size for house negaim is two split beans; detailed calculations of relative sizes

candidates.name: Purification Ritual of the Metzora
candidates.notes: Group covering all aspects of the metzora's two-stage purification process: birds, oil, blood application, shaving, stages of purity, and sacrifices

candidates.name: Laws of Bodily Tzaraat
candidates.notes: Group covering detailed laws specific to tzaraat of the human body: exempted body parts, plucking signs, doubtful cases, color assessment, and permanently clean spots

candidates.name: Laws of the Woman Who Gave Birth
candidates.notes: Group covering detailed laws related to the yoledet: blood of purity, yoledet b'ziva, miscarried fetuses, and the afterbirth

candidates.name: Laws of Blood Stains (Ketamim)
candidates.notes: Group covering detailed laws of blood stain attribution and testing: location rules and the seven stain-removing substances

candidates.name: Body Parts Exempt from Tzaraat Uncleanness
candidates.notes: Twenty-four tips of limbs and other bodily areas that do not become unclean from quick flesh or bright spots: fingertips, toes, ear tips, nose tip, penis tip, nipples; internal body areas (inside eye, ear, nose, mouth, armpits, wrinkles, soles)

candidates.name: Plucking Signs of Tzaraat Uncleanness
candidates.notes: Prohibition of plucking out white hairs or burning quick flesh; legal consequences: if done before priest's certification the person is clean, but if after certification remains unclean; rabbinic dispute about plucking during isolation

candidates.name: Doubt in Negaim (Safek Negaim)
candidates.notes: Rules for doubtful tzaraat cases: before uncleanness established, doubt is treated as clean; after uncleanness established, doubt treated as unclean; specific cases of two men whose negaim may have spread to each other

candidates.name: Assessing Tzaraat Colors Relative to Skin Tone
candidates.hebrew: ראיית נגעים לפי גוון עור הנבדק
candidates.notes: Dispute about how to assess brightness of negaim on very dark or very light-skinned individuals; Rabbi Akiva's painter analogy; Rabbi Judah and Sages' positions on using standard intermediate skin tone as reference

candidates.name: Bright Spots That Are Permanently Clean
candidates.notes: Categories of negaim that are permanently clean and not subject to inspection: present before the Torah was given, present when a convert converted, present at birth, hidden in a crease and later revealed, on areas that later became boil scars

candidates.name: Purification Ritual of the Metzora (Overview)
candidates.notes: The two-stage purification process for a healed metzora: first-day ritual with two birds, cedarwood, hyssop, scarlet wool, living water, and earthenware vessel; second shaving on day seven; eighth-day sacrifices (guilt offering, sin offering, burnt offering)

candidates.name: Two Birds of the Metzora Purification
candidates.notes: Laws of the two birds used in metzora purification: must be wild birds, matched in appearance and price, purchased at same time; one slaughtered over living water in earthenware vessel, the other released into open field; what happens if one dies or is found non-kosher

candidates.name: Log of Oil in Metzora Purification
candidates.notes: The log of oil used in metzora purification: sprinkling toward Holy of Holies seven times, application to ear, thumb, and big toe over guilt-offering blood, application of remainder to head; dispute about necessity of 'putting upon' the head for atonement; replenishment if oil is missing

candidates.name: Application of Guilt-Offering Blood to Metzora
candidates.notes: Procedure for applying guilt-offering blood to the metzora's right ear tip, right thumb, and right big toe; the metzora immersed in the chamber of metzoraim and stood at the Nikanor gate; dispute if limbs are missing

candidates.name: Shaving of the Metzora
candidates.notes: Two required shavings of the metzora: first shaving (all hair) on day one of purification, second shaving on day seven; razor over entire body; same shaving rules apply to nazirite and Levites; invalidity if not done with razor or if two hairs remain

candidates.name: Stages of Metzora's Progressive Purification
candidates.notes: Three progressive stages of the metzora's purification: after first-day ritual (clean re: entry but impure like sheretz); after second shaving on day seven (clean re: sheretz but like tevul yom, may eat maaser sheni); after eighth-day offerings (may eat kodashim)

candidates.name: Conduct of the Metzora During Impurity
candidates.notes: Rules governing the metzora while impure: conveys uncleanness to all vessels in a house up to the roof beams; must have partition in synagogue; cannot enter within walls of Jerusalem while impure; forbidden from intercourse during intermediate stage of purification

candidates.name: Rich vs. Poor Metzora's Sacrifices
candidates.notes: Difference between rich and poor metzora's eighth-day offerings: rich brings two lambs and ewe; poor brings two birds; if status changes between diagnosis and offering, dispute whether guilt-offering or sin-offering determines status; a man may bring rich sacrifice for family members

candidates.name: Detailed Laws of Tzaraat in Garments
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of garment tzaraat: which garments are susceptible (wool, linen, hides; not sea-hides unless combined with land material); mixed wool/camel hair thresholds; colored garments; warp and woof susceptibility; isolation, washing, burning; patching procedures; mixing up isolated vs. certified garments

candidates.name: Detailed Laws of Tzaraat in Houses (Nigei Batim)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws: which houses are susceptible (four-sided, containing stones/wood/earth; not round, triangular, ship-built, non-Jewish houses); minimum number of stones; inspection procedure; isolation, scraping, replastering, demolition; stones from isolated house used elsewhere; uncleanness by entry

candidates.name: Uncleanness Conveyed by Entering a Leprous House
candidates.notes: Laws of entering a house certified as having tzaraat: immediate uncleanness; clothing worn remains clean unless stayed long enough to eat half a loaf; clothing carried on shoulders becomes unclean immediately; head and majority of body inside constitutes entry; metzora entering causes all vessels to become unclean

candidates.name: Who is Susceptible to Tzaraat Uncleanness
candidates.notes: All persons may become impure from tzaraat except non-Jews and resident aliens (gerim toshavim); non-Jewish garments and houses not susceptible; a convert's pre-conversion negaim are clean; all may inspect negaim but only a priest may declare clean or unclean

candidates.name: Bridegroom and Festival Exemption from Tzaraat Inspection
candidates.notes: A bridegroom whose nega appears during the seven days of the marriage feast receives a grace period before inspection; similarly during a festival all days of the festival constitute a grace period; applies to him, his house, and his clothing

candidates.name: Hyssop (Eizov) in Purification Rituals
candidates.notes: The hyssop used in the metzora purification: must be standard hyssop without a qualifying name (not ezovyon, blue hyssop, Roman hyssop, wild hyssop); minimum size; bound together with cedarwood and scarlet wool

candidates.name: Cedarwood (Eitz Erez) in Purification Rituals
candidates.notes: The cedarwood used in metzora purification: minimum one cubit in length, quarter of a bed-leg in thickness; bound with hyssop and scarlet wool

candidates.name: Fixed Menstrual Cycle (Veset Kavua)
candidates.notes: Laws of a woman who has established a fixed menstrual cycle — her time is sufficient and she does not transmit impurity retroactively; how a veset is established after three occurrences

candidates.name: Body-Sensation Menstrual Cycle (Veset HaGuf)
candidates.notes: Fixed menstrual cycles established through bodily sensations such as yawning, sneezing, stomach pain, or shuddering rather than calendar-based patterns

candidates.name: Blood of Virginity (Dam Besulim)
candidates.notes: Halakhic status of blood discharged when the hymen is ruptured during first intercourse — dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel regarding how long such blood is attributed to the torn hymen and remains pure

candidates.name: Four Women Whose Time is Sufficient
candidates.notes: The four categories of women (virgin, pregnant, nursing, elderly) who do not transmit impurity retroactively — dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua

candidates.name: Blood of Purity (Dam Tohar)
