candidates.notes: Blood seen by a woman during the days of purity following childbirth (33 or 66 days), which is ritually pure and does not render her impure; disputes about her status with regard to teruma and Temple entry

candidates.name: Woman Who Gives Birth as a Zava (Yoledet b'Ziva)
candidates.notes: A woman who experienced three days of ziva-type bleeding during labor and then gave birth; she must observe seven clean days in addition to the birth-related impurity period

candidates.name: Miscarried Fetuses and Discharges (Nefalim)
candidates.notes: Rules governing various forms of miscarriage or abnormal discharge — gestational sacs, sandal-shaped fetuses, tissue, flesh — and whether they trigger yoledet impurity periods

candidates.name: Afterbirth (Shilya)
candidates.notes: Halakhic status of the afterbirth — whether it triggers yoledet impurity and whether a house containing an afterbirth is rendered impure due to the assumption that an offspring was present within it

candidates.name: Blood Stain Attribution and Location Rules
candidates.notes: Detailed rules about where on the body or garment a blood stain was found determines impurity; ability to attribute stains to wounds, lice, other women's blood, or gentile sources; location relative to the body determines whether blood could have originated in the uterus

candidates.name: Seven Stain-Removing Substances (Shiva Ikurin)
candidates.notes: The seven substances (tasteless saliva, split bean liquid, urine, natron, borit, Cimolian earth, potash) used to test whether a stain is blood or dye; rules about their order of application

candidates.name: Impurity Transmitted by Infant on Day of Birth
candidates.notes: A baby boy even one day old conveys full halakhic status — transmits corpse impurity, creates levirate bonds, enables or disqualifies mother from teruma; one who kills him is liable

candidates.name: Ritual Impurity of Samaritans (Kutim)
candidates.notes: Samaritan women deemed as menstruating from cradle; Samaritan men deemed as those who engage in intercourse with menstruating women; their garments and bedding transmit impurity accordingly; credibility of Samaritans in certain testimony

candidates.name: Blood of a Gentile Woman
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel about whether blood of a gentile woman transmits impurity; Hillel holds it is like her saliva and urine, transmitting impurity only while moist

candidates.name: Beit HaPeras Impurity Rules
candidates.notes: Specific rules about beit haperas and credibility of Samaritan testimony regarding graves; area of 100 cubits considered impure due to dispersal of bones by plow

candidates.name: Impurity of Blood Discharged from a Corpse
candidates.notes: A quarter-log of blood emerging from a woman's corpse transmits impurity both as menstrual blood and as corpse blood (tent impurity); dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbis about whether post-mortem discharge transmits menstrual impurity

candidates.name: Components and Minimum Quantities of Corpse Impurity
candidates.notes: Group covering the various physical components of a corpse and their minimum quantities that convey impurity

candidates.name: Mechanics of Tent Impurity (Hilkhot Ohel)
candidates.notes: Group covering the structural and halakhic mechanics of how tents spread, block, or transmit corpse impurity

candidates.name: Types of Beit HaPras Fields
candidates.notes: Group covering the three types of impure fields: plowed-over grave, lost grave, and kokhin field

candidates.name: Examination Cloths and Intercourse Examinations
candidates.notes: Use of examination cloths before and after intercourse; disputes between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel about frequency of examination; the modest women's practice of using a third cloth

candidates.name: Parable of the House — Uterine Anatomy in Purity Law
candidates.notes: The rabbinic model of female anatomy using the metaphor of inner room (uterus), corridor (vaginal canal), and upper story (bladder); determining the source of blood found in the corridor

candidates.name: Colors of Impure Menstrual Blood (Chamisha Damim)
candidates.notes: The five (or seven, per Beit Shammai) colors of blood that render a woman impure as a niddah; red, black, crocus, earth-water, diluted wine; specific standards for each color

candidates.name: Seven Clean Days of Zav and Zava
candidates.notes: Requirements for counting seven clean days before purification; examination obligations on each day; dispute between Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yehoshua, and Rabbi Akiva about what constitutes sufficient examination

candidates.name: Impurity Status After Caesarean Birth
candidates.notes: A child born by caesarean section (yotzei dofen) — the mother does not observe the standard days of impurity and purity for childbirth; dispute with Rabbi Shimon

candidates.name: Impurity Begins Upon Internal Flow (Hargashat Davar)
candidates.notes: Women become impure when blood flows into the vaginal canal even before leaving the body; contrast with zav and baal keri who become impure only when emission exits the body

candidates.name: Impurity Transmission When Moist vs. Dry
candidates.notes: Rules about which impure substances transmit impurity when dry as well as when moist (menstrual blood, corpse flesh) vs. those that transmit impurity only when moist (ziva discharge, saliva, semen, sheretz); soaking test to determine restorability

candidates.name: Yoledet Impurity for Tumtum and Hermaphrodite Births
candidates.notes: A woman who gives birth to a tumtum or hermaphrodite observes combined stringencies of male and female birth; impurity for 14 days but blood of purity for only 33 additional days

candidates.name: Samaritan House of Impurity (Beit HaTumah)
candidates.notes: The room used by Samaritan women during menstruation transmits tent-impurity like a corpse due to stillborn children buried there; dispute between Rabbi Yehuda who denies this

candidates.name: Labor Blood Does Not Constitute Ziva Blood
candidates.notes: Blood emitted during labor pains is not counted as blood of ziva; disputes about how far in advance of birth labor blood exemption applies (2 weeks per R. Yosi/Shimon, 1 month per R. Yehuda, up to 40-50 days per R. Meir)

candidates.name: Eleven Days Between Menstrual Periods (Yemei Ziva)
candidates.hebrew: אחד עשר ימי בין נידה לנידה
candidates.notes: The eleven-day period between menstrual cycles during which blood emissions are classified as ziva rather than niddah; significance for counting clean days and bringing offerings

candidates.name: Attribution of Blood Found on Shared Bench or Bed
candidates.hebrew: ייחוס כתם שנמצא על ספסל ומיטה משותפת
candidates.notes: Rules for attributing blood stains found on a bench or bed used by multiple women; all are impure unless one examined herself and found blood; stone and bathhouse benches not susceptible to impurity and therefore blood stains on them do not render users impure (Rabbi Nechemya)

candidates.name: Ohel (Tent) as Vehicle of Corpse Impurity
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of how a tent/covering spreads or blocks corpse impurity, including minimum sizes, slopes, partial coverings, and configurations of structures

candidates.name: Minimum Quantities for Corpse Impurity (Shiurei Tumat Met)
candidates.notes: Specific minimum quantities that convey corpse impurity: olive-size of flesh, quarter-kav of bones, quarter-log of blood, ladleful of corpse mold, etc.

candidates.name: Nezel (Corpse Fluid)
candidates.notes: The fluid that drains from a decomposing corpse and its role in transmitting impurity

candidates.name: Afar Kuvarim (Grave Dust / Corpse Mold)
candidates.notes: Dust or mold from a decomposed corpse and its minimum quantity (ladleful) for conveying impurity

candidates.name: Dam HaMet (Blood of a Corpse)
candidates.notes: Blood of a corpse that conveys impurity, including mixed blood (dam tarbut), minimum quantity of quarter-log, and distinctions between blood that flowed during life vs. after death

candidates.name: Limbs from a Corpse (Evarim min HaMet)
candidates.notes: Laws of whole limbs severed from a corpse or from a living person and how they convey impurity; the 248 limbs of the human body and their required flesh content

candidates.name: Spreading and Blocking of Corpse Impurity (Mevi and Chotzetz)
candidates.notes: Objects and structures that spread (mevi) corpse impurity to other spaces vs. those that block (chotzetz) its transmission; requires one cubic handbreadth space

candidates.name: One Cubic Handbreadth (Tefach Murbah) as Threshold for Impurity
candidates.notes: The minimum space of one cubic handbreadth (tefach al tefach b'rum tefach) that constitutes a halakhic 'tent' for purposes of corpse impurity

candidates.name: Sealed Vessel Protecting Contents in Ohel (Tzamid Patil b'Ohel)
candidates.notes: Earthenware vessel sealed with a tight-fitting lid protecting its contents from corpse impurity inside a tent; dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel

candidates.name: Bet HaPeras (Field with Plowed Grave)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of a field made impure by plowing over a grave, its dimensions (100 cubits furrow), types (plowed grave, lost grave, kokhin field), purification methods, and examination procedures

candidates.name: Field in Which a Grave Was Lost (Sadeh sheNiavad Kever)
candidates.notes: A field in which a grave has been lost, distinguished from a plowed-over grave field; may be sown but not planted, transmits impurity by overshadowing

candidates.name: Kokhin Field (Sadeh Kokhin)
candidates.notes: A field used for burial niches (kokhin); may neither be planted nor sown, but its earth is considered clean for use in making ovens for sacred purposes

candidates.name: Impurity of the Land of the Nations (Tumat Eretz HaAmim)
candidates.notes: Rabbinic decree that lands of non-Jews convey impurity; detailed rules about travel over such lands, purchasing fields in Syria, and how this interacts with terumah and shemitah obligations

candidates.name: Impurity of Non-Jewish Dwellings (Tumat Ohel Nochrim)
candidates.notes: Rabbinic decree that dwellings of non-Jews are impure due to presumption that fetuses were buried beneath them; requires examination after 40 days of habitation

candidates.name: Finding Multiple Corpses and Establishing a Graveyard
candidates.notes: Laws governing discovery of corpses in a field: finding one may be removed, finding three within a space of a bier and bearers (4-8 cubits) establishes a graveyard requiring 20-cubit search

candidates.name: Opening of the Grave/Womb (Pesicat HaKever)
candidates.notes: The concept of the womb opening during childbirth creating impurity like a grave opening; stillborn children and the point at which the womb is considered 'opened'

candidates.name: Impurity Goes Out but Does Not Go In (Darkah Latzet v'Lo Lavo)
candidates.notes: Halakhic principle that corpse impurity naturally spreads outward from its source, so a sealed inner space may protect against outside impurity but not against impurity within it

candidates.name: Garlic Skin Principle (Klipat HaShum)
candidates.notes: A covering as thin as garlic skin can block corpse impurity if there is a space of one cubic handbreadth beneath it; used in cases of covering over drains, pillars, and wall spaces

candidates.name: Objects That Convey vs. Block Impurity (Mevi u'Chotzetz)
candidates.notes: Classification of objects into: those that both convey and block impurity, those that convey but don't block, those that block but don't convey, and those that neither convey nor block

candidates.name: Chain of Defilement from Corpse (Shelshelel HaTumah)
candidates.notes: The graduated chain of corpse impurity transmission: first-degree (corpse itself), persons and vessels touching it receive 7-day impurity, subsequent generations receive evening-only impurity; the maximum chain length

candidates.name: Bone the Size of a Barleycorn (Etzem k'Seorah)
candidates.notes: Minimum bone fragment (barleycorn size) that conveys corpse impurity by contact and carrying but not by overshadowing; disputes about divided bones

candidates.name: Majority or Structural Majority of a Corpse's Bones
candidates.hebrew: רוב בניינו ורוב מניינו של מת
candidates.notes: The structural majority (rov binyan) or numerical majority (rov minyan, 125 bones) of a corpse's skeleton that conveys full corpse impurity including by overshadowing

candidates.name: Minimum Opening Size for Impurity Passage (Shiur Petach HaOhel)
candidates.notes: Detailed rules about minimum opening sizes (one handbreadth square, or drill-hole size) in walls, doors, windows, and ceilings that allow corpse impurity to pass through or that protect against its spread

candidates.name: Detailed Laws of Tent Impurity (Ohel)
candidates.notes: Detailed rules governing what constitutes a halakhic ohel and how impurity is conveyed or blocked through tents and enclosures

candidates.name: Laws of Mei Chatat (Purification Waters — Details)
candidates.notes: Detailed rules governing the preparation, validity, sprinkling, vessels, water fitness, and invalidating factors of the purification waters of the red heifer

candidates.name: Communal Impurity and the Paschal Lamb (Details)
candidates.hebrew: פרטי דיני טומאה הותרה בציבור בפסח
candidates.notes: Rules governing the offering and eating of the Paschal lamb when the majority of the community is ritually impure, including which types of impurity are permitted and distinctions between cases

candidates.name: Vessels Found in Uncertain Circumstances (Presumptive Purity/Impurity)
candidates.notes: Rules for the presumptive ritual status of vessels found in ambiguous locations such as near bathhouses or before Passover

candidates.name: 248 Limbs of the Human Body
candidates.notes: The enumeration of 248 limbs in the human body; each whole limb with appropriate flesh can defile by contact, carrying, and overshadowing

candidates.name: Covering Stone and Buttressing Stone of a Grave
candidates.notes: The flat stone covering a burial niche and the stone supporting it; they defile by contact and overshadowing; dispute whether they defile by carrying and whether grave dust beneath them matters

candidates.name: Projections and Balconies as Ohel (Ziz and Gessissah)
candidates.notes: Architectural projections (ziz), balconies (gessissah), and cornices extending from a wall that serve as ohel for transmitting or blocking corpse impurity; minimum width of one handbreadth

candidates.name: Tent Made by Human Action vs. Naturally Formed Tent
candidates.notes: Dispute (Rabbi Judah) whether a tent must be deliberately made by a human to qualify as a halakhic ohel, or whether naturally formed enclosures (crevices, crags) also qualify

candidates.name: Persons and Vessels as Ohel (Adam u'Kelim k'Ohel)
candidates.notes: Living persons and vessels can serve as an ohel to convey corpse impurity (e.g., pallbearers carrying a coffin) but cannot serve as an ohel to protect against impurity

candidates.name: Preparation of Mei Chatat (Mixing Ashes with Water)
candidates.notes: Rules governing the mixing of red heifer ashes with water: valid/invalid vessels, intention, work during preparation, multiple simultaneous preparations

candidates.name: Sprinkling of Mei Chatat (Haza'ah)
candidates.notes: Laws of sprinkling the purification waters: use of hyssop, valid/invalid sprinklers, intention during sprinkling, sprinkled on multiple objects, dripping water

candidates.name: Madaf Uncleanness (for Mei Chatat)
candidates.notes: Special stringency for purity of mei chatat whereby objects that are susceptible to midras are treated as if they have madaf-level uncleanness; unique to the hatat domain

candidates.name: Hyssop (Ezov) for Purification
candidates.notes: Rules for valid hyssop used in mei chatat sprinkling: species requirements, invalid named varieties, minimum quantity, stalks and buds, combination with thread and spindle-reed

candidates.name: Children Raised in Purity for Mei Chatat (Shiloah)
candidates.notes: Special institution of raising children in purity over rock-hewn courtyards to draw water from the Shiloah spring for sanctifying the mei chatat ashes

candidates.name: Work Invalidating Mei Chatat
candidates.notes: Any work performed while drawing, carrying, or mixing the hatat waters invalidates them; detailed rules about what constitutes work and exceptions

candidates.name: Stringency of Mei Chatat Purity (Middat Chumra Hapacha leKula)
candidates.notes: The paradox that those engaged with the red heifer become impure themselves even though the rite purifies others; stringencies of hatat purity that end up being lenient

candidates.name: Fitness of Water for Mei Chatat
candidates.notes: Which water sources are valid for mei chatat: living vs. drawn water, mixed waters (Jordan/Yarmuk), marsh waters, spoiled/salty water, well water with sediment

candidates.name: Vessels for Hatat Waters
candidates.notes: Rules for valid vessels to collect and hold mei chatat: earthenware, stone, dung vessels, boat; what counts as a vessel vs. not (cupped hands, wall of vessel, stopper)

candidates.name: Stone Trough for Hatat Waters
candidates.notes: Laws specific to stone troughs fixed to the ground vs. moveable, dual troughs, holes in troughs, clay rims — their status for drawing, mixing and sprinkling hatat waters

candidates.name: Defilement of Garments by Red Heifer Participants
candidates.notes: All who participate in the red heifer rite defile their garments; the paradox that the cow itself does not defile garments but those who handle it do

candidates.name: Levels of Ritual Impurity Transmission (Rishon, Sheni, Shlishi)
candidates.notes: The graded transmission of impurity from primary (av hatumah) through first, second, third degree; how liquids that become unclean defile vessels at higher degrees than their own source

candidates.name: Tightly-Fitting Cover (Tzamid Patil) for Hatat Waters
candidates.notes: Whether a tightly-fitting cover protects hatat waters from impurity; distinction between sealed water that has been prepared vs. unprepared water

candidates.name: Intention Affecting Validity of Hatat Waters
candidates.notes: Changed intention during drawing or mixing (switching from one mixture to multiple or vice versa), intending to drink hatat water, intending to store vs. pour water — effect on validity

candidates.name: Paschal Lamb in Communal Ritual Impurity (Tumah Hutrah b'Tzibur)
candidates.notes: When the majority of Israel is ritually impure and the Paschal lamb is sacrificed in impurity, including which types of impurity permit eating and which do not

candidates.name: Ritual Impurity of the Deep (Tumah b'Makom Ne'elam)
candidates.notes: Concept of tumah that was unknown to anyone and is only discovered retroactively; in context of Paschal lamb, the frontplate atones for such impurity

candidates.name: Communal Offering in State of Impurity (Rov haTzibur beTumah)
candidates.notes: When most of the community is ritually impure the Paschal lamb is offered in impurity by all, but those with non-corpse impurity (zav, zavah, niddah, yoledet) may not eat from it; distinction from minority impurity cases

candidates.name: Eight Sheratzim (Specific Creeping Animals with Impurity)
candidates.notes: The eight specific creeping animals listed in Leviticus 11 that transmit ritual impurity, distinct from other creeping animals

candidates.name: Duration of Semen's Impurity (Three Days)
candidates.notes: The derivation that a woman who discharges semen within three days of relations is ritually impure, based on the verse from Exodus 19:15

candidates.name: Ritual Purity of Spittle Found in Jerusalem
candidates.notes: Rabbinic presumption that spittle found in Jerusalem is ritually pure (except in the upper marketplace); dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei about middle vs. side of streets, with variation at Festival time

candidates.name: Vessels Found Near a Bathhouse (Ritual Purity)
candidates.hebrew: כלים הנמצאים דרך ירידה לבית המרחץ
candidates.notes: The rule that vessels found on the way into a bathhouse are presumed impure and those on the way out are pure; exception for grave-digging tools

candidates.name: Knife Found Before Passover (Presumption of Purity)
candidates.notes: Rules for knives and cleavers found on the 13th or 14th of Nisan regarding presumed ritual purity and whether immersion is required

candidates.name: Legal Status of a Beehive (Kaveret)
candidates.notes: Debate whether a beehive is considered like land (not susceptible to tumah, prozbul security, Shabbat liability) or like a movable vessel; dispute between R. Eliezer and Sages

candidates.name: Awareness of Impurity in Defiling Temple or Sacrificial Food (Yediot HaTumah)
candidates.notes: Detailed rules about whether awareness existed at beginning/end of transgression and how this affects liability for sliding-scale offering — Shevuot ch. 1-2

candidates.name: Degrees of Food Uncleanness (Rishon, Sheni, Shlishi)
candidates.notes: The graduated system of food impurity: first, second, third (and fourth for kodesh), how they interact, combine, and are transmitted; central topic of Taharot tractate

candidates.name: Combination of Foods for Minimum Measure (Tziruf)
candidates.notes: Rules for combining different pieces of food to meet the minimum bulk (egg-size) required for conveying or contracting impurity, including foods of different grades

candidates.name: Doubtful Impurity in Private vs. Public Domain
candidates.hebrew: ספק טומאה ברשות היחיד ורשות הרבים
candidates.notes: The fundamental rule that doubtful impurity in a private domain is deemed unclean while in a public domain it is deemed clean; distinctions between domains for purposes of impurity law

candidates.name: Am HaAretz and Chaver in Laws of Purity
candidates.notes: Rules governing the presumed impurity of an am haaretz and the effect of leaving objects in their possession; the chaver's practices of purity and their interaction with am haaretz

candidates.name: Susceptibility to Impurity of Olives and Grapes
candidates.notes: When olives and grapes become susceptible to impurity through their liquids during pressing; debates between Bet Shammai and Bet Hillel on the stages of preparation

candidates.name: Neveilah of a Clean Bird (Neveilat Of HaTahor)
candidates.notes: Special impurity rules for the carcass of a clean bird: intention requirement, gullet defilement, sanctuary entry guilt, terumah burning, and effect of slaughtering or melikah

candidates.name: Netilat Yadayim and Tumat Yadayim (Hand Washing and Hand Impurity)
candidates.notes: Cluster covering the rabbinic institution of ritual hand washing and the decree of hand impurity, including procedures, doubts, and the defilement of hands by sacred scrolls

candidates.name: Laws of the Zav (Tractate Zavim)
candidates.notes: Detailed sub-topics from Tractate Zavim covering examination, counting, grades of impurity, and modes of transmission specific to the zav

candidates.name: Liquids as Conveyors and Connectors of Impurity
candidates.notes: Rules about liquids serving as connectors (tziruf) between objects for impurity transmission; flow between vessels, dripping moisture as connective; outer surfaces of vessels and liquids

candidates.name: Doubtful Contact with Sheretz
candidates.notes: Rules for doubtful contact with a dead sheretz in public and private domains, including moving sheretz, weasel carrying sheretz, and sheretz found in various contexts

candidates.name: Status of Impurity Determined at Time of Discovery
candidates.notes: Principle that all cases of doubtful impurity are assessed according to their condition at the time they are found (e.g., needle found rusty is clean)

candidates.name: Testimony and Witness Credibility in Impurity Cases
candidates.notes: Rules on when one or two witnesses are believed regarding impurity, including conflict between witnesses, self-testimony, and testimony of women in purity contexts

candidates.name: Midras Impurity from Am HaAretz
candidates.notes: Clothes and objects left with or exposed to an am haaretz are presumed to have midras (pressure) impurity; rules for deposits with am haaretz

candidates.name: Beit HaPras Doubtful Impurity Cases
candidates.notes: Among the six doubtful impurity cases for which terumah is burned; the specific rules of beit hapras as a source of doubtful corpse impurity

candidates.name: Purity Standards in Olive Press and Wine Press
candidates.notes: Detailed rules for maintaining purity during olive and grape pressing; workers' movements, trusted/untrusted persons, cleansing of press vessels

candidates.name: Designation as Food (Machshavah) for Susceptibility to Impurity
candidates.notes: Whether designation (intention) for human consumption renders an object susceptible to food impurity; role of intent vs. act in making food susceptible; deaf-mute and minor's intention

candidates.name: Tevul Yom (Immersed That Day — Detailed Laws)
candidates.notes: The existing 'tevul_yom' entry is minimal; this tractate covers the full halakhic status of the tevul yom — their degree of impurity (third grade), what they disqualify vs. render impure, and how they interact with terumah, hullin, and kodashim.

candidates.name: Connection of Foods (Chibbur/Tziruf) for Impurity Purposes
candidates.notes: Whether foods stuck together, batter-cakes joined in baking, froth, scum, or liquids floating on other liquids serve as connectives (mitzaref/mechubar) for purposes of transmitting impurity from a tevul yom or other impure sources.

candidates.name: Nitzok (Stream of Poured Liquid as Connective)
candidates.notes: Whether a stream of liquid poured from one vessel to another serves as a connective for transmitting impurity between them; discussed in context of tevul yom touching the stream.

candidates.name: Yad (Handle) of Food for Impurity
candidates.notes: Handles or stems of food that serve as connectives for impurity transmission — when the handle is touched by an impure person or tevul yom, whether the food itself becomes impure.

candidates.name: Ashkelon Grappling-Irons and Broken Tool Susceptibility
candidates.notes: Whether broken tools (Ashkelon grappling-irons, pitchforks, rakes, combs) that retain partial functionality remain susceptible to impurity; includes the rabbinic principle introduced by the scribes referenced by Rabbi Joshua.

candidates.name: Third-Degree Impurity Clean in Hullin (Shlishi b'Hullin Tahor)
candidates.notes: The principle that an item with third-degree impurity is considered clean with respect to non-sacred (hullin) food, though it disqualifies terumah; central to Tractate Tevul Yom chapters 3-4.

candidates.name: Liquids Issuing from an Impure Person
candidates.notes: Whether liquids that issue from or are touched by an impure person (including tevul yom) acquire first-degree impurity and can render other things susceptible to impurity; dispute between Rabbi Meir and the Sages regarding tevul yom.

candidates.name: Netilat Yadayim (Ritual Hand Washing)
candidates.notes: The rabbinic requirement of ritual hand washing before meals and other activities; minimum water quantities, valid vessels, and procedures

candidates.name: Tumat Yadayim (Ritual Impurity of Hands)
candidates.notes: The rabbinic decree of second-degree impurity on hands, degrees of hand impurity, and what causes it

candidates.name: Kitvei HaKodesh Meting'im et HaYadayim (Holy Scriptures Defiling Hands)
candidates.notes: The rabbinic decree that canonical Holy Scriptures defile the hands; debates over which books (Song of Songs, Kohelet) are canonical and defile hands

candidates.name: Mayim Rishonim and Mayim Shniyim (First and Second Waters for Hand Washing)
candidates.notes: The two-stage hand washing process: first water to remove impurity, second water to clean off the first water; laws governing each stage

candidates.name: Aramaic Sections in Scripture (Defiling Hands)
candidates.notes: Status of Aramaic sections in Ezra and Daniel and their capacity to defile hands; requirement that canonical text be in Assyrian script on parchment in ink

candidates.name: Doubt Regarding Hand Impurity (Safek Yadayim)
candidates.notes: Rules for cases of doubt whether hands became impure or whether they were purified; the general leniency applied to doubts about hand impurity

candidates.name: Continuous Flow of Liquid (Hashaka / Tziruf)
candidates.notes: Dispute between Pharisees and Sadducees whether an uninterrupted stream of liquid connects two vessels for purposes of impurity transmission (nizoq)

candidates.name: Zav/Zavah — Laws of Gonorrheal Discharge
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of the zav: counting of sightings, examination for causes, threshold between one/two/three issues, distinction from keri, relationship to sacrifice obligation

candidates.name: Examination of the Zav (Bedikat haZav)
candidates.notes: Seven factors examined to determine whether a zav's discharge was caused by an external factor (food, drink, carrying, jumping, illness, sight, thought) which would exempt him from zav status

candidates.name: Hefsek in Zav Counting (Interruption Undoing Days)
candidates.notes: Rules about how an emission of semen or additional zov during the counting period undoes previous clean days; dispute between Bet Shammai and Bet Hillel

candidates.name: Mishkav and Moshav (Objects for Lying and Sitting)
candidates.notes: Special category of objects that can become midras-defiled and in turn convey second-degree impurity to persons and garments; detailed rules about which objects qualify

candidates.name: Madaf Tumah (Impurity Above the Zav)
candidates.notes: Objects resting above a zav (even without direct contact) that become defiled at a lesser grade; the madaf conveys impurity to food and liquids

candidates.name: Zav — Impurity Through Carrying and Moving
candidates.notes: Rules distinguishing defiling through carrying (masa) vs. moving (heset) a zav; who defiles whom when zav and clean person share a moving object like a boat or animal

candidates.name: Heset (Moving/Displacing Impurity)
candidates.notes: Impurity transmitted when a zav moves an object or is moved by it, even without direct contact; distinct from touch and carrying; major topic of tractate Zavim

candidates.name: Grades of Impurity — Rishon and Sheni in Zav Context
candidates.notes: Detailed treatment of first and second degree impurity conveyed by touching/carrying a zav or objects connected to him; how separation from source affects degree; disqualification of terumah at further remove

candidates.name: Drawn Water (Mayim She'uvim) Disqualifying Immersion
candidates.notes: Rule that three logs of drawn water falling on a clean person's head and majority of body disqualifies terumah; also immersing head and majority in drawn water

candidates.name: Categories That Disqualify Terumah (Posel et haTerumah)
candidates.notes: Enumerated list of those who disqualify terumah without rendering it impure outright: eating first/second degree impure food, drinking impure liquids, tevul yom, drawn water, unwashed hands, sacred scrolls, food defiled by liquids

candidates.name: Sefer (Sacred Scroll) Defiling the Hands
candidates.notes: Rabbinic ruling that sacred scripture scrolls defile the hands; listed among those who disqualify terumah

candidates.name: Immersion of Zav in Running Water (Mayanot)
candidates.notes: Requirement for a zav to immerse specifically in running spring water (mayim chayim), not just a mikvah; applies even in intermediate cases

candidates.name: Androginus and Tumtum in Laws of Zivah
candidates.notes: Rules that androginus and tumtum bear stringencies of both male and female regarding zivah: defiled by blood like a woman and by seminal-like discharge like a man; their impurity is doubtful

candidates.name: Zav on a Balance Scale
candidates.notes: Specific case: if a zav sits on one side of a balance and objects fit for sitting are on the other side; whether the objects become defiled depends on which side outweighs the other

candidates.name: Garment Impurity from Burning Communal Sin Offerings
candidates.notes: Kohanim who burn the bulls and goats that are burned outside Jerusalem render their garments impure; when this occurs and when it does not

candidates.name: Impurity of Bird Carcasses (Neveilat Of)
candidates.notes: Unique impurity of bird carcasses transmitted through swallowing (beit habeli'ah); how melikah prevents this impurity even for tereifa birds; debate between Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Yosi

candidates.name: The Five Pairs (Zugot)
candidates.notes: The five pairs of leading sages who served as Nasi and Av Beit Din in the Second Temple period; their disputes over semichah on festival offerings are recorded in Mishnah Chagigah.

candidates.name: Laws of Circumcision
candidates.notes: Grouping for detailed halakhic rules governing the performance, timing, and validity of circumcision

candidates.name: Canonicity of Biblical Books
candidates.notes: Grouping for disputes and rulings regarding which biblical books are considered sacred scripture and defile the hands

candidates.name: Whether Kohelet Defiles the Hands (Canonical Status)
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (Kohelet does not defile the hands) and Beit Hillel (it does defile the hands), regarding the canonical/sacred status of Ecclesiastes; Eduyot 5:3

candidates.name: Canonicity of Biblical Books
candidates.notes: Debates over whether certain books (Shir HaShirim, Kohelet) belong to the biblical canon; the vote at Yavneh

candidates.name: Purchase of Torah Scrolls and Sacred Objects from Gentiles
candidates.notes: Prohibition against paying above market value to purchase Torah scrolls, tefillin, or mezuzot from gentiles to prevent increased theft; Gittin 4:6

candidates.name: Shape and Placement of Tefillin
candidates.notes: Round tefillin are invalid; placement on forehead (not above hairline) or palm (not bicep) are ways of heretics; gold-plated or worn on outside of sleeve are ways of outsiders

candidates.name: Greatness of Circumcision (Gedulat haMilah)
candidates.notes: Aggadic and halakhic enumerations of the greatness of circumcision — overrides Shabbat, overrides tzaraat, 13 covenants, Moses punished for delay, Abraham called wholehearted only after circumcision

candidates.name: Circumcision Overriding Shabbat
candidates.notes: Laws of how circumcision at its appointed time overrides Shabbat, what preparations may be made on Shabbat, and when the override applies

candidates.name: Timing of Circumcision (Zman Milah)
candidates.notes: Laws governing when circumcision is performed — eighth day, ninth, tenth, eleventh, or twelfth day — based on birth circumstances, illness, and Shabbat/Festival coincidence

candidates.name: Shreds that Invalidate Circumcision (Tzitzin HaMeakvin)
candidates.notes: Which remaining flesh shreds invalidate a circumcision and require correction, and the requirement to uncover the corona membrane (priah)

candidates.name: Laws of Melachot on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: Cluster covering the various permitted and prohibited labors specific to Yom Tov, including food preparation, slaughter, hunting, fire, sorting, and related principles

candidates.name: Melachot on Yom Tov (Permitted and Prohibited Labors)
candidates.notes: The specific labors permitted or prohibited on Yom Tov, including the principle that only food preparation is permitted, and the distinctions from Shabbat

candidates.name: Ochel Nefesh (Food Preparation on Yom Tov)
candidates.notes: The halakhic principle permitting food-related labors on Yom Tov; the scope and limits of what counts as food preparation

candidates.name: Slaughtering Animals on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: Rules governing the slaughter of animals on Yom Tov, including the requirement that enough time remain to eat from the animal, and treatment of firstborn animals and animals in danger of dying

candidates.name: Hunting and Trapping on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: Prohibition of trapping fish, animals, and birds on Yom Tov; rules for taking animals from enclosures (beivarim)

candidates.name: Taking Doves from a Dovecote on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: Specific rules for taking fledgling doves from a dovecote on Yom Tov; disputes about pre-designation and moving ladders

candidates.name: Selecting/Sorting (Borer) on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: Rules for separating food from refuse (legumes, etc.) on Yom Tov; which tools and methods are permitted

candidates.name: Producing Fire on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: Prohibition of producing new fire on Yom Tov (from wood, stones, tiles, water vessels); only transferring existing fire is permitted

candidates.name: Kindling Fire on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: The dispute whether kindling fire on Yom Tov is permitted for non-food purposes such as heating water for washing feet; Beit Shammai vs. Beit Hillel

candidates.name: Shinui (Performing Actions in an Unusual Manner) on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: The principle of performing certain actions on Yom Tov in an unusual manner (shinui) to distinguish them from weekday activities; e.g., pounding spices, sharpening knives, transporting goods

candidates.name: Weighing and Measuring on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: Prohibition of weighing and measuring in a commercial manner on Yom Tov; permitted alternatives using unconventional methods

candidates.name: Domestic vs. Desert Animals on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: Distinction between domestic animals (sleeping in city) and desert animals (sleeping in pasture) with respect to slaughter and watering on Yom Tov

candidates.name: Insulating Hot Food on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: The prohibition of insulating food on Yom Tov for Shabbat ab initio; Rabban Gamliel's stringency in this area

candidates.name: Egg Laid on Yom Tov (Nolad)
candidates.notes: The specific dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel regarding an egg laid on Yom Tov; the classic case of nolad on Yom Tov

candidates.name: Preparation for Yom Tov (Hachanah)
candidates.notes: The requirement to prepare items before Yom Tov begins; designation of animals, produce, and other items for Festival use

candidates.name: Muktzeh on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: Application of muktzeh rules on Yom Tov; items not designated before the Festival such as undomesticated animals, scattered wood, and dead animals

candidates.name: Shevut on Yom Tov (Rabbinic Prohibitions)
candidates.notes: Rabbinic decrees (shevut) that apply equally on Yom Tov as on Shabbat, including climbing trees, riding animals, clapping, dancing, and various mitzva-related acts

candidates.name: Techum on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: Travel boundary restrictions on Yom Tov; how they apply to people, animals, vessels, borrowed objects, produce, and water

candidates.name: Feet of the Owner (Regel BeAlim / Kedei Raglo)
candidates.notes: The principle that objects follow the Shabbat/Yom Tov travel limits of their owner; governs animals, vessels, borrowed items, produce, water, and gifts

candidates.name: Animals Transferred Between Domains on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: The principle that animals follow the Shabbat limits of their owner; implications for borrowed animals and those given to shepherds

candidates.name: Sending Gifts and Portions on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: The halakhot of sending gifts of food and live animals to others on Yom Tov; the dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel

candidates.name: Karpef (Enclosed Storage Area)
candidates.notes: An enclosed area near a city used for storage; halakhic status regarding handling scattered wood and other muktzeh items on Yom Tov

candidates.name: Beivarim (Animal Enclosures)
candidates.notes: Enclosures containing animals, fish, or birds; halakhic status of taking from such enclosures on Yom Tov — whether it constitutes hunting

candidates.name: Cooking on Yom Tov for Shabbat
candidates.notes: The prohibition of cooking on Yom Tov for the following Shabbat without an eruv tavshilin; the institution of eruv tavshilin to permit this

candidates.name: Second Day of Yom Tov (Yom Tov Sheni shel Galuyot)
candidates.notes: Implicit context in tractate Beitzah regarding consecutive days of Yom Tov and Shabbat; the institution of the second festival day in the diaspora

candidates.name: Details of the Havdalah Ceremony
candidates.notes: Cluster covering the specific blessings, their order, and the candle blessing within the havdalah ceremony, as disputed by Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel

candidates.name: Havdalah Blessings and Their Order
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel on the order of candle, spices, Grace after Meals, and havdalah blessings; also the exact wording of the candle blessing

candidates.name: Blessing over Fire/Candle at Havdalah
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (bara, past tense) and Beit Hillel (boreh, present tense) for the candle blessing; prohibition against blessing over gentile fire, fire for the dead, or fire of idolatry

candidates.name: Havdalah in the Amida
candidates.notes: Dispute between Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Eliezer regarding in which blessing of the Amida havdalah is inserted

candidates.name: Order of Kiddush Blessings
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel whether the blessing over wine or over the day comes first in kiddush

candidates.name: Etrog's Halakhic Classification
candidates.notes: The etrog is compared to both a tree and a vegetable — implications for orlah, revai, shemitah, and tithing by harvest time vs. growth time

candidates.name: Simchat Yom Tov (Rejoicing on the Festival)
candidates.notes: Obligation to rejoice on pilgrimage festivals through peace-offerings; how priests and Israelites fulfill the obligation of rejoicing differently; what foods qualify for simcha.

candidates.name: Use of Demai for Eruv
candidates.notes: Permissibility of using demai produce for eruv chatzeirot and shitufei mevo'ot; reciting blessings and zimmun over demai

candidates.name: Conditional Intercalation of the Year
candidates.notes: Testimony that a year may be intercalated conditionally, pending approval by a leader; case of Rabban Gamliel who approved upon return from Syria; Eduyot 7:7

candidates.name: Intercalation Throughout the Entire Month of Adar
candidates.notes: Testimony that the year may be intercalated throughout all of Adar, not only until Purim; Eduyot 7:7

candidates.name: Lechi (Side Post for Alleyway)
candidates.notes: The side post used to render an alleyway fit for carrying on Shabbat; distinct from the cross beam (korah); rules about its minimum dimensions and construction

candidates.name: Korah (Cross Beam for Alleyway)
candidates.notes: The cross beam placed over the entrance of an alleyway to permit carrying; rules about its minimum width, strength, height, and material

candidates.name: Mechitzot and Partition Laws (for Eruvin)
candidates.notes: Laws governing valid partitions for creating Shabbat domains, including structural principles such as lavud, tzurat hapetach, and breach rules

candidates.name: Measurement and Calculation of Techum Shabbat
candidates.notes: Technical rules for measuring the Shabbat limit: rope length, terrain adjustments, city boundary squaring, karpef buffer, and city outline extension

candidates.name: Water and Domain Rules on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Specific domain and carrying issues related to water: drawing water, pouring waste water, balconies over water, and partition requirements

candidates.name: Rescuing Sacred Objects on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Laws governing the rescue of sacred writings and phylacteries found in the public domain on Shabbat, including carrying methods and rabbinic leniencies

candidates.name: Megillah Reading — Laws and Requirements
candidates.notes: Laws governing when, where, and how the Megillah is read, including walled vs. unwalled cities, advancing to day of assembly, and writing requirements

candidates.name: Passei Biraot (Boards Around a Well)
candidates.notes: The rabbinic enactment permitting upright corner boards (deyomadin) arranged around a public well to create a virtual partition, enabling drawing water on Shabbat

candidates.name: Deyomadin (Corner Posts Around a Well)
candidates.notes: The L-shaped double corner posts used in pairs to construct the virtual partition around a well; their minimum dimensions and spacing requirements

candidates.name: Tzurat HaPetach (Form of a Doorway)
candidates.notes: Two vertical posts with a horizontal beam spanning them, serving as a valid halakhic partition or entrance marker for eruvin purposes

candidates.name: Mechitzot (Partitions for Shabbat Domains)
candidates.notes: The laws of valid partitions for creating Shabbat domains, including minimum height (10 handbreadths), construction from various materials, lavud principle, and breach rules

candidates.name: Breach in a Wall or Partition on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Rules about when a breach invalidates a partition: breaches up to 10 cubits treated as doorways; breaches over 10 cubits invalidating the domain

candidates.name: Lavud (Constructive Connection of Gaps)
candidates.notes: The halakhic principle that gaps of less than 3 handbreadths between surfaces are treated as closed/connected; applied to partitions in eruvin

candidates.name: Eruv Techumin (Joining of Shabbat Boundaries)
candidates.notes: The eiruv that allows extension of the Shabbat limit by depositing food at a chosen location before Shabbat, establishing one's 'residence' there; distinct from eruv chatzeirot

candidates.name: Conditional Eruv (Eiruv Al Tenai)
candidates.notes: The ability to establish an eruv with a condition, choosing which direction the eruv will take effect based on circumstances; rules and limits of such conditions

candidates.name: Two Days of Yom Tov — Eruv Considerations
candidates.notes: The dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbis about establishing separate eruvin for each of two consecutive days of Yom Tov or Yom Tov adjacent to Shabbat

candidates.name: Shituf Mevo'ot (Merging of Alleyways)
candidates.notes: The specific procedures, measures, and food requirements for merging courtyards that open into a shared alleyway; how it relates to eruv chatzeirot

candidates.name: Renunciation of Domain Rights (Bitul Reshut)
candidates.notes: The act by which a resident who forgot to participate in an eruv renounces his domain rights in the courtyard to allow the others to carry; rules about timing and effect

candidates.name: Renting Domain from Gentile for Eruv
candidates.notes: The requirement to rent the rights of a gentile or non-observant resident in a shared courtyard in order to permit carrying there via eruv

candidates.name: Shabbat Residence in Courtyard (Shevisah b'Chatzar)
candidates.notes: The concept that a person's Shabbat residence is established in his home and courtyard, forming the basis for eruv chatzeirot; interaction between house, courtyard and alleyway domains

candidates.name: Measurement of Shabbat Limit (Middot Techum)
candidates.notes: The technical rules for measuring the 2000-cubit Shabbat limit: use of 50-cubit rope, treatment of hills and valleys, squaring the city, extending the city boundary (karpef)

candidates.name: City Boundary Extension for Shabbat (Tzurat HaIr)
candidates.notes: Rules for extending the outline of a city to include protrusions, turrets, and remnants of walls before measuring the Shabbat limit; squaring the city to gain corners

candidates.name: Karpef Addition to City Boundary
candidates.notes: The additional 70-cubit buffer added around every city before measuring the Shabbat limit; how this combines two adjacent towns into one for techum purposes

candidates.name: Shabbat Limit for One Taken Out Involuntarily
candidates.notes: Rules for one taken outside the Shabbat limit by gentiles or mental illness: whether he retains only 4 cubits or regains his original limit upon return

candidates.name: Acquisition of Shabbat Residence While Asleep or Unaware
candidates.notes: Dispute whether a sleeping or unaware person automatically acquires a Shabbat residence at his location or requires only 4 cubits (Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri vs. Rabbis)

candidates.name: Alleyway (Mavoy) — Eruv Laws
candidates.notes: The halakhic definition of a mavoy (alleyway), its structural requirements for carrying, and interaction between eruv chatzeirot and shituf mevo'ot

candidates.name: Gezuztra (Balcony) — Shabbat Domain
candidates.notes: Rules about balconies overhanging water or public domains and drawing water through holes on Shabbat; partition requirements for balconies

candidates.name: Drawing Water on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Specific rules governing drawing water from cisterns, channels, or wells on Shabbat, including partition requirements and domain considerations

candidates.name: Pouring Waste Water on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Laws about pouring waste water into a small courtyard or public domain on Shabbat; requirement for a pit, minimum courtyard size of 4 cubits

candidates.name: Carrying Between Domains (Transfer of Objects)
candidates.notes: Practical rules about a person standing in one domain and handling objects in another domain; positions of body and object relative to domain boundaries

candidates.name: Carrying Phylacteries on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Special rules for rescuing phylacteries found in the public domain on Shabbat by donning them pair by pair; passing them hand-to-hand less than 4 cubits

candidates.name: Rescuing Sacred Writings on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Rules about rolling back a Torah scroll that fell into the public domain on Shabbat; priority of rescue of sacred writings over rabbinic Shabbat decrees

candidates.name: Rooftops as Shabbat Domain
candidates.notes: The dispute whether all roofs of a city form one shared domain or each is independent; rules about height differences between adjacent roofs

candidates.name: Two Days of Rosh HaShanah — Eruv and Calendar Uncertainty
candidates.hebrew: שני ימי ראש השנה לעניין עירוב
candidates.notes: Rabbi Yehuda's view allowing separate eruvin for the two potentially-Rosh-HaShanah days due to calendar uncertainty; rabbinic disagreement; conditional tithing on Rosh HaShanah

candidates.name: Military Camp Exemptions (Machaneh Tzava)
candidates.notes: Four exemptions granted to soldiers in a military camp: wood gathering without concern for theft, handwashing before eating, separation of demai tithes, and eruv establishment

candidates.name: Yom Kippur Atoning for Uncertain Sins
candidates.notes: Yom Kippur exempts one from bringing a provisional guilt offering for uncertainties that arose even at nightfall ending the day; sin offerings and definite guilt offerings are not exempted by Yom Kippur

candidates.name: Megillah Reading Times and Locations (Walled vs. Unwalled Cities)
candidates.notes: Laws governing when Megillah is read — 14th vs. 15th of Adar — based on whether a city was walled since the days of Joshua; includes advancing reading to day of assembly for villages

candidates.name: Walled Cities (Kerakin Mukafoot Chomah) — Purim on 15th
candidates.hebrew: כרכים המוקפין חומה מימות יהושע בן נון
candidates.notes: Definition and halakhic status of cities walled since Joshua's time, who read Megillah on the 15th of Adar

candidates.name: Day of Assembly (Yom HaKenisah) — Advancing Mitzvot
candidates.notes: Rabbinic enactment permitting villages to advance Megillah reading to Monday or Thursday (day of assembly/market day)

candidates.name: Requirements for Writing the Megillah
candidates.notes: Megillah must be written in Ashurit (Hebrew script), on parchment, with ink; specific invalid writing materials listed

candidates.name: Gifts to the Poor on Purim (Matanot LaEvyonim)
candidates.notes: Obligation to distribute gifts to the poor on Purim; must be performed on actual Purim day even when Megillah reading is advanced

candidates.name: First and Second Adar (Adar Rishon v'Sheni) — Purim Timing
candidates.notes: Distinction between first and second Adar in a leap year regarding Megillah reading and Purim observance — Purim is in second Adar

candidates.name: Laws of Megillah Reading (Keriat HaMegillah)
candidates.notes: Grouping of laws governing the reading of the Megillah on Purim

candidates.name: Requirements for Reading the Megillah (Keriat HaMegillah)
candidates.notes: Reading must be in order, not by heart, not in translation one doesn't understand; who is obligated and who may read; need for intent

candidates.name: Who is Fit to Read the Megillah
candidates.notes: All are fit to read except deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor (Rabbi Yehuda permits a minor); language requirements

candidates.name: Language of Megillah Reading
candidates.notes: Foreign-language speakers may hear Megillah in their language; one who hears it in Hebrew (Ashurit) fulfills obligation regardless of language; reading by heart or in unknown language does not fulfill obligation

candidates.name: Hakhel (Assembly of the Nation)
candidates.notes: Commandment for the king to read Deuteronomy before all Israel on Sukkot following the Sabbatical year; mentioned as an example of a mitzvah that is postponed rather than advanced

candidates.name: Labor on Chol HaMoed (Melacha b'Moed)
candidates.notes: Detailed rules governing which types of work are permitted or forbidden on the intermediate days of a Festival, including distinctions between professional and amateur work, public needs vs. private, and avoiding financial loss (davar ha'aved)

candidates.name: Davar HaAved (Preventing Financial Loss on Chol HaMoed)
candidates.notes: Principle permitting otherwise prohibited labor on Chol HaMoed when there is risk of significant financial loss; covers agricultural and commercial contexts

candidates.name: Tzorech HaMoed (Labor for Festival Needs)
candidates.notes: Category of permitted Chol HaMoed labor done specifically for the needs of the Festival itself, e.g., food preparation, obtaining clothing

candidates.name: Mourning on Chol HaMoed
candidates.notes: Rules governing mourning practices (aninut, avelut) that occur during or coincide with Chol HaMoed; includes restrictions on eulogies, rending garments, overturned bed, consolation meal

candidates.name: Irrigation on Chol HaMoed
candidates.notes: Rules permitting irrigation from newly emerged or established springs but prohibiting use of cistern water or shadoof due to excessive labor

candidates.name: Prohibition of Marriage on Chol HaMoed
candidates.notes: Prohibition against marrying a new wife (virgin or widow) on Chol HaMoed so as not to mix one's personal joy with the joy of the Festival; remarrying divorced wife is permitted

candidates.name: Laundering Clothes on Chol HaMoed
candidates.notes: General prohibition on laundering on Chol HaMoed; exceptions for those returning from abroad, released from prison/captivity, released from nidui, zavim/zavot, yoledot, and quick-dirtying towels

candidates.name: Haircutting on Chol HaMoed
candidates.notes: General prohibition on cutting hair on Chol HaMoed; exceptions for those who could not cut hair before the Festival: returnees from abroad, released prisoners, those released from nidui/vow, nazirite, metzora

candidates.name: Writing Documents on Chol HaMoed
candidates.notes: Which legal documents may be written on Chol HaMoed (betrothal, divorce, wills, prozbul, chalitza, etc.) and which may not (loan documents, Torah scrolls, tefillin, mezuzot)

candidates.name: Public Welfare Work on Chol HaMoed (Tzorchei Rabbim)
candidates.notes: Category of permitted labor on Chol HaMoed for communal/public needs: repairing cisterns, roads, streets, ritual baths, marking graves, uprooting kilayim

candidates.name: Laws of Chametz (Searching, Nullifying, Removing)
candidates.notes: Grouping of laws governing the search, nullification, removal, and prohibition of chametz before and during Passover

candidates.name: Bedikat Chametz (Searching for Leaven)
candidates.notes: Laws of searching for chametz on the night of the 14th of Nisan, including which areas require searching, use of candlelight, and concerns about animals dragging leaven

candidates.name: Bitul Chametz (Nullification of Leaven)
candidates.notes: The nullification of chametz in one's heart as a valid form of removal, distinct from physical destruction

candidates.name: Zman Biur Chametz (Time for Removing Leaven)
candidates.notes: Dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda regarding the exact hours of the 14th of Nisan during which chametz may be eaten and when it must be burned

candidates.name: Chametz sheAvar Alav HaPesach (Leaven Over Which Passover Passed)
candidates.notes: Prohibition against deriving benefit from chametz belonging to a Jew that remained in his possession throughout Passover, and permissibility of chametz belonging to a gentile

candidates.name: Chametz as Collateral (Mashkon)
candidates.notes: Laws of chametz given as collateral to a gentile or by a gentile to a Jew before Passover and the question of ownership during the festival

candidates.name: Issur Melacha b'Erev Pesach (Prohibition of Work on Passover Eve)
candidates.notes: Regional customs regarding performing labor on the morning of Passover eve, including disputes between different locales and between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel regarding the night before

candidates.name: Siur and Nichratz (Stages of Leavening)
candidates.notes: The two stages of dough becoming leavened: siur (beginning to crack like locust antennae) and nichratz (fully cracked/leavened), and their halakhic consequences including liability for karet

candidates.name: Chametz on Passover Eve that Falls on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Special rules when the 14th of Nisan falls on Shabbat, including how and when to remove chametz, differing opinions of Rabbi Meir, the Rabbis, and Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok

candidates.name: Five Grains for Matza (Chamesh Minim)
candidates.notes: The five species of grain (wheat, barley, spelt, rye, oats) from which matza may be made to fulfill the Passover obligation

candidates.name: Five Vegetables for Maror (Chamesh Minim leMaRor)
candidates.notes: The five species of vegetables (hazeret, tamkha, harḥavina, olashin, maror) with which one may fulfill the obligation of bitter herbs on Passover

candidates.name: Seder Night Practices
candidates.notes: Grouping of laws and practices specific to the Passover seder night

candidates.name: Seder Night Rituals and Order
candidates.notes: The order of the Passover seder including reclining, four cups of wine, dipping vegetables, matza and maror, haggadah recitation, and the obligation of every person to view himself as personally leaving Egypt

candidates.name: Arba Kosot (Four Cups of Wine at the Seder)
candidates.notes: Obligation to drink four cups of wine at the Passover seder, including provision for the poor; dispute regarding drinking between the third and fourth cups

candidates.name: Haggadah and Sippur Yetziat Mitzrayim (Telling the Exodus Story)
candidates.notes: Obligation to tell the story of the Exodus including beginning with disgrace and ending with glory, expounding from 'An Aramean tried to destroy my father,' and Rabban Gamliel's three required mentions of Pesach, matza, and maror

candidates.name: Afikoman
candidates.notes: Prohibition of concluding after the Paschal lamb with an afikoman; the requirement that the Paschal lamb be the last food eaten; related rules about interruptions in eating

candidates.name: Interrupting a Journey to Remove Chametz
candidates.notes: Laws governing whether one traveling for a mitzvah must return home to remove chametz, depending on the nature of the mitzvah and whether there is time to complete it

candidates.name: Four New Years (Arba Roshei Shanim)
candidates.notes: Grouping of entries related to the four different new year dates for different halakhic purposes

candidates.name: Four New Years (Arba Roshei Shanim)
candidates.notes: The four different new year dates for different purposes: kings, festivals, animal tithes, trees, vegetables, shemitah/yovel

candidates.name: New Year for Kings (Rosh HaShanah laMelachim)
candidates.notes: First of Nisan as the new year for counting years of a king's reign

candidates.name: New Year for Trees (Rosh HaShanah laIlanot)
candidates.notes: Tu b'Shevat (Beit Hillel) or 1 Shevat (Beit Shammai) as the cutoff for fruit tithes; distinct from the general Tu b'Shevat entry in that it addresses the halakhic mechanism of tithing

candidates.name: New Year for Animal Tithes
candidates.notes: First of Elul (or 1 Tishrei per R. Elazar and R. Shimon) as the cutoff date for grouping animals for maaser beheimah

candidates.name: Divine Judgment on Rosh HaShanah
candidates.notes: The concept that all creatures pass before God like sheep (bnei maron) on Rosh HaShanah; also judgment on Pesach for grain, Shavuot for fruit, Sukkot for water

candidates.name: Witnesses for Sanctifying the New Month
candidates.notes: Rules for qualification, examination, and acceptance of witnesses who testify about sighting the new moon; desecrating Shabbat to bring testimony; disqualification of relatives and others

candidates.name: Procedures for Sanctifying the New Month
candidates.notes: Grouped parent for the procedural aspects of kiddush hachodesh: witnesses, examination, declaration, messengers, and court authority

candidates.name: Messengers Sent Out for New Month (Shelichei Beit Din)
candidates.notes: The six months in which messengers were dispatched to inform the Diaspora of the new moon; later replaced by torch signals; historical and legal background

candidates.name: Torch Signals for the New Moon (Massuot)
candidates.notes: The original system of lighting torches on mountaintops to relay the news of the new month; discontinued due to Samaritan interference

candidates.name: Beit Ya'azek (Witness Assembly Court)
candidates.notes: The Jerusalem courtyard where witnesses for the new moon gathered; Rabban Gamliel's institution of 2000-cubit movement rights for witnesses and others who arrived on Shabbat

candidates.name: Examination of New Moon Witnesses
candidates.notes: The procedure for examining witnesses about the shape, position, and direction of the new moon; Rabban Gamliel's diagram of lunar forms

candidates.name: Declaration of the New Month (Mekudash)
candidates.notes: The formal pronouncement by the head of the court 'It is sanctified' and communal response; whether sanctification is needed when moon was not seen at anticipated time

candidates.name: Authority of Beit Din to Sanctify the Month
candidates.notes: The principle that the calendar is determined by the earthly court's declaration, not heavenly calculation; Rabban Gamliel's authority even when disputed; submission to court ruling as binding

candidates.name: Laws of the Shofar
candidates.notes: Grouped parent for detailed shofar laws: types, blast sequences, intent, Temple vs. provinces distinctions, and Shabbat-Rosh HaShanah

candidates.name: Types and Materials of the Shofar
candidates.notes: Which animals' horns are valid for shofar; cow horn disqualified; ibex (straight) for Rosh HaShanah Temple service; ram's horn for fast days; cracked or repaired shofarot

candidates.name: Shofar in the Temple vs. Provinces
candidates.notes: Distinctions between shofar practice in the Temple (with gold-mouthed ibex horn + two silver trumpets) and elsewhere; shofar on Shabbat only in Temple or (post-Temple) where there is a court

candidates.name: Shofar on Shabbat-Rosh HaShanah
candidates.notes: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai's institution permitting shofar blowing on Shabbat-Rosh HaShanah wherever there is a court of 23 after Temple destruction

candidates.name: Intent When Hearing the Shofar (Kavvanah)
candidates.notes: Requirement to intend to fulfill the mitzva when hearing shofar; one who hears from a pit or echo; one who hears from behind a synagogue; comparison to Megillah reading

candidates.name: Tekiah, Terua, Shevarim (Shofar Blast Types)
candidates.notes: The three types of shofar sounds, their lengths relative to each other, the order of sets (tekia-terua-tekia), and rules about extended tekiot

candidates.name: Lulav All Seven Days (Zecher laMikdash)
candidates.notes: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai's institution that the lulav be taken all seven days of Sukkot outside the Temple, in commemoration of Temple practice

candidates.name: Bnei Maron (Divine Review of All Creatures)
candidates.notes: The imagery of all humanity passing before God like sheep (bnei maron) on Rosh HaShanah for divine judgment

candidates.name: Domains of Shabbat (Reshuyot)
candidates.notes: Classification of public domain (reshut harabim), private domain (reshut hayachid), karmelit, and exempt domain (mekom patur) for purposes of Shabbat carrying prohibitions

candidates.name: Pre-Shabbat Activities (Erev Shabbat Restrictions)
candidates.notes: Restrictions on beginning activities on Shabbat eve that will continue into Shabbat, including the Beit Shammai/Beit Hillel dispute about when one must cease

candidates.name: Shabbat Candles (Hadlakat Nerot Shabbat)
candidates.notes: Laws of kindling Shabbat lights, permitted and forbidden wicks and oils, and the obligation to light before Shabbat

candidates.name: Hatmanah (Insulating Food on Shabbat)
candidates.notes: Laws of insulating cooked food before Shabbat to keep it warm, including permitted and forbidden insulating materials and heat-generating vs. non-heat-generating materials

candidates.name: Bishul on Shabbat (Cooking Prohibition)
candidates.notes: Laws of the prohibition of cooking on Shabbat including chazarah (returning food to the fire), kli rishon/sheni, and related rabbinic decrees

candidates.name: Chazarah (Returning Food to Heat on Shabbat)
candidates.notes: Laws regarding returning a pot to the stove on Shabbat, and the conditions under which it is permitted

candidates.name: Medical Treatment on Shabbat (Refuah b'Shabbat)
candidates.notes: Rabbinic prohibition on taking medicine or engaging in medical treatments on Shabbat unless there is danger to life, including specific cases of foods and ointments used medicinally

candidates.name: Pikuach Nefesh (Life-Threatening Danger Overrides Shabbat)
candidates.notes: The principle that saving life overrides Shabbat, including childbirth, circumcision complications, and related cases

candidates.name: Measures for Carrying on Shabbat (Shi'urei Hotzaah)
candidates.notes: The minimum measures of various substances for which one becomes liable for carrying in a prohibited domain on Shabbat

candidates.name: Thirty-Nine Melachot (Arba'im Chaser Achat)
candidates.notes: The enumerated list of the 39 primary categories of prohibited labor on Shabbat derived from the work of the Tabernacle

candidates.name: Throwing Objects on Shabbat (Zrikah)
candidates.notes: Laws of liability for throwing objects between domains on Shabbat, including objects that pass through a public domain between two private domains

candidates.name: Tying and Untying Knots on Shabbat (Kesher v'Hitarah)
candidates.notes: Laws of the prohibited labors of tying and untying on Shabbat, including which knots are Torah-level prohibitions and which are rabbinic

candidates.name: Trapping on Shabbat (Tzeidah)
candidates.notes: Laws of the prohibited labor of trapping animals on Shabbat, including minimum enclosure sizes for liability and distinction between domesticated and wild animals

candidates.name: Writing on Shabbat (Ketivah)
candidates.notes: Laws of the prohibited labor of writing two letters on Shabbat, including valid writing substances, languages, and surfaces

candidates.name: Building on Shabbat (Binyan)
candidates.notes: Laws of the prohibited labor of building on Shabbat, including any constructive act that endures

candidates.name: Weaving on Shabbat (Oreg)
candidates.notes: Laws of the prohibited labors of weaving, making meshes, sewing, and tearing on Shabbat including minimum measures for liability

candidates.name: Extinguishing Fire on Shabbat (Mechabeh)
candidates.notes: Laws of extinguishing fire on Shabbat, exemptions for fear and the sick, and indirect extinguishing

candidates.name: Preventing Fire Spread on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Laws of rescuing items from a fire on Shabbat, how much one may rescue, use of barriers, and role of gentile firefighters

candidates.name: Rescuing Sacred Writings from Fire on Shabbat
candidates.notes: The obligation and limits of rescuing Torah scrolls, Prophets, Writings, and their coverings from fire on Shabbat

candidates.name: What Animals May Carry on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of what equipment and adornments animals may go out with into the public domain on Shabbat, distinguishing protective items from burdens

candidates.name: Women's Ornaments on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Laws of which ornaments and accessories a woman may wear into the public domain on Shabbat and which are considered burdens

candidates.name: Childbirth on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Laws permitting desecration of Shabbat for a woman giving birth, calling a midwife, and related actions

candidates.name: Laws of Sukkah (Construction and Dwelling)
candidates.notes: Laws governing the physical construction, validity, and dwelling obligations of the sukkah

candidates.name: Sukkot Temple Rites and Ceremonies
candidates.notes: Ceremonial and temple-based practices specific to Sukkot: water drawing, altar circling, willow mitzva, and Hakhel

candidates.name: Social and Commercial Activities on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Laws governing borrowing, lending, drawing lots, measuring, and similar social or quasi-commercial activities on Shabbat

candidates.name: Death and Mourning on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Laws concerning preparation of a corpse, funeral arrangements, and related activities on Shabbat and at its conclusion

candidates.name: Preparation of a Corpse on Shabbat
candidates.notes: What may and may not be done for a corpse on Shabbat, including anointing, rinsing, moving limbs, and closing eyes

candidates.name: Types of Muktzeh (Categories)
candidates.notes: Different categories of muktzeh including muktzeh machmat gufo, muktzeh machmat chisaron kis, and graf shel re'i (disgusting objects set aside from use)

candidates.name: Prohibition of Weekday Speech on Shabbat (Dibur b'Shabbat)
candidates.notes: Prohibition against discussing weekday activities such as hiring workers or commercial arrangements on Shabbat

candidates.name: Gentile Performing Labor on Shabbat (Amirah l'Nochri)
candidates.notes: Laws regarding instructing or benefiting from a gentile's performance of prohibited labor on Shabbat, including the cases of a lamp lit by a gentile and a ramp made by a gentile

candidates.name: Filtering and Selecting on Shabbat (Borer)
candidates.notes: Laws of the prohibited labor of selecting on Shabbat, including filtering wine, separating chaff from grain, and similar activities

candidates.name: Squeezing Fruits on Shabbat (Sechitah)
candidates.notes: Laws of squeezing fruits for their juice on Shabbat and the status of liquids that seep from fruit on their own

candidates.name: Folding Garments on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Laws permitting folding garments on Shabbat for use on Shabbat, and prohibiting folding in preparation for after Shabbat

candidates.name: Measuring on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Prohibition of measuring on Shabbat and exceptions for measuring a mikveh, a rag for ritual impurity, or for a mitzva purpose

candidates.name: Primary and Secondary Vessels (Kli Rishon v'Sheni)
candidates.notes: Distinction between a primary vessel that was on the fire and a secondary vessel into which food was poured, affecting cooking prohibition on Shabbat

candidates.name: Incomplete Labor Performed by Two People (Shenayim she'Asu)
candidates.notes: The rule that when two people jointly perform a prohibited labor, each performing only part, they are generally exempt, and its exceptions

candidates.name: Unusual Manner of Performing Labor on Shabbat (Shinui)
candidates.notes: The principle that performing a prohibited labor on Shabbat in an unusual manner (shinui) affects liability, including cases of carrying behind one's back

candidates.name: Borrowing and Lending on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Laws permitting informal borrowing of food or vessels on Shabbat using euphemistic language to avoid commercial transactions

candidates.name: Drawing Lots on Shabbat
candidates.notes: Permission to draw lots among family members for food portions on Shabbat, and among priests for sacrificial portions on Festivals

candidates.name: Waiting at Techum Boundary on Shabbat Eve
candidates.notes: Law of waiting at the Shabbat boundary at nightfall in order to tend to needs immediately after Shabbat, including permitted and forbidden purposes

candidates.name: Funeral Preparations at Shabbat's End
candidates.notes: Laws of waiting at the Shabbat boundary to attend to funeral needs, and use of items prepared by gentiles (coffin, grave) on Shabbat for a Jew

candidates.name: Smearing Oil as Substitute for Drinking on Yom Kippur
candidates.notes: The derivation that anointing/smearing oil is prohibited on Yom Kippur like drinking, based on Psalms 109:18

candidates.name: Coffin and Grave Made by Gentile on Shabbat
candidates.notes: A coffin or grave made by a gentile on Shabbat: if done for himself, a Jew may use it; if done for a Jew, it is permanently forbidden

candidates.name: Hakhel (Assembly at Sukkot)
candidates.notes: The septennial public Torah reading by the king at Sukkot following the Sabbatical Year: procedure, Torah portions read, blessings recited, and King Agrippa episode

candidates.name: Sukkah Structure and Validity
candidates.notes: Laws governing the physical construction and validity of the sukkah: height requirements, walls, schach, and related rules

candidates.name: Schach (Sukkah Roofing)
candidates.notes: Laws of valid and invalid roofing material for a sukkah, including susceptibility to impurity and attachment to the ground

candidates.name: Dofen Akumah (Curved Wall Principle)
candidates.notes: Legal principle by which part of an existing roof or ceiling is treated as an extension of the wall, enabling a sukkah to be valid

candidates.name: Yeshivat Sukkah (Dwelling in the Sukkah)
candidates.notes: Obligation to eat, sleep, and dwell in the sukkah during the seven days of the festival, including the first night obligation and exemptions

candidates.name: Exemptions from Sukkah
candidates.notes: Who is exempt from the sukkah obligation: women, minors, slaves, the ill, travelers performing a mitzvah, and rain as a sign of exemption

candidates.name: Simchat Beit HaShoevah (Celebration of Water Drawing)
candidates.notes: The great celebration in the Temple courtyard during Sukkot associated with the water libation, including music, dancing, torches, and illumination

candidates.name: Aravah (Willow Branch Mitzva on Sukkot)
candidates.notes: The distinct mitzva of encircling the altar with willow branches on Sukkot (separate from the willow of the four species), including the seven-day and Shabbat override issues

candidates.name: Hakafot (Circling the Altar on Sukkot)
candidates.notes: The practice of circling the altar once each day of Sukkot and seven times on Hoshana Rabbah, with lulav and aravah

candidates.name: Lulav Ownership on First Day
candidates.notes: Requirement that the lulav belong to the person fulfilling the mitzva on the first day of Sukkot; inability to use a borrowed lulav on the first day

candidates.name: Waving the Lulav (Naanuim)
candidates.notes: Laws of when to wave the lulav during Hallel, in which directions, and at which verses

candidates.name: Etrog Specifications and Validity
candidates.notes: Physical requirements for a valid etrog including size, blemishes, orla status, teruma status, and color

candidates.name: Lulav, Myrtle, and Willow Specifications
candidates.notes: Physical requirements for valid lulav, hadas, and aravah, including dryness, severed tops, minimum lengths, and number of species

candidates.name: Shemini Atzeret (Eighth Day of Assembly)
candidates.notes: The eighth day following Sukkot as an independent festival, with obligations of rejoicing and Hallel but not sukkah or lulav

candidates.name: Hoshana Rabbah (Seventh Day of Sukkot)
candidates.notes: The seventh day of Sukkot on which the altar is encircled seven times and special willow-branch customs are performed

candidates.name: Fast Days for Rain (Taanit Geshamim)
candidates.notes: The structured progression of communal and individual fasts decreed when rain fails to fall, including the three stages of increasing severity

candidates.name: Seventeenth of Tammuz Fast
candidates.notes: The five calamities that occurred on the seventeenth of Tammuz including the breaking of the tablets, cessation of the daily offering, breach of Jerusalem walls, burning of a Torah scroll, and placement of an idol in the Sanctuary

candidates.name: Laws of Tisha B'Av (Prohibitions and Practices)
candidates.notes: Specific prohibitions of the Ninth of Av week and day: haircuts, laundering, two cooked dishes, meat and wine; the custom of overturning one's bed

candidates.name: Fast Day Ceremonies and Procedures
candidates.notes: Ritual procedures and ceremonies associated with communal fast days

candidates.name: Afflictions and Fasting on Yom Kippur
candidates.notes: Laws governing the five afflictions on Yom Kippur, their measures, exceptions, and application to minors and the ill

candidates.name: Scope and Mechanism of Yom Kippur Atonement
candidates.notes: What Yom Kippur atones for, including the distinction between sins against God and sins against other people

candidates.name: Mourning Practices of the Month of Av
candidates.notes: Decreasing acts of rejoicing from Rosh Chodesh Av, including restrictions on building, planting, business, betrothals, and greetings

candidates.name: Tu b'Av Celebrations and Marriage Market
candidates.notes: The daughters of Jerusalem dancing in borrowed white garments in vineyards to attract marriage partners; the concept that borrowed garments were required to avoid embarrassing the poor

candidates.name: Megillat Ta'anit (Scroll of Fasts)
candidates.notes: The ancient scroll listing days on which fasting and eulogizing are prohibited; rules about fasting on the day before and after such days

candidates.name: Ashes on the Ark and Heads on Fast Days
candidates.hebrew: אפר על ראשי הנשיא ועל התיבה
candidates.notes: The ceremony of placing burnt ashes on the ark, on the head of the Nasi and deputy Nasi, and on everyone's heads as a sign of mourning during communal fast days

candidates.name: Sounding the Shofar on Fast Days
candidates.notes: Blowing the shofar (tekiah and teruah) during communal fast days as a cry to God; the procedure in the Temple context vs. outside; distinction from Rosh Hashanah shofar

candidates.name: Completing a Fast After Rain Falls (Hashlamat HaTa'anit)
candidates.notes: Whether a community must complete a fast after the desired outcome (rain) arrives before or after midday/sunrise; the incident in Lod with Rabbi Tarfon

candidates.name: Local Calamities Requiring Immediate Fasting
candidates.hebrew: תענית על צרות פרטיות של עיר
candidates.notes: Calamities requiring immediate communal fast without waiting: blight, locusts, dangerous beasts, pestilence, sword, a city receiving no rain while surroundings did; criteria for pestilence

candidates.name: Crying Out for Help on Shabbat (Tza'akah beShabbat)
