candidates.notes: Crying out to God or summoning help on Shabbat for emergencies such as siege, flood, or shipwreck; dispute about whether crying out differs from sounding the alarm

candidates.name: Five Afflictions on Yom Kippur (Inuyim)
candidates.notes: The five prohibitions constituting affliction on Yom Kippur: eating/drinking, bathing, anointing, wearing shoes, and conjugal relations; their measures and exceptions

candidates.name: Measures for Eating/Drinking on Yom Kippur
candidates.notes: The date-bulk measure for food and cheekful measure for drink that create liability on Yom Kippur; whether food and drink combine

candidates.name: Training Minors to Fast (Chinuch for Yom Kippur)
candidates.notes: The practice of training children one or two years before bar/bat mitzvah to fast partial fasts on Yom Kippur

candidates.name: Saving Life (Pikuach Nefesh) Overriding Yom Kippur
candidates.notes: Cases where danger to life overrides Yom Kippur fasting: pregnant women with cravings, the ill, bulmos sufferers, rockslide victims

candidates.name: Bulmos (Life-Threatening Hunger Illness)
candidates.notes: The medical condition of severe hunger causing vision impairment; one may feed the sufferer even impure food until his eyes recover

candidates.name: Scope of Yom Kippur Atonement
candidates.notes: What Yom Kippur atones for: transgressions between person and God vs. between people; requirement to appease others; the interplay between sin-offering, guilt-offering, death, repentance and Yom Kippur

candidates.name: Atonement for Interpersonal Sins (Bein Adam laChavero)
candidates.hebrew: כפרה על עבירות שבין אדם לחברו
candidates.notes: The principle that Yom Kippur does not atone for sins between people until one appeases the offended party

candidates.name: Half-Slave Half-Free (Chatzi Eved Chatzi Ben Chorin)
candidates.notes: Grouping of laws pertaining to a person of mixed slave/free status, including disputes between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel, emancipation obligations, and the case of the shifcha charufah

candidates.name: Half-Slave Half-Free Person (Chatzi Eved Chatzi Ben Chorin)
candidates.notes: The status and obligations of a person who is half-slave and half-free; Beit Shammai's argument that the master must emancipate him to allow him to fulfill the obligation of procreation; Beit Hillel changed their ruling; Eduyot 1:13

candidates.name: Half-Slave's Emancipation (Eved Chatzi Ben Chorin)
candidates.notes: Laws of a slave owned jointly where one owner freed him — Beit Hillel vs. Beit Shammai dispute; obligation to fully emancipate for the world's betterment; Gittin 4:5

candidates.name: Espoused Maidservant (Shifcha Charufah)
candidates.notes: Halakhot of the half-slave half-free betrothed maidservant; the guilt offering brought for intercourse with her; distinctions from other forbidden relationships regarding punishment, offering type, and conditions for liability

candidates.name: Parallel Laws of Get and Get Shichrur (Bill of Manumission)
candidates.notes: Ways in which bills of divorce and bills of manumission share identical halakhot; Gittin 1:4, 9:3

candidates.name: Slave Sold to Gentiles — Automatic Emancipation
candidates.notes: Penalty that a slave sold to a gentile or to a Jew outside Eretz Yisrael is automatically emancipated; Gittin 4:6

candidates.name: Manumission of Slave Through Property Gift
candidates.notes: Master who gives all his property to his slave in writing thereby frees the slave; if master retains any portion, slave is not freed; dispute about exception clause

candidates.name: Disputes of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel
candidates.notes: General grouping for the phenomenon and specific instances of disputes between the schools of Shammai and Hillel

candidates.name: Halakhic Measurements and Shiurim
candidates.notes: Standard halakhic measurements and units used in legal determinations — olive, egg, cubit, etc.

candidates.name: Historical Rabbinic Enactments (Named Sages)
candidates.notes: Grouping for specific sets of rabbinic enactments attributed to named historical sages or bodies

candidates.name: Fence Around the Torah (Seyag laTorah)
candidates.notes: The principle of erecting protective enactments around Torah law to prevent transgression; mentioned in Avot 1:1, 3:13.

candidates.name: Disputes of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel (General)
candidates.notes: The general phenomenon of halakhic disputes between the schools of Shammai and Hillel; cases where Beit Shammai is lenient and Beit Hillel is strict

candidates.name: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel Disputes (Meals/Prayer)
candidates.hebrew: מחלוקות בית שמאי ובית הלל בסעודה ותפילה
candidates.notes: The series of disputes between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel regarding kiddush, handwashing, havdalah, and meal practices in tractate Berakhot

candidates.name: Beit Hillel Changed Their Opinion to Follow Beit Shammai
candidates.hebrew: חזרו בית הלל להורות כדברי בית שמאי
candidates.notes: The specific instances recorded in Eduyot where Beit Hillel reversed their position and ruled according to Beit Shammai's opinion

candidates.name: Eighteen Decrees of Beit Shammai
candidates.notes: The eighteen rabbinic decrees issued by Beit Shammai's majority in the upper story of Chananya ben Chizkiya ben Garon, representing a landmark moment in rabbinic legislation

candidates.name: Comparative Halakhic Analysis (X is like Y in some ways)
candidates.notes: The Mishnaic literary form of comparing legal categories (terumah vs. bikkurim, etrog vs. tree/vegetable, koy vs. behemah/hayyah, androginus vs. man/woman) to derive halakha

candidates.name: Mountains Hanging by a Hair (Minimal Biblical Basis for Major Topics)
candidates.notes: The category of halakhot — Shabbat, Festival peace-offerings, meilah — that have minimal written basis in the Torah yet have elaborate rabbinic detail; methodological classification of Torah topics.

candidates.name: Eduyot — Testimonial Format of Halakhic Transmission
candidates.notes: The unique format of Tractate Eduyot whereby rulings are transmitted as formal testimonies (eduyot) before sages; the halakhic and jurisprudential significance of this mode of transmission

candidates.name: Tikkun Olam (Rabbinic Enactments for the Betterment of Society)
candidates.notes: Category of rabbinic enactments justified by 'for the betterment of the world' — redeeming captives, prozbul, widow's oath, orphan guardianship, etc.; Gittin chapters 4-5

candidates.name: Priority Between Mitzvot Based on Frequency (Tadir)
candidates.notes: The principle that a more frequent mitzva precedes a less frequent one, and a more sanctified person precedes a less sanctified one, as applied to ordering sacrificial rites and communal priorities.

candidates.name: Standard Halakhic Measures (Shiurim)
candidates.notes: The enumeration and definition of standard halakhic measurements — olive, fig, pomegranate, date, egg, barleycorn, lentil, ox-goad thickness, cubit — and what 'moderate size' means for each (Keilim chapter 17)

candidates.name: The Standard Cubit (Amah)
candidates.notes: The definition and history of the cubit measurement, the two cubits at Shushan HaBirah, difference between building cubit and vessel cubit, application in Temple context

candidates.name: Mitzvot Dependent on the Land (Mitzvot haTeluyot baAretz)
candidates.notes: Principle distinguishing mitzvot that apply only in Eretz Yisrael from those applying everywhere; exceptions such as orlah and kilayim that apply even outside the land

candidates.name: Women Exempt from Time-Bound Positive Commandments
candidates.hebrew: נשים פטורות ממצוות עשה שהזמן גרמן
candidates.notes: The rule that women are exempt from positive time-bound commandments and its exceptions; application in Kiddushin to distinguish men's and women's obligations

candidates.name: Double Condition Requirement (Tenai Kaful)
candidates.notes: Rabbi Meir's view that a legally valid condition must state both the positive and negative consequences; derived from the condition of Gad and Reuben (Numbers 32); dispute with Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel

candidates.name: Enactments of Yochanan the High Priest
candidates.notes: The historical rabbinic enactments attributed to Yochanan the High Priest: abolition of the viduy maaser recitation, abolition of the 'wakers' (hammers in the Temple), and declaration that demai need not be examined in his day.

candidates.name: All-Day Validity of Mitzvot (Kol HaYom Kasher)
candidates.notes: Principle that mitzvot of the day may be performed any time during the day; parallel principle for nighttime mitzvot

candidates.name: Preventing Fulfillment by Absence of Ritual Components
candidates.notes: Extensive list of paired or grouped ritual components that prevent each other: goats of Yom Kippur, lambs and loaves of Shavuot, branches of menorah, passages of mezuzah and tefillin, four species, leper purification components, etc.

candidates.name: Mitzvot Without a Defined Measure (Ein Lahem Shiur)
candidates.notes: Category of mitzvot for which no minimum measure is prescribed: peah, bikkurim, re'iyah, gemilut chasadim, talmud Torah; discussed in Mishnah Peah 1:1

candidates.name: Local Customs (Minhag HaMakom)
candidates.notes: Laws governing travelers who move between communities with differing customs, including the principle that one must follow both the stringencies of origin and destination; illustrated through Passover eve labor customs

candidates.name: Takkanot of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
candidates.notes: Post-Temple institutions by Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai: shofar on Shabbat where there is a court; lulav all seven days outside Temple; prohibition on new grain all day of 16 Nisan; accepting new moon testimony all day

candidates.name: Seven Court Ordinances of Rabbi Shimon
candidates.notes: Seven specific court ordinances relating to financial aspects of offerings: libations for found animals, libations for gentile offerings sent from abroad, libations for a deceased convert's offerings, the High Priest's daily offering after his death, salt and wood for priests, red heifer ashes, and replacement of disqualified bird-pairs

candidates.name: Voluntary Repayment Beyond Legal Obligation
candidates.notes: Cases where repayment is not legally required after shemitah cancellation but sages express approval for voluntary repayment; connects to lifnim mishurat hadin

candidates.name: Takkanot of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai for Sukkot
candidates.hebrew: תקנות רבן יוחנן בן זכאי לסוכות
candidates.notes: Post-Temple enactments of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai: lulav taken seven days everywhere, and prohibition of new grain extended through 16 Nisan as zecher lamikdash

candidates.name: Laws of Firstborn Animals (Bekhorot)
candidates.notes: Grouping for detailed laws of firstborn animals including kosher animals, donkeys, blemishes, examination, partnerships, and related topics

candidates.name: Detailed Laws of Animal Tithe
candidates.notes: Grouping for detailed practical laws of animal tithe including counting procedures, errors, new year dates, and exemptions

candidates.name: Property Laws of Hekdesh and Valuations
candidates.notes: Grouping for laws concerning consecrated fields, proclamation of sales, repossession of property, and conflicts with creditors

candidates.name: Levite Temple Music and Instruments
candidates.notes: Grouping for laws of Levite musicians in the Temple including instruments, numbers, and days of flute playing

candidates.name: Laws of Pidyon HaBen
candidates.notes: Grouping for detailed laws of firstborn son redemption including the distinction between firstborn for inheritance vs. redemption

candidates.name: Sdeh Miknah — Purchased Field Consecration Laws
candidates.notes: Laws of consecrating a purchased field: redemption at market value; does not go to priests at Jubilee; distinction from ancestral field; case where son purchased from father

candidates.name: Proclamation of Consecrated Property Sale (Hakrazah)
candidates.notes: Announcing the sale of consecrated property or orphan's property for 30 or 60 days morning and evening to maximize price; bidding procedures; reneging on bids

candidates.name: Repossession of Property for Valuations and Hekdesh
candidates.notes: Court repossession of property to pay valuations; what the treasurer leaves for the obligated person (30 days food, 12 months clothing, tools of trade); phylacteries; wife and children's garments

candidates.name: Conflict Between Hekdesh and Ketubah/Creditor Claims
candidates.notes: When one consecrates property that has liens for ketubah or creditor; collusion prevention; vow of benefit to prevent remarriage after divorce

candidates.name: Laws of Levite Cities
candidates.notes: Levites may always redeem their fields and houses; 2000 cubits surrounding cities; division into empty lots and fields; prohibition on converting field to empty lot or vice versa; Levite inheritance from Israelite

candidates.name: Temple Trumpet Blasts (Teki'ot HaMikdash)
candidates.notes: Minimum 21 and maximum 48 trumpet blasts daily; occasions for extra blasts; Friday of Sukkot with water libation; signals for gates, offerings, and Shabbat

candidates.name: Levite Musicians in the Temple
candidates.notes: Minimum and maximum numbers of lyres, flutes, harps; 12 days of flute playing; cymbal used alone; minor Levites as cadets; minimum 12 Levites on platform; debate on their status

candidates.name: Flute Playing in the Temple (Chalil)
candidates.notes: 12 days per year for flute before altar: Pesach slaughtering, second Pesach, first day of Pesach, Shavuot, 8 days of Sukkot; reed flute preferred over copper; concluding with single flute

candidates.name: Semichah (Laying Hands) on Festival Offerings
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel whether one may lay hands on a peace-offering or burnt-offering brought on a Yom Tov

candidates.name: Delivering Priestly Gifts on Yom Tov
candidates.notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel whether challah and other priestly gifts (foreleg, jaw, maw) may be delivered to a priest on Yom Tov

candidates.name: Firstborn Animal with Blemish on Festival
candidates.notes: Rules for slaughtering a blemished firstborn animal that fell into a cistern on a Festival; whether a blemish must be certified before the Festival

candidates.name: Redemption of Firstborn Donkey (Peter Chamor)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of redeeming the firstborn donkey with a lamb, including cases of uncertainty, partnerships with gentiles, breaking the neck (arifah), and what happens when the lamb dies before or after designation

candidates.name: Breaking the Neck of the Firstborn Donkey (Arifah)
candidates.notes: The obligation to break the neck of the firstborn donkey when one does not wish to redeem it, and the principle that redemption takes precedence over breaking the neck

candidates.name: Firstborn of Kosher Animals (Bechor Beheimah Tehorah)
candidates.notes: Laws of the firstborn of kosher animals (cattle, sheep, goats), including partnerships with gentiles, when sanctity applies, animals born by caesarean section, uncertainty cases, and the role of priests and Levites

candidates.name: Blemishes of the Firstborn Animal
candidates.notes: Detailed enumeration and classification of blemishes that permit slaughter of a firstborn animal outside the Temple, including blemishes of the ear, eye, nose, lip, genitals, tail, legs, and additional blemishes enumerated by Ila in Yavne

candidates.name: Expert Examination of Firstborn Blemishes
candidates.notes: Requirements for expert examination before slaughtering a firstborn animal based on its blemish, liability of non-expert who rules incorrectly, payment of wages to examiners, and credibility of priests and shepherds in testifying about blemishes

candidates.name: Intentionally Caused Blemish (Mum sheNaaseh beYadayim)
candidates.notes: Prohibition against intentionally causing a blemish on a consecrated firstborn animal; if blemish was caused intentionally, the animal may not be slaughtered on its account, but if unintentionally, it may be slaughtered

candidates.name: Prohibition of Shearing a Firstborn Animal
candidates.notes: Prohibition of shearing the firstborn animal's wool, and the related question of wool that shed naturally or was stored, as debated by Akavya ben Mahalalel and the Rabbis

candidates.name: Laws of Animal Tithe (Maaser Beheimah)
candidates.notes: Detailed practical laws of animal tithe: when it applies (in and outside Israel, with or without Temple), procedure of passing animals under the rod, counting, painting the tenth animal, times of year for gathering, joining of flocks, and errors in counting

candidates.name: Errors in Counting Animal Tithe
candidates.notes: Halakhic consequences when the ninth animal is called tenth, tenth called ninth, eleventh called tenth — status of each animal as tithe, peace offering, or substitute, and dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda

candidates.name: New Year for Animal Tithe
candidates.notes: Dispute between Rabbi Akiva, Ben Azzai, Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon, and Rabbi Meir regarding the dates that mark the new year for animal tithe and when different birth cohorts are tithed together

candidates.name: Orphan Animal Exempt from Animal Tithe
candidates.notes: Definition of 'orphan' animal (whose mother died during or after birth) and its exemption from animal tithe along with other exempt categories like tereifa and caesarean-born animals

candidates.name: Partnership with a Gentile Exempting Firstborn Status
candidates.notes: Various forms of partnership, sale, or receivership with a gentile that exempt an animal's offspring from firstborn sanctity, based on the verse that the mitzva applies only to Israel

candidates.name: Guaranteed Investment from a Gentile (Iska) and Firstborn
candidates.hebrew: קיבל צאן ברזל מן הגוי ובכורה
candidates.notes: When a Jew receives animals as a guaranteed investment from a gentile, the offspring and their descendants are exempt from firstborn status as long as they serve as collateral for the gentile's claim

candidates.name: Blemishes Disqualifying Priests from Temple Service
candidates.notes: Extensive enumeration of physical blemishes that disqualify a priest from performing Temple service, including head shape, eye conditions, nose and lip defects, bodily proportions, epilepsy, extra or missing limbs, and skin conditions — some applying to animals but not priests and vice versa

candidates.name: Blemishes Unique to Animals vs. Those Unique to Priests
candidates.hebrew: מומין השווים בבהמה ובאדם ומומין המיוחדים
candidates.notes: Comparative analysis of which blemishes disqualify both priests and animals, which disqualify only priests (e.g., deaf-mute, imbecile, drunkard), and which disqualify only animals (e.g., tereifa, caesarean birth, same-day slaughter)

candidates.name: Laws of Redemption of the Firstborn Son (Pidyon HaBen)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws: who is firstborn for redemption vs. inheritance, cases of miscarriage, caesarean section, conversion, uncertain parentage; the five sela payment in Tyrian coinage; timing of obligation; who redeems when father dies; precedence of self-redemption vs. son's redemption

candidates.name: Firstborn for Inheritance vs. Firstborn for Redemption
candidates.notes: The tractate's systematic analysis of cases where a son is firstborn for inheritance but not for priestly redemption, firstborn for redemption but not inheritance, both, or neither — including cases of miscarriage, caesarean section, prior births by maidservant or gentile woman

candidates.name: Person Suspected of Firstborn Animal Violations
candidates.notes: Restrictions on purchasing meat, hides, and wool from one suspected of improperly slaughtering firstborn animals; the graduated suspicion from raw products to processed goods

candidates.name: Sale of Disqualified Consecrated Animals
candidates.notes: How disqualified consecrated animals (other than firstborn and animal tithe) are sold in the market by weight; contrast with firstborn and animal tithe which are sold at home by estimate, with all profit going to the owner

candidates.name: Caesarean-Born Animal and Firstborn Status
candidates.notes: An animal born by caesarean section and the animal following it — neither has firstborn sanctity; dispute between Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva on whether either has any firstborn status

candidates.name: Priestly Gifts from Slaughtered Animals (Foreleg, Jaw, Maw)
candidates.notes: Obligation to give the foreleg, jaw, and maw to a priest from non-sacred slaughtered animals; exemption of blemished firstborn animals (and their uncertain counterparts) from this obligation; dispute between Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Meir

candidates.name: Ila's Enumeration of Blemishes at Yavne
candidates.notes: The expert Ila enumerated blemishes that permit firstborn slaughter at Yavne; he added three novel blemishes (eye like a human, mouth like a pig, most of speech-facilitating tongue removed) which were later accepted by the court

candidates.name: Respectful Conduct Toward the Temple Mount
candidates.notes: Prohibition against entering Temple Mount with staff, shoes, money belt, or dust on feet; not using it as a shortcut; not spitting there; not acting with levity opposite the eastern gate

candidates.name: Temple Blessing Conclusion Formula
candidates.notes: The change in blessing conclusion formula in the Temple from 'until the world' (haolam) to 'from world to world' (min haolam ve'ad haolam) due to Sadducee heresy about the afterlife. Note: original parent_id 'temple_prayers' not found in existing taxonomy; reassigned to beit_hamikdash

candidates.name: Horayot — Offerings for Erroneous Rulings
candidates.notes: Group covering the various offerings brought as a result of erroneous halakhic rulings by the court, High Priest, king, or individual

candidates.name: High Priest — Status, Duties, and Liabilities (Horayot)
candidates.notes: Group covering the specific laws of the High Priest's status, distinctions between types of High Priests, and their special obligations and liabilities as discussed in tractate Horayot

candidates.name: Ma'amad (Assembly for Temple Pilgrimage)
candidates.notes: The cities of the maamad would assemble together and travel jointly to Jerusalem for bikkurim; the maamad officer's role

candidates.name: Obligation of Aliyah laRegel (Appearance at the Temple)
candidates.notes: Who is obligated to appear at the Temple on pilgrimage festivals, exemptions for deaf-mutes, minors, women, lame, blind, sick, etc. Details of minimum age for minors (Beit Shammai vs. Beit Hillel).

candidates.name: Olat Reiyah (Burnt-Offering of Appearance)
candidates.notes: The burnt-offering brought upon appearing at the Temple during the three pilgrimage festivals; minimum value requirements and disputes between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel.

candidates.name: Shalmei Simcha (Peace-Offerings of Rejoicing)
candidates.notes: Festival peace-offerings brought specifically to fulfill the obligation of rejoicing on Yom Tov; minimum values, sources of funding (non-sacred vs. second tithe), and timing.

candidates.name: Tashlumin (Make-Up Days for Festival Offering)
candidates.notes: If one failed to bring the Festival peace-offering on the first day, he may make it up throughout the remaining days of the festival. After the festival passes, no restitution is owed.

candidates.name: Semichah on Offerings on Yom Tov (Laying Hands on Festival Day)
candidates.notes: The dispute among the Zugot pairs (five pairs) over whether one may lay hands on an offering on a Festival day; relates to labor prohibitions on Yom Tov.

candidates.name: Onen's Prohibition from Sacrificial Food
candidates.notes: An acute mourner (onen) on the day of bereavement requires immersion to eat sacrificial food, but not for teruma; similarly one who is mechusar kapparah.

candidates.name: Purification of Temple Vessels After the Festival
candidates.notes: After the pilgrimage festival when amei haaretz entered the Temple, all vessels required immersion. Disputes about when this is done; golden and bronze altars are exempt as they are like the ground.

candidates.name: Distribution of Priestly Gifts to Any Priest
candidates.notes: List of items that may be given to any priest (devoted things, firstlings, pidyon haben, shoulder/cheeks/maw, first fleece, bikkurim, etc.) vs. items requiring specific conditions

candidates.name: Melikah (Nipping of Bird Offerings) — Location Requirements
candidates.notes: Distinction between valid locations for melikah vs. shechitah — nape valid for melikah, throat for shechitah

candidates.name: Ben Pekuah — Fetus Permitted by Mother's Slaughter
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of the fetus found in a slaughtered mother: when it requires its own slaughter, when it is permitted by mother's slaughter, limbs severed from fetus

candidates.name: Priestly Gifts from Slaughtered Animals (Foreleg, Jaw, Maw)
candidates.notes: Obligation to give foreleg, jaw, and maw of slaughtered non-sacred animals to priests; scope, exclusions (sacrificial animals), definition of each body part

candidates.name: Firstborn Animal — Laws of Consecration and Blemish
candidates.notes: Detailed rules when permanent blemish precedes consecration vs. when consecration precedes blemish: gifts of priesthood, shearing, labor, offspring, milk, slaughter outside Temple

candidates.name: Kalbon (Premium on Half-Shekel) and Animal Tithe — Partnership Rules
candidates.notes: Brothers who are partners: when obligated in kalbon are exempt from animal tithe and vice versa; rules for partners and non-partners

candidates.name: Redemption of Firstborn Donkey That Died Before Redemption
candidates.notes: Dispute whether the owner bears financial responsibility if the firstborn donkey dies before redemption; Eduyot 7:1

candidates.name: First Sanctification of Jerusalem — Permanent for All Time
candidates.hebrew: קידוש ראשון קידש לשעתו ולעתיד לבוא
candidates.notes: Rabbi Joshua's testimony that the original sanctification of Jerusalem sanctified it for its own time and for the future, permitting sacrifices even without the Temple standing; Eduyot 8:6

candidates.name: Offering Sacrifices Without the Temple Standing
candidates.notes: Rabbi Joshua's view that sacrifices may be offered even without the Temple, and most holy sacrifices eaten without the curtains; Eduyot 8:6

candidates.name: Sin Offering Stolen When Theft Was Unknown — Atonement Valid
candidates.hebrew: חטאת גזולה שלא נודע לרבים — כיפר
candidates.notes: Testimony that a stolen sin-offering whose theft was not publicly known still effects atonement for the welfare of the altar; Eduyot 7:9

candidates.name: Offspring of a Peace-Offering — May It Be Brought as a Peace-Offering
candidates.notes: Testimony of Rabbi Joshua and Rabbi Papias that the offspring of a peace-offering may itself be brought as a peace-offering; Rabbi Eliezer disagrees; Eduyot 7:6

candidates.name: Morning Tamid Offered at the Fourth Hour
candidates.notes: Testimony of Rabbi Judah ben Bava that the morning daily offering was brought at the fourth hour; Eduyot 6:1

candidates.name: Wine Forty Days Old as Valid for Altar Libation
candidates.notes: Testimony of Rabbi Judah ben Bava that wine forty days old was used as a libation on the altar; Eduyot 6:1

candidates.name: Temple Shabbat Leniencies (Miqdash vs. Medinah)
candidates.notes: Activities permitted in the Temple on Shabbat that are forbidden outside it due to rabbinic decree: closing bolts, removing impurity, tying harp strings, cutting warts, medical treatment of priests

candidates.name: Removing Creeping Animal Impurity from Temple on Shabbat
candidates.notes: The obligation and method for removing a sheretz (creeping creature) from the Temple precincts on Shabbat; dispute about which areas require removal

candidates.name: Erroneous Court Ruling (Horayot) — Communal Sin Offering
candidates.hebrew: הוראת בית דין שגגה — פר העלם דבר של ציבור
candidates.notes: The specific laws of when a Sanhedrin's erroneous ruling obligates a communal bull sin-offering, including the conditions of nullifying part vs. whole of a mitzva, majority of congregation acting on it, etc.

candidates.name: Individual's Exemption When Following Erroneous Court Ruling
candidates.hebrew: יחיד שעשה על פי בית דין — פטור
candidates.notes: The principle that an individual who acts on an erroneous Sanhedrin ruling is exempt from a personal sin-offering, and its limits (e.g., if the individual knew the court erred).

candidates.name: High Priest's Bull Sin-Offering for Erroneous Ruling
candidates.hebrew: פר כהן משיח על שגגת הוראה
candidates.notes: The anointed High Priest who issues an erroneous ruling for himself and acts on it unwittingly brings a bull sin-offering; the parallel between High Priest liability and Sanhedrin liability.

candidates.name: Anointed High Priest vs. High Priest Consecrated by Garments
candidates.notes: The legal distinctions between a High Priest anointed with the anointing oil and one who was consecrated solely by wearing the eight special garments after the anointing oil was hidden.

candidates.name: High Priest Sacrificing as an Acute Mourner (Onen)
candidates.notes: The High Priest may sacrifice offerings on the day a close relative dies (as an onen) but may not eat from them; contrast with an ordinary priest who is an onen.

candidates.name: King's (Nasi's) Sin-Offering — Male Goat
candidates.notes: The king (nasi) who sins unwittingly brings a male goat as a sin-offering, distinct from the individual's ewe/female goat and the High Priest's bull. Discusses who qualifies as 'nasi'.

candidates.name: Change of Status Before/After Sin — High Priest and King
candidates.hebrew: שינוי מעמד לפני ואחרי העבירה — כהן גדול ונשיא
candidates.notes: Rules for determining which offering is brought when a High Priest or king sinned before appointment or after leaving office, and whether they bring the offering of their current or former status.

candidates.name: Acting (Temporary) High Priest vs. Current High Priest
candidates.hebrew: כהן גדול שעבר לעומת הממונה תחתיו
candidates.notes: Distinctions between the current serving High Priest and a former/substitute High Priest regarding the Yom Kippur bull, daily meal-offering, and other obligations such as marriage to a virgin and restrictions on mourning.

candidates.name: Provisional Guilt-Offering (Asham Talui) — Who Is Liable
candidates.notes: In Horayot: individual and king are liable for an asham talui; anointed priest and court are exempt. Covers which categories of persons owe an asham talui vs. chatat.

candidates.name: Absence of Awareness of Halakha (Heflem Davar) as Trigger for Communal Offering
candidates.hebrew: העלם דבר של ציבור — תנאי החיוב
candidates.notes: The requirement that the court's error must consist of unawareness of the law combined with unwitting action by the public; intentional ruling with unwitting public action, or unwitting ruling with intentional public action, changes liability.

candidates.name: Special Rules for Erroneous Ruling on Idol Worship
candidates.notes: When the communal sin involves an erroneous ruling on idolatry, the offerings are a bull and a goat (rather than just a bull), and special rules apply for individual, king, priest, and court.

candidates.name: Grades of Holiness (Dargot Kedushah)
candidates.notes: Ten grades of holiness from Land of Israel through the Holy of Holies, and corresponding restrictions on entry for various classes of impure persons, as enumerated in Keilim 1:6-9

candidates.name: Meilah — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Detailed halakhot of tractate Meilah: liability thresholds, stages, joining of measures, agency, repeated misuse, and distinctions between sanctity levels

candidates.name: Kinim — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Detailed halakhot of tractate Kinim: types of bird pairs, mixing and invalidation, assignment, priestly discretion, and women's obligations

candidates.name: Asham Talui (Provisional Guilt Offering)
candidates.notes: The provisional guilt offering brought when one is uncertain whether they committed a sin requiring a sin offering; rules of when it applies, when it atones, and what happens if certainty is later established

candidates.name: Sliding-Scale Offering — Detailed Rules (Oleh v'Yored)
candidates.notes: Detailed rules of the sliding-scale offering: the five categories obligated (false oath of testimony, false oath on deposit, defiling the Temple or its foods, woman after childbirth, leper); substitution between animal, bird, and flour depending on financial status

candidates.name: Mechusar Kapparah — Detailed Rules
candidates.notes: The four categories of mechusar kapparah (zav, zava, woman after childbirth, leper) and their inability to eat sacrificial meat until the atonement offering is brought; also nazirite and convert in this context

candidates.name: Lapse of Awareness (He'elem) in Sin Offering Liability
candidates.notes: Rules governing what constitutes a single lapse of awareness for purposes of sin offering liability; whether multiple transgressions in one lapse require one or multiple offerings; combining different prohibitions

candidates.name: Doubt in Sin Offering Liability (Safek Chatat)
candidates.notes: Cases of doubt whether one committed a sin requiring a sin offering, including mixed pieces of forbidden/permitted food, uncertainty about Shabbat vs. weekday labor; dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua

candidates.name: Doubt in Misuse of Consecrated Property (Safek Meilah)
candidates.notes: Rabbi Akiva's position that a provisional guilt offering is brought for uncertainty about meilah; dispute with Rabbis; Rabbi Tarfon's alternative procedure of paying immediately with conditional guilt offering

candidates.name: Discovery of Innocence After Bringing Offering
candidates.notes: What happens to a provisional or definite guilt offering when it is discovered that no sin was committed: before/after slaughter, before/after blood sprinkling; dispute between Rabbi Meir, Rabbis, Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yosei

candidates.name: Guilt Offering of the Pious (Asham Chasidim)
candidates.notes: Rabbi Eliezer's view that one may voluntarily bring a provisional guilt offering at any time; the practice of Bava ben Buta who brought one daily; dispute with the Rabbis who limit the provisional guilt offering to actual cases of doubt

candidates.name: Designation of Offering for Specific Sin (Kavvanat HaKorban)
candidates.notes: A sin offering may not be redirected to atone for a different sin than originally designated; one's heirs may not bring a designated sin offering in place of the decedent; derived from 'for his sin that he sinned'

candidates.name: Two Partners Bringing One Atonement Offering
candidates.notes: Dispute whether two people who each may have committed a sin can jointly bring one sin offering or guilt offering as partners with a stipulation; Rabbi Shimon permits it conditionally; Rabbi Yosei prohibits conditional atonement offerings

candidates.name: Acquisition of Hekdesh by Speech
candidates.notes: The principle that consecration to the Temple treasury takes effect through speech alone, unlike acquisition between private parties which requires a formal act

candidates.name: Kinim — Mixed Bird Offerings (Laws of Mixed-Up Pairs)
candidates.notes: Laws governing what happens when bird pairs (hatat and olah) become mixed up with each other or with other bird offerings, including rules of invalidation and valid remainder

candidates.name: Bird Hatat (Chatat haOf)
candidates.notes: Specific laws of the bird sin-offering, performed below the red line on the altar, distinct from beast chatat

candidates.name: Bird Olah (Olat haOf)
candidates.notes: Specific laws of the bird burnt-offering, performed above the red line on the altar, distinct from beast olah

candidates.name: Red Line of the Altar (Chut haSikra)
candidates.notes: The red line dividing the upper and lower halves of the outer altar, which determines where bird and beast offerings are performed

candidates.name: Obligatory Bird Offerings (Kinnim Chovat)
candidates.notes: Bird pairs brought as obligatory offerings (e.g., for birth, zivah), consisting of one hatat and one olah

candidates.name: Voluntary Bird Offerings (Kinnim Nedavah)
candidates.notes: Bird pairs brought as freewill or vow offerings, all of which are olot; no hatat is included

candidates.name: Assigned and Unassigned Bird Pairs (Mefurashin v'she'Einan Mefurashin)
candidates.notes: Distinction between bird pairs that have been assigned to specific purposes (hatat or olah) and those that have not yet been designated

candidates.name: Bird Flying Away and Invalidating Offerings
candidates.notes: Rules governing when a bird from a pair flies away into other groups of birds, the consequent invalidation, and calculation of which offerings remain valid

candidates.name: Pairing of Turtledoves and Pigeons
candidates.notes: Rule that turtledoves and pigeons cannot be paired together for a single kin; the hatat and olah must be of the same species

candidates.name: Leaving Invalid Birds to Die (Yumtu)
candidates.notes: Halakhic ruling that certain mixed or invalid bird offerings must be left to die rather than offered or redeemed

candidates.name: Priestly Discretion in Offering Kinnim
candidates.notes: Laws concerning whether the priest seeks guidance before offering mixed bird pairs, and the different outcomes depending on whether advice was sought

candidates.name: Women's Obligations for Kinnim
candidates.notes: Specific scenarios involving women who owe bird offerings for birth or zivah and the rules when multiple women's pairs become mixed

candidates.name: Hierarchy of Sacred Objects (Maalot HaKedushah)
candidates.hebrew: מעלות הקדושה — עולין בקודש ואין מורידין
candidates.notes: Principle of ascending in sanctity and not descending — proceeds from sale of sacred items may only purchase items of greater sanctity

candidates.name: Non-Priestly Watches (Anshei Ma'amad)
candidates.notes: Representatives of the lay public who accompanied or fasted during the priestly watches; they read from Creation in the Torah; mentioned in context of special Torah reading occasions

candidates.name: Bull of Anointed Kohen Gadol for Erroneous Ruling
candidates.hebrew: פר כהן משיח על שגגת הוראה
candidates.notes: The anointed (oil) High Priest brings a special bull if he issued an erroneous ruling and acted upon it; the multi-garment High Priest does not bring this offering

candidates.name: Meilah (Misuse of Consecrated Property — General)
candidates.notes: Detailed halakhot of meilah: liability thresholds, stages of consecration, permitting factors, joining of measures, and agent liability — the core subject of tractate Meilah

candidates.name: Shiur Peruta for Meilah (Minimum Value for Misuse Liability)
candidates.notes: The minimum benefit of one peruta required to incur liability for meilah; disputes between Rabbi Akiva and Rabbis regarding benefit vs. damage requirement

candidates.name: Meilah After Meilah (Repeated Misuse of Same Item)
candidates.notes: Whether repeated misuse of the same consecrated item by multiple persons each incurs liability; applies to animals and service vessels

candidates.name: Period of Fitness for Priests (Ra'ui laKohanim) in Meilah
candidates.notes: Rabbi Yehoshua's principle: if a sacrificial item had a period during which it was permitted to priests before being disqualified, no meilah liability applies afterward

candidates.name: Agency in Meilah (Shliach b'Meilah)
candidates.notes: Rules for who bears meilah liability when an agent uses consecrated property: if agent follows instructions, homeowner is liable; if agent deviates, agent is liable

candidates.name: Joining Consecrated Items for Meilah Measure (Tziruf b'Meilah)
candidates.notes: Rules for combining different consecrated items or multiple acts of benefit to reach the minimum peruta measure for meilah liability

candidates.name: Stages of Offering and Meilah Liability
candidates.notes: How meilah liability changes at each stage of the sacrificial process: consecration, slaughter, blood sprinkling, placement on altar, and burning

candidates.name: Meilah in Kodshei Kodashim vs. Kodashim Kalim
candidates.hebrew: מעילה בקדשי קדשים לעומת קדשים קלים
candidates.notes: The distinction in meilah rules between most sacred offerings and offerings of lesser sanctity, including the concept of leniency and stringency of the sprinkling act

candidates.name: Growth of Consecrated Property (Gidulei Hekdesh)
candidates.notes: Whether growths, offspring, eggs, or milk that develop after consecration are themselves subject to meilah; dispute between Rabbis and Rabbi Yosi

candidates.name: Detailed Laws of Meilah
candidates.notes: Detailed halakhic rules governing meilah liability in various scenarios

candidates.name: Rites of the Meal Offering
candidates.notes: The specific ritual acts performed in the processing of meal offerings

candidates.name: Ingredients and Quality Standards of Meal Offerings
candidates.notes: Requirements for flour, oil, frankincense, wine, and grain used in meal offerings

candidates.name: Shewbread and Two Loaves — Laws and Procedures
candidates.notes: Detailed rules governing the preparation, arrangement, dimensions, and replacement of the shewbread and the two loaves of Shavuot

candidates.name: Meilah in Libations and Blood (Nesachim and Dam)
candidates.notes: Rabbi Shimon's ruling on meilah for blood (lenient at outset, stringent at end) vs. libations (stringent at outset, lenient at end)

candidates.name: Consecrated Peruta Among Non-Sacred Money
candidates.notes: Dispute between Rabbi Akiva and Rabbis about when meilah is incurred when a consecrated peruta is mixed into a purse of non-sacred perutot

candidates.name: Desacralization of Consecrated Money (Pidyon to Prevent Meilah)
candidates.notes: Procedure by which one can desacralize a consecrated peruta already sent with an agent by transferring its sanctity to another peruta or vessel

candidates.name: Five Sin Offerings Left to Die (Chamesh Chatat HaMeitot)
candidates.notes: The five categories of sin offerings that must be left to die rather than sacrificed, including offspring of a sin offering, substitute for a sin offering, sin offering of one who died, one that passed a year, and one that was lost and found blemished after atonement

candidates.name: Consecrated Items Fit and Unfit for Altar or Temple Maintenance
candidates.hebrew: הקדש הראוי ושאינו ראוי למזבח ולבדק הבית
candidates.notes: Rules for meilah liability when consecrated items are fit only for altar, only for Temple maintenance, both, or neither — and how items consecrated empty differ from those subsequently filled

candidates.name: Meilah Status of Willow Branches and Siloam Water
candidates.notes: Meilah status of water drawn from Siloam for libation before and after placement in service vessel, and willow branches for the altar before and after their placement

candidates.name: Meilah Status of Inner Altar Ash and Candelabrum Wicks
candidates.notes: The ashes from the inner altar and wicks of the Candelabrum may not be used but if benefit was derived there is no meilah liability; if re-consecrated, meilah liability applies

candidates.name: Kemitzah (Removal of the Handful)
candidates.notes: The rite of removing the handful from a meal offering; covers who may perform it, how it is done, disqualifying intentions, left-hand removal, outsized/lacking handful, etc.

candidates.name: Shirayim (Remainder of the Meal Offering)
candidates.notes: The remainder of the meal offering after the handful is burned; rules about its consumption by priests, conditions under which it is permitted or forbidden.

candidates.name: Meal Offering of Sinner and Sota — Special Disqualification Rules
candidates.notes: The meal offering of a sinner and the sota's jealousy meal offering are disqualified if any of the four rites (kemitzah, placing in vessel, conveying, burning) is performed not for their sake, unlike other meal offerings.

candidates.name: Machavat and Marcheshet (Shallow and Deep Pan Meal Offerings)
candidates.notes: Two types of pan-prepared meal offerings; differences in their preparation (depth, cover, consistency of product) and halakhic interchangeability when vowed.

candidates.name: Shewbread — Detailed Laws of Arrangement and Replacement
candidates.notes: Detailed rules: dimensions of loaves, placement on Table, gold panels and rods, simultaneous removal and placement to ensure constant presence, distribution on Shabbat.

candidates.name: Shtei HaLechem — Detailed Laws of the Two Loaves
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of the two loaves on Shavuot: leavening method, dimensions, relation to accompanying lambs, whether they prevent or are prevented by each other.

candidates.name: Omer Harvest Rite
candidates.notes: Detailed procedure for harvesting the omer: fashioning sheaves, nighttime reaping, public ceremony with repeated declarations, rebuttal of Boethusian practice.

candidates.name: Grades of Olive Oil for Menorah and Meal Offerings
candidates.notes: Three harvests, each producing three grades of oil; first grade for Candelabrum, remainder for meal offerings; ranking of nine grades; geography of optimal oil sources.

candidates.name: Wine Quality Requirements for Libations
candidates.notes: Rules about which wines are valid or invalid for libations; forbidden types (irrigated, fertilized vineyard, smoked, boiled, sweet, etc.); geographic sources of best wine.

candidates.name: Measuring Vessels of the Temple (Midot)
candidates.notes: Dry and liquid measuring vessels used in the Temple for meal offerings and libations; their sizes, purposes, and the sanctity of their overflows.

candidates.name: Intermingling of Libations
candidates.notes: Rules about mixing libations of bulls with rams, lambs with lambs, individual with communal, same day with previous day; when mixing validates or invalidates.

candidates.name: Placing Hands on Offering — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Who performs semichah; who is exempt (deaf-mute, minor, blind, gentile, slave, agent, woman); requirement to lean with two hands; immediate slaughter following; comparison with tenufah.

candidates.name: Tenufah (Waving) — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Which offerings require waving vs. bringing near; manner of waving (four directions, up and down); waving of live animals vs. slaughtered; comparison with semichah.

candidates.name: Hagashah (Bringing the Meal Offering Near)
candidates.notes: The rite of bringing the meal offering near the southwest corner of the altar; which meal offerings require it; distinction from tenufah; order of rites.

candidates.name: Prohibition of Leavening Meal Offerings
candidates.notes: Most meal offerings must be matza; method of kneading with lukewarm water; lashing for leavening at each stage of preparation (kneading, shaping, baking).

candidates.name: Oil and Frankincense Requirements of Meal Offerings
candidates.notes: Classification of meal offerings by whether they require oil, frankincense, both, or neither; prohibition of adding oil or frankincense to sinner's or sota's meal offering.

candidates.name: Loaves of the Thanks Offering — Detailed Laws
candidates.notes: Forty loaves (ten each of four types); measures of flour and oil; terumah loaf given to priest; consecration of loaves dependent on valid slaughter; use of non-sacred vs. second-tithe money.

candidates.name: Temple of Onias (Beit Chonyo)
candidates.notes: Egyptian temple built by Onias; offerings sacrificed there do not fulfill obligations; priests who served there may not serve in Jerusalem; halakhic status compared to blemished priests.

candidates.name: Quality Requirements for Grain Used in Meal Offerings
candidates.notes: Geographic sources of optimal flour (Makhnis, Zateḥa, Aforayim); prohibition of fertilized, irrigated, or tree-shaded fields; inspection method; sifting requirements.

candidates.name: Measure of the Handful (Melo Kometz)
candidates.notes: Definition of a valid handful: neither overflowing with fingers apart nor taken with fingertips only; how the priest folds fingers onto palm; role of foreign objects disqualifying the handful.

candidates.name: High Priest's Daily Griddle-Cake Offering (Chavitei Kohen Gadol)
candidates.notes: Half offered in morning, half in afternoon; brought as whole and divided by High Priest; rules when High Priest dies mid-day; whether it comes from communal or heirs' funds.

candidates.name: Dimensions and Structure of the Shewbread Table
candidates.notes: Dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Meir over cubit size; dimensions of loaves and table; placement of loaves and frankincense bowls; gold panels and rods supporting the loaves.

candidates.name: Baking of Two Loaves and Shewbread
candidates.notes: Where kneading and baking take place (inside/outside courtyard); whether preparation overrides Shabbat or Festival; use of mold (defus); minimum and maximum days from baking to eating.

candidates.name: Breaking Meal Offerings into Pieces (Petitah)
candidates.notes: Procedure for breaking loaves into olive-bulk pieces; differences between Israelite meal offering, priestly meal offering, and High Priest's offering; folding method.

candidates.name: Consecration of Meal Offering in a Service Vessel
candidates.notes: Whether handful must be sanctified in a service vessel; dispute between Rabbi Shimon and the Sages; procedures inside vs. outside the Temple courtyard.

candidates.name: Redeeming a Blemished Consecrated Animal
candidates.notes: When a consecrated animal becomes blemished, it may be redeemed and its value used to purchase a replacement; rules about combining or splitting redemption money for replacement offerings.

candidates.notes: Voluntary meal offerings must come from wheat (fine flour), not barley; must include oil and frankincense; minimum measure of one tenth of an ephah; no partial tenths.

candidates.name: Temple Watch (Mishmar HaMikdash)
candidates.notes: Laws and procedures of the priestly and Levitical guard watch in the Temple, including the officer of the Temple Mount, beating of sleeping watchmen, and burning of clothes

candidates.name: Temple Courtyard Sections
candidates.notes: The distinct subdivisions of the Temple courtyard complex, including the courts of Women, Israel, and Priests

candidates.name: Temple Chambers (Lishkot)
candidates.notes: The various chambers (lishkot) within the Temple complex and their specific functions

candidates.notes: Detailed sub-topics of the Red Heifer laws including ritual procedure, invalidating factors, priest's purity, location on Mount of Olives, and division of ashes

candidates.name: Temple Gates (Sha'arei HaMikdash)
candidates.notes: The specific gates of the Temple Mount and Temple Courtyard, their names, purposes, and special features including the gates of Nicanor, Huldah, Kiponus, Taddi, and others

candidates.name: Beit HaMoked (Fire Chamber)
candidates.notes: The fire chamber in the Temple where priests slept and kept watch, its structure, chambers, and the key-storage arrangements

candidates.name: Hel (Temple Rampart)
candidates.notes: The ten-cubit wide rampart between the Soreg and the courtyard steps

candidates.name: Altar Dimensions and Structure
candidates.notes: Precise measurements and construction of the outer altar, including the foundation, surround, horns, and ramp; the red dividing line between upper and lower blood applications

candidates.name: Kevesh (Altar Ramp)

candidates.name: Altar Stones — Prohibition of Iron

candidates.name: Ezrat Nashim (Women's Courtyard)

candidates.name: Ezrat Yisrael (Israelites' Courtyard)
candidates.notes: The Court of Israel, its dimensions (135x11 cubits), and its separation from the Court of the Priests by a row of mosaic stones

candidates.name: Ezrat Kohanim (Priests' Courtyard)
candidates.notes: The Court of the Priests, its dimensions, its height relative to the Court of Israel, and the thirteen prostrations made there

candidates.name: Ulam (Temple Porch)
candidates.notes: The entrance porch of the Temple Sanctuary: its dimensions (40 cubits high, 20 cubits wide), the five ash beams over the doorway, cedar poles, golden chains, and the golden vine

candidates.name: Golden Vine of the Temple (Gefen shel Zahav)
candidates.notes: The golden vine at the door of the Sanctuary upon which worshippers would hang donated leaves, grapes, and bunches

candidates.name: Ta'im (Temple Cells/Side Chambers)
candidates.notes: The thirty-eight cells surrounding the Hekhal on three sides, their arrangement in three stories, widths, and interconnecting doors

candidates.name: Upper Chamber (Aliyah) of the Temple

candidates.name: Lishkat HaGazit (Chamber of Hewn Stone)
candidates.notes: The chamber of hewn stone in the Temple courtyard where the Great Sanhedrin sat to judge priestly fitness; the procedures for disqualified and qualified priests

candidates.name: Lishkat HaMelach (Salt Chamber)
candidates.notes: The chamber in the Temple courtyard where salt for the offerings was stored

candidates.name: Lishkat HaParvah (Parvah Chamber)

candidates.name: Fifteen Steps (of the Temple)
candidates.notes: The fifteen semi-circular steps leading from the Court of Women to the Court of Israel, corresponding to the fifteen Songs of Ascent in Psalms, upon which the Levites sang

candidates.name: Temple Procession — Entering and Exiting Right

candidates.name: Gate of Nicanor (Sha'ar Nicanor)

candidates.notes: Detailed measurements of the Hekhal (100x100x100 cubits), its walls, porch, Holy of Holies, side cells, and the full east-west and north-south calculations

candidates.name: Korban Pesach (Paschal Offering)

candidates.name: Paschal Lamb Slaughtered Not for Its Purpose (shelo Lishmo)

candidates.name: Notar of the Paschal Lamb
candidates.notes: Laws of leftover Paschal lamb meat that must be burned; the rule that after midnight the Paschal lamb renders hands impure as notar; burning of bones, sinews, and leftovers on the 16th of Nisan

candidates.name: Boundary for Eating the Paschal Lamb

candidates.name: Frontplate Appeasing for Impurity (Ritzui Tzitz b'Tumah)

candidates.notes: Use of silver trumpets alongside the shofar in the Temple on Rosh HaShanah and fast days; rules about when trumpets sound long vs. short blasts

candidates.notes: Laws governing the special war-priest: appointment, speech, and function before battle

candidates.notes: Detailed laws of priestly watch rotation, festivals, fasting, and penalties

candidates.notes: The specific placement of limbs of daily, additional, and New Moon offerings on different parts of the altar ramp

candidates.notes: Dispute among R. Meir, R. Yehuda, and R. Shimon about which sins the goats of Rosh Chodesh and Yom Tov atone for — Shevuot ch. 1

candidates.notes: Procedure for consecrating additions to the Temple courtyard requiring king, prophet, Urim veTummim, Sanhedrin, two thanks-offerings, and song — Shevuot 2:2

candidates.notes: The special priest appointed to address soldiers before battle, his speech in Hebrew, and his role in war preparations

candidates.name: Shewbread Distribution on Festivals
candidates.notes: Rules for distribution of the shewbread among priestly watches when Shabbat coincides with or is adjacent to a festival

candidates.name: Mishmar of Bilgah (Priestly Penalty)

candidates.name: Zecher laMikdash (Commemoration of Temple Practice)
candidates.notes: Rabbinic enactments instituted to remember Temple practices, such as taking lulav seven days outside the Temple after its destruction

candidates.name: Sukkot Bull Offerings (Seventy Bulls)

candidates.name: Ma'amadot (Non-Priestly Watches)

candidates.name: Wood Offering (Korban Etzim)

candidates.name: Temple Service Lottery (Payis)

candidates.name: Daily Temple Service Procedure (Seder HaTamid)

candidates.name: Laws of Temurah (Substitution of Consecrated Animals)

candidates.name: Sin Offerings Left to Die (Chatat HaMutot)
candidates.notes: Grouping for the halacha leMoshe miSinai categories of sin offerings that are sequestered and left to die

candidates.name: Destruction of Prohibited Sacred Items (Sereifah u'Kevurah)

candidates.name: Candelabrum Cleaning and Kindling Procedure

candidates.name: Arrangement of Wood on the Altar (Ma'arachah)

candidates.name: Division and Carrying of Sacrificial Limbs

candidates.name: Temple Crier (Gevini HaKorei)
candidates.notes: The role of the Temple crier who announced each morning to priests, Levites, and Israelites to take their respective positions for the daily service
