candidates.name: Temple Slaughterhouse and Rings (Beit HaMitbachayim)
candidates.notes: The northern slaughterhouse area of the Temple with its twenty-four rings affixed to the floor for holding animals during slaughter, the pillars, hooks, and marble tables

candidates.name: High Priest's Prerogative to Sacrifice Any Offering
candidates.hebrew: זכות הכהן הגדול להקריב בכל עת
candidates.notes: The High Priest's right to offer any portion of any sacrifice he wishes at any time, and the procedure by which he receives the limbs from other priests and places his hands upon them

candidates.name: Deputy High Priest (Segan HaKohanim)
candidates.notes: The role of the deputy high priest (segan) in assisting the High Priest, standing to his right, signaling the Levites with cloths during the libation, and other functions

candidates.name: Trumpet and Cymbal Signal for Libation and Levitical Song
candidates.notes: The procedure of sounding trumpets (tekia, terua, tekia) and clashing cymbals by Ben Arza to signal the start of the Levitical psalm during the libation, and the people's prostration at each section

candidates.name: Chamber of Hewn Stone (Lishkat HaGazit)
candidates.notes: The Chamber of Hewn Stone where lotteries were conducted and the priests recited Shema and its blessings each morning before the daily service

candidates.name: Temple Shovel Sound (Magreifah)
candidates.notes: The instrument thrown between the Entrance Hall and the altar that produced a sound so loud no voice could be heard in Jerusalem, signaling priests, Levites, and the non-priestly watch to assemble

candidates.name: Pesakhter (Large Ash Vessel)
candidates.notes: A large vessel holding a half-kor used to remove ashes from the altar, to cover scattered coals on Shabbat, and to cover a dead creeping animal found in the Temple on Shabbat

candidates.name: Temurah (Substitution of Consecrated Animals)
candidates.notes: The act of substituting a non-sacred animal for a consecrated one; both become sacred and the owner receives lashes. Core topic of tractate Temurah.

candidates.name: Temurah Taking Effect (Bidieved)
candidates.notes: Though substitution is prohibited, once done it takes halakhic effect; both original and substitute become sacred.

candidates.name: Temurah: Individual vs. Communal Offerings
candidates.notes: Only individual owners can effect substitution; communal offerings and partners cannot render substitutes.

candidates.name: Kohen's Ownership of Priestly Gifts and Substitution
candidates.hebrew: בעלות כהן על מתנות כהונה לענין תמורה
candidates.notes: Dispute between R. Yochanan ben Nuri and R. Akiva whether a kohen who received a firstborn can effect substitution, hinging on when ownership is acquired.

candidates.name: Comparative Stringencies: Temurah vs. Kodashim
candidates.hebrew: חומרות תמורה על קדשים וקדשים על תמורה
candidates.notes: Mishnah 2:3 compares stringencies unique to temurah (e.g., blemished animal gains inherent sanctity, no redemption of wool/labor) vs. those unique to consecrated animals.

candidates.name: Unwitting Substitution Treated as Intentional
candidates.notes: The Torah treats one who substitutes unintentionally like one who acts intentionally — the substitution takes effect. Contrasted with consecration where unwitting act is ineffective.

candidates.name: Five Sin Offerings Left to Die
candidates.notes: Halacha leMoshe miSinai: five categories of sin offerings that are sequestered and left to die — offspring of chatat, substitute of chatat, chatat whose owner died, chatat after owner achieved atonement with another, chatat whose year passed.

candidates.name: Offspring of a Sin Offering (Vlad Chatat)
candidates.notes: The offspring of a sin offering is left to die and may not be sacrificed or used for benefit.

candidates.name: Sin Offering After Owner Achieved Atonement
candidates.notes: A sin offering found after its owner achieved atonement with a different animal is left to die. Extensive discussion of cases with money and animals replacing each other.

candidates.name: Offspring of Consecrated Animals (Vlad Kodashim)
candidates.notes: Status of offspring born to consecrated animals; inherits the sanctity of the parent offering (e.g., offspring of shelamim is shelamim, offspring of olah follows olah rules).

candidates.name: Animals Disqualified from the Altar (Issurei Mizbeach — Specific Cases)
candidates.notes: Tractate Temurah ch. 6 details nine categories of animals prohibited on the altar: copulated with, object of bestiality, set-aside for idolatry, worshipped, payment to prostitute, price of a dog, kilayim, tereifa, yotzei dofen.

candidates.name: Payment to Prostitute and Price of Dog — Altar Prohibition
candidates.notes: Detailed rules on what constitutes etnan zonah and mechir kelev that disqualify an animal from the altar, including barter, maidservant cases, and whether offspring are also prohibited.

candidates.name: Caesarean-Born Animal (Yotzei Dofen) in Kodashim
candidates.notes: An animal born by caesarean section is disqualified from the altar and cannot effect temurah.

candidates.name: Differences Between Altar Consecrations and Temple Maintenance Consecrations
candidates.hebrew: הבדלים בין קדשי מזבח לקדשי בדק הבית
candidates.notes: Ch. 7 systematically enumerates distinctions: temurah, piggul/notar/tumah liability, offspring/milk restrictions, slaughter outside courtyard, unspecified consecrations, effect on all items, liability for by-products.

candidates.name: Burial of Prohibited Sacred Items (Kevurah)
candidates.notes: Items from which benefit is forbidden that must be buried rather than burned: fetus of consecrated animal, placenta, stoned ox, eglah arufah, metzora birds, nazirite's hair, peter chamor, basar bechalav, non-sacred animals slaughtered in courtyard.

candidates.name: Burning vs. Burial — Method of Destruction for Prohibited Items
candidates.notes: Distinction between items requiring burning (chametz, impure terumah, orlah, kilei hakerem, piggul/notar offerings) and items requiring burial; the two categories cannot be switched even for stringency.

candidates.name: Asham Taluy After Determination of Sin
candidates.notes: A provisional guilt offering (asham taluy) that is found unnecessary when the person learns he did not sin — it is burned, per R. Yehuda buried.

candidates.name: Firstborn and Animal Tithe Offerings from Outside Eretz Yisrael
candidates.notes: Firstborn and animal tithe should not be brought to the Temple from outside Eretz Yisrael ab initio; if brought unblemished they are sacrificed, if blemished eaten in place.

candidates.name: Eating Rules for Firstborn and Animal Tithe (vs. Other Kodashim)
candidates.hebrew: דיני אכילת בכור ומעשר לעומת שאר קדשים
candidates.notes: Firstborn and tithe differ from other kodashim: not sold in market by litra, not subject to redemption, sold/eaten only from home; their substitutes and offspring graze until blemished then eaten.

candidates.name: Designating a Fetus in the Womb as an Offering
candidates.notes: One can preemptively designate the fetus in the womb as a burnt or peace offering before birth, thereby avoiding the firstborn obligation. Rules for twins, tumtum, hermaphrodite.

candidates.name: Female Animal Designated for a Male-Only Offering
candidates.notes: If one designated a female for a burnt offering or guilt offering (which require males), the animal grazes until blemished, is sold, and the proceeds fund the proper offering.

candidates.name: Substitution for Limbs and Fetuses
candidates.notes: One cannot substitute for consecrated limbs or fetuses with whole animals, nor whole animals for limbs; dispute of R. Yosei whether substituting a limb consecrates the entire animal.

candidates.name: Simultaneous Designation of One Animal for Two Offerings
candidates.notes: Dispute (R. Meir vs. R. Yosei) about what happens when one simultaneously or sequentially designates an animal as substitute for both a burnt offering and a peace offering.

candidates.name: Formulas That Effect Temurah
candidates.notes: Which verbal formulas effect temurah: 'in place of,' 'substitute,' 'exchange for' — effective; 'desacralized' — not temurah, but if blemished animal, effects redemption.

candidates.name: Set-Aside and Worshipped Animals — Prohibited for Altar
candidates.notes: Animal set aside for idol worship (muktzeh) vs. animal actually worshipped (ne'evad) — both prohibited on altar; distinction regarding what is on them and their consumption.

candidates.name: Prohibited Animals Mixed with Permitted — Altar Nullification Rules
candidates.notes: Animals prohibited on the altar (the nine categories) prohibit an entire mixture in any amount — no nullification applies, unlike food mixtures.

candidates.name: Differences Between Individual and Communal Offerings
candidates.hebrew: הבדלים בין קרבנות יחיד לקרבנות ציבור
candidates.notes: Systematic list: individual offerings — temurah, male or female, require compensation; communal offerings — override Shabbat and tumah, fixed time determines this rule per R. Meir.

candidates.name: Chamber of Parhedrin (High Priest's Pre-Yom Kippur Quarters)
candidates.notes: The chamber where the High Priest was sequestered for seven days before Yom Kippur; its laws and practices

candidates.name: High Priest's Seven-Day Preparation for Yom Kippur
candidates.notes: The seven-day sequestering, practice of service, and preparation of the High Priest before Yom Kippur

candidates.name: Designating a Replacement Wife for the High Priest
candidates.notes: The debate whether to designate a replacement wife for the High Priest lest his wife die before Yom Kippur, based on 'his house' meaning his wife

candidates.name: Priestly Lottery (Payis) for Temple Service
candidates.notes: The four daily lotteries conducted in the Temple to determine which priests perform the various services; history of how the lottery replaced a race after injury

candidates.name: Oath Administered to the High Priest Before Yom Kippur
candidates.notes: The oath administered by the elders to the High Priest that he would not deviate from the prescribed Yom Kippur service, particularly regarding incense in the Holy of Holies

candidates.name: Keeping the High Priest Awake on Yom Kippur Eve
candidates.notes: The practices used to prevent the High Priest from sleeping on Yom Kippur eve, including Torah reading, snapping fingers, and standing on cold floor

candidates.name: Confession (Vidui) on Yom Kippur
candidates.notes: The three confessions recited by the High Priest on Yom Kippur: over his bull (for himself and family), again over the bull (adding the priests), and over the scapegoat (for all Israel)

candidates.name: Utterance of the Explicit Divine Name (Shem HaMephorash)
candidates.notes: The High Priest's utterance of the Tetragrammaton on Yom Kippur during the confessions; the people's response 'Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom'

candidates.name: Lots for the Two Yom Kippur Goats (Goralot)
candidates.notes: The lottery procedure to designate which goat is for God and which for Azazel; the lottery receptacle and its historical development from wood to gold

candidates.name: Incense Offering in the Holy of Holies
candidates.notes: The unique Yom Kippur incense service performed inside the Holy of Holies; the coal pan, spoon, handfuls of incense, procedure of entry and exit

candidates.name: Blood Sprinklings on Yom Kippur
candidates.notes: The specific blood sprinklings of Yom Kippur: inside the Holy of Holies (one up, seven down), on the parochet, and on the golden altar; counting method

candidates.name: Foundation Stone (Even HaShtiya)
candidates.notes: The foundation rock in the Holy of Holies from the days of the early prophets, three fingerbreadths high, upon which the High Priest placed the incense after the Ark was taken

candidates.name: Dispatching the Scapegoat to the Wilderness
candidates.notes: The procedure of leading the scapegoat to the cliff (Tzuk), the booths along the route, the crimson strip, the escort, and the signal system back to Jerusalem

candidates.name: Crimson Strip (Lashon shel Zehorit)
candidates.notes: The crimson strip tied to the scapegoat's horns and to the sanctuary entrance; its miraculous turning white when sins were forgiven

candidates.name: Burning the Bull and Goat of Yom Kippur
candidates.hebrew: שריפת הפר והשעיר של יום הכיפורים
candidates.notes: The procedure of burning the bull and goat sin-offerings outside Jerusalem; when their carriers become impure

candidates.name: Torah Reading by the High Priest on Yom Kippur
candidates.hebrew: קריאת התורה של כהן גדול ביום הכיפורים
candidates.notes: The High Priest's public Torah reading on Yom Kippur from Leviticus 16 and 23; the eight blessings he recites afterward

candidates.name: Device for Sinking the Temple Basin (Mukheni)
candidates.notes: The mechanical device built by ben Katin to sink the Temple laver into water overnight to prevent its water from being disqualified by remaining overnight

candidates.name: Temple Benefactors and Their Contributions
candidates.notes: Those who contributed to the Temple: Yehoshua ben Gamla (gold lots), ben Katin (mukheni, spigots), King Munbaz (gold handles), Queen Helene (chandelier, golden tablet), Nicanor (doors). Contrasted with those who withheld secrets: House of Garmu, House of Avtinas, Hugras ben Levi, ben Kamtzar

candidates.name: House of Avtinas (Incense Preparers)
candidates.notes: The family that held the secret formula for preparing the Temple incense and refused to teach it to others

candidates.name: House of Garmu (Shewbread Bakers)
candidates.notes: The family that held the secret of preparing the shewbread and refused to teach it to others

candidates.name: High Priest's Five Immersions and Ten Sanctifications on Yom Kippur
candidates.hebrew: חמש טבילות ועשר קידושין של כהן גדול
candidates.notes: The five immersions and ten sanctifications of hands and feet performed by the High Priest throughout the Yom Kippur service; where each is performed

candidates.name: White Linen Garments of the High Priest on Yom Kippur
candidates.notes: The special white linen garments worn by the High Priest during Yom Kippur's inner services (Holy of Holies); their cost, origin (Pelusium vs. India), and alternation with golden garments

candidates.name: Order of the Yom Kippur Service (Seder HaAvodah)
candidates.notes: The precise sequential order of all Yom Kippur services; consequence of performing them out of order; need to repeat services if blood spills

candidates.name: Gate of Nicanor
candidates.notes: The famous gate of the Temple named after Nicanor; the miracle associated with its doors

candidates.name: Signal System from Wilderness to Temple
candidates.notes: The system of platforms and waving scarves used to signal from the wilderness back to Jerusalem when the scapegoat arrived; debate about its necessity

candidates.name: Sacrifice of the Zav
candidates.notes: The obligation of a confirmed zav to bring a sacrifice after purification; threshold of three sightings required for sacrifice obligation; cases where he is exempt from sacrifice but still obligated in running water

candidates.name: Intent and Proper Designation in Sacrificial Rites
candidates.notes: Group covering the various aspects of intent (lishmah, shinui makom, pigul) and the required designations when performing sacrificial rites

candidates.name: Blood Rites and Altar Placement
candidates.notes: Group covering the detailed laws of blood collection, conveyance, sprinkling, number of placements, and mixtures of different bloods

candidates.name: Consumption of Sacrificial Meat — Location and Time
candidates.notes: Group covering where and when sacrificial meat may be consumed, including notar and distinctions between grades of sanctity

candidates.name: Altar Structure and Sanctifying Power
candidates.notes: Group covering the physical components of the altar (base, red line) and the halakhic principle that the altar sanctifies items placed upon it

candidates.name: Lishmah (Offering for Its Own Sake)
candidates.notes: The requirement that offerings be sacrificed with proper intent for the specific type of offering; consequences of slaughtering not for its own sake (shelo lishmah)

candidates.name: Shinui Makom (Improper Location Intent for Offering)
candidates.notes: Disqualification of offerings due to intent to eat or burn sacrificial portions outside the designated area (chutz limkomo), distinct from pigul which involves intent beyond designated time

candidates.name: Four Sacrificial Rites (Arba Avodot)
candidates.notes: The four essential rites of sacrifice: slaughter, blood collection, conveying blood to altar, and sprinkling blood; disqualifying intent during any of these invalidates the offering

candidates.name: Six Intentions Required for Sacrificial Rites
candidates.notes: The six matters for which an offering must be slaughtered: for the sake of its type, its owner, God, consumption by fire, aroma, pleasing God; plus atonement for sin offerings and guilt offerings

candidates.name: Kodshei Kodashim vs. Kodashim Kalim (Most Sacred vs. Lesser Sanctity)
candidates.notes: Distinction between offerings of the highest sanctity and offerings of lesser sanctity, with differences in location of slaughter, consumption, and who may eat them

candidates.name: Tzafon (Northern Section of Temple Courtyard)
candidates.notes: Requirement that offerings of the most sacred order be slaughtered in the northern section of the Temple courtyard; detailed laws of this location requirement

candidates.name: Number of Blood Placements (Matnot Dam)
candidates.notes: Rules governing required number of blood placements: one placement, two placements that are four, four placements on corners, and inner altar placements; consequences of omitting placements

candidates.name: Dam HaNefesh and Sheyarei HaDam (Soul Blood and Remainder Blood)
candidates.notes: Distinction between the initial blood spurting from the neck and the remainder blood; the remainder is poured at the base of the altar and its absence does not disqualify the offering

candidates.name: Mixtures of Different Bloods
candidates.notes: Laws governing when blood of different offerings become mixed; rules for presenting mixed bloods on altar; blood of fit offerings mixed with unfit bloods; blood requiring inner vs. outer presentation

candidates.name: Yesod HaMizbeach (Base of the Altar)
candidates.notes: The base/foundation of the outer altar where remainder blood is poured; not all sides have a base, affecting where blood can be placed

candidates.name: Chut HaSikra (Red Line of the Altar)
candidates.notes: The red line running along the middle of the outer altar dividing it into upper and lower halves; blood of different offerings must be placed on the correct side of this line

candidates.name: Ascending the Altar – Shall Not Descend (Ya'aleh Lo Yeirid)
candidates.notes: Rule that disqualified offerings that have ascended the altar are not removed; distinction between items that may remain and items that must be removed; sanctification by the altar

candidates.name: Sanctification by the Altar (Kiddush Mizbeach)
candidates.notes: The principle that the altar sanctifies items suited to it; similarly the ramp and service vessels sanctify; items already on the altar are not removed even if disqualified

candidates.name: Misuse Liability for Disqualified Offerings
candidates.notes: Whether disqualified offerings retain their consecrated status for purposes of misuse liability; relationship between sin offerings and burnt offerings that were changed in designation

candidates.name: Tadir uMekudash (Precedence of Frequent and Sacred Offerings)
candidates.notes: Rules of priority in sacrificing offerings: more frequent offerings precede less frequent ones; more sacred offerings precede less sacred ones

candidates.name: Shechitat Chutz (Slaughtering Outside the Temple)
candidates.notes: Detailed laws of liability for slaughtering and offering sacrifices outside the Temple courtyard; conditions for liability including fitness of the animal and intent

candidates.name: History of Bamot (Private Altars — Permitted and Prohibited Periods)
candidates.notes: Historical progression of permitted and prohibited private altars: Tabernacle period, Gilgal, Shiloh, Nov, Gibeon, Jerusalem Temple; differences in laws of consumption at each location

candidates.name: Laws Unique to the Tabernacle vs. Private Altars
candidates.notes: Specific rites that apply only at the Tabernacle/Temple and not at private altars: semichah, slaughter in north, blood placements, waving, bringing to corner; piggul, notar, and impurity apply equally

candidates.name: Location of Eating Sacrificial Meat
candidates.notes: Rules governing where sacrificial meat may be eaten: within curtains (Temple courtyard), within Jerusalem walls, or anywhere; differences between most sacred and lesser sanctity offerings

candidates.name: Time Limit for Eating Sacrificial Meat (Zman Achilah)
candidates.notes: Time limits within which sacrificial meat must be consumed: one day and night (until midnight), two days and one night; consequences of eating after the permitted time (notar)

candidates.name: Notar (Leftover Sacrificial Meat)
candidates.notes: Prohibition against eating sacrificial meat left over beyond its permitted time; karet liability; distinction from pigul

candidates.name: Hides of Sacrificial Animals (Orot Kodashim)
candidates.notes: Rules governing who receives the hides of burnt offerings and other sacrificial animals; hides of burnt offerings go to priests; hides of offerings of lesser sanctity go to owners; conditions affecting this

candidates.name: Burning of Disqualified Offerings (Serifat Kodashim)
candidates.notes: Laws of burning disqualified offerings in the place of burning (beit hadeshen) or in the Temple courtyard; distinction between offerings burned outside Jerusalem and those burned inside

candidates.name: Blood of Sin Offering on Garments
candidates.notes: Laws requiring laundering of garments on which sin offering blood was sprayed; applies to both eaten and burned sin offerings; must be laundered in the sacred area

candidates.name: Cooking Vessels for Sacrificial Meat — Scouring and Rinsing
candidates.notes: Requirement to scour and rinse copper vessels in which sin offerings were cooked; must be done in the sacred area; distinction between earthenware (broken) and copper (scoured and rinsed) vessels

candidates.name: Mixtures of Sacrificial Limbs and Animals
candidates.notes: Laws when sacrificial animals or their limbs become intermixed; solutions including letting them graze until blemished, selling, eating by most stringent rule

candidates.name: Bird Sin Offering Rites (Melikah and Dam)
candidates.notes: Detailed rites of the bird sin offering: melikah at nape, sprinkling blood below red line, squeezing blood at base; differences from bird burnt offering

candidates.name: Bird Burnt Offering Rites
candidates.notes: Detailed rites of the bird burnt offering: melikah at nape with separation of head, squeezing blood at upper altar, removal of crop and feathers, rending the body

candidates.name: Distribution of Sacrificial Meat Among Priests
candidates.notes: Rules for which priests receive a share of sacrificial meat; priests unfit for service on a given day do not receive a share; relationship between sprinkling blood and receiving a share

candidates.name: Offerings of Gentiles (Korban Goyim)
candidates.notes: Special rules for offerings consecrated by gentiles: not subject to piggul, notar, or eating-in-impurity prohibitions; liability for slaughtering outside the Temple

candidates.name: Service Performed by Disqualified Priest
candidates.notes: Effect of Temple service performed by various disqualified priests (impure, lacking vestments, tevul yom, mechusar kapparah, onen, uncircumcised) on the validity of the offering
